answers and the debate.
mr president, commissioner, i would first like to congratulate mr van nistelrooy on the efforts he has made on this resolution, which has been long awaited in our committee on regional development, and mrs mikhailova for supporting such initiatives. as you know, 80% of the european budget is managed by the member states and a huge percentage of this money is spent by european municipalities through projects that take place on their territory. but often a very large part of this money is difficult for municipalities to realise, to turn into projects. they say the only thing worse than not having money is having it and not knowing what to do with it. to avoid such a situation, i suggest a few things: first, support for municipalities from a to z, from project selection through submission, reporting and management, so that no mistakes are made; create flexible funding. i know many mayors in many countries who can't afford to do a project because they don't have the money. we need to encourage countries to create compensatory mechanisms for this.
in writing. colleagues, regional and local authorities are closest to citizens and have the best view of local needs, policies and initiatives to improve citizens' lives job creation, health, environment, energy, transport, etc. on the other hand, these bodies have limited resources compared to the national level and need more substantial budget support, both for co-financing projects and for specific local policies. in general, regional and local authorities must be able to participate in the shaping of european and national policies that have an impact at regional and local level. there is certainly a tendency to increase the degree of consultation of regional and local authorities in cohesion policy, but this consultation varies widely between member states. cities are engines of economic growth and employment and an ideal platform for innovation and start-ups. smart cities and smart specialisation strategies are two areas that can quickly become specific eu policies or initiatives. in this context, the commission should take the initiative to strengthen the role and influence of local and regional authorities in the management of the european structural and investment funds, so that they can serve european citizens in the most effective way.
in writing. ‒ the european commission's annual report rightly recognises that the legal and institutional framework to guarantee the fundamental rights of minorities is in place, but unfortunately the legislation remains on paper and is not implemented. i am in constant contact with the bulgarian community in serbia, which complains of severe discrimination by the local authorities bulgarian schools are not funded, there is a lack of educational materials in bulgarian, freedom of association is restricted. people generally live in fear of being called bulgarians. i supported the european parliament resolution on serbia's 2015 progress report because it calls on the serbian government to ensure consistency in the implementation of the legal framework for the protection of minorities throughout the country. serbia has much to do to ensure that every ethnic minority can freely use its language, have access to education, participate in local government, have media and worship services in the minority language. i strongly hope that in the process of serbia's integration with the european union, the situation of the bulgarian community will improve.
in writing. ‒ i support the report because it is an indisputable fact that serbia has embarked on the path of reform and european integration. we should congratulate the country on the opening of accession negotiations on chapters 32 (financial control) and 35 (normalization of relations with kosovo). the willingness of serbia to work in this direction is a clear sign of the presence of political will for change and development. in the past year, serbia has also emerged as an important partner of the european union in the balkans on the issue of the migration crisis. the government has made great efforts to provide asylum and protection to many third-country nationals on its territory. of course, despite the progress made, serbia needs to make additional efforts to address issues in leading political spectrums such as the protection of minorities, the rule of law, the fight against corruption and discrimination, and violence against lgbti people. i believe that the european union can provide significant technical assistance to the country to meet these challenges. i think it is extremely important for the serbian government to bring its foreign policy fully into line with that of the european union. efforts in this direction will legitimize serbia's desire to be part of the european family. and what greater reward for the european union than the membership of all the western balkan countries in our structures?
in writing. – serbia has made substantial progress on its path towards the european union. as a neighbouring country to bulgaria, the two countries are closely related and cross-border cooperation could be facilitated if serbia enters the eu. i welcome serbian reform efforts and i vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ as rapporteur in the shadow of the european parliament resolution on kosovo's european integration process, i am satisfied with the final text of the resolution, as many of my amendments and proposals were taken into account. i am very pleased that the resolution mentions the bulgarian community, the so-called 'gorani', and calls for respect for their rights and freedoms. although i support the european integration of kosovo, i decided to abstain because the resolution contains a text with which i do not entirely agree, namely a call on the european commission to liberalize the visa regime with kosovo as soon as possible. i and my colleagues in the european conservatives and reformists group are of the opinion that the country has to fulfil a number of requirements and commitments in the fight against organised crime before the european commission takes steps towards visa liberalisation. the situation is further complicated by the fact that of all the countries in europe, the largest number of foreign fighters for the islamic state comes from kosovo. that is why i think that the visa regime should not be liberalised at this stage.
in writing. - we're looking into the situation in libya. there is no situation in libya, simply because there is no libya anymore. this country, which was a friend of all western democracies, no longer exists. in the territory of the former libya, today we have a war, a war between different tribal alliances, supporting one or another terrorist organization and/or those who fight against them. and here we have to say in plain text who is to blame for this. now we have to deal with those consequences, but we also have to learn the lessons and help this country work again. and that goes through stopping isis and its backers like turkey. i hope that happens, which is why i supported this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the situation in libya is disturbing. just across the mediterranean sea, anarchy, chaos and violence are spreading. nowadays in libya there is an ongoing civil war, an enormous migration crisis and the presence of a brutal terrorist organisation, daesh. because of growing instability oil-rich libya can be considered a failed state. there is no doubt that in this complicated situation the eu should act quickly in order to avoid the spread of instability and terror in the region and beyond. we should bear in mind that this neighbouring failed state represents a real threat to the eu’s security and stability. therefore, the eu should urge libya’s rival politicians to accept the creation of an un-backed unity cabinet. a united libyan cabinet will have a significant chance to restore stability and peace in a war-torn country. in case that unity cabinet is formed, the eu has to provide extensive development assistance and aid in order to support the future institution-building process in the country.
in writing. – the situation in libya is particularly alarming - human rights situation is deteriorating throughout the country and violence against civilians, journalists, officials, political figures and human rights defenders perpetrated by all parties are a tragic reality. international community, along with the eu, should stand ready to support libyans in their efforts to successfully implement libiyan political agreement. that is the reason i vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted with 'abstention' on this resolution, as i do not entirely agree with some of the proposals made in it. i agree that the eu islands, as peripheral areas, are particularly vulnerable to the challenges europe is currently facing. in particular, the southern regions are exposed to increasing migration flows. these island regions are also leading tourist destinations, which also contribute to the eu's diversity in terms of both culture and the environment; they have the capacity to contribute to sustainable development with their renewable energy production potential or because of their specific location. however, i do not think that the european commission should yet create specific instruments to support these regions. in view of the crisis facing the eu, i believe that a better solution would be for member states with such island territories to develop a strategy to better absorb european funds and to better use existing instruments.
in writing. i supported this resolution because i strongly believe that disadvantaged areas, which include most rural areas in addition to islands, areas affected by industrial transition, and regions affected by serious and permanent natural or demographic handicaps, such as border and mountain areas, deserve special attention from the community, which should be reflected in financial and planning terms. these regions often have unique livelihoods, traditions and characteristics. in its quest for sustained economic growth, europe is pouring more and more resources into highly urbanised and already privileged areas for a number of reasons. however, geographically more remote or isolated areas are not only peripheral, but are also on the way to becoming economically and socially isolated, because they cannot always meet the criteria for economic return, which in most cases are based on the experience and statistics of urbanised and highly developed regions. i also support and call for the declaration of a 'year of islands and mountains' through this resolution, because such an initiative and other accompanying initiatives would help to overcome the economic and social difficulties faced by these specific regions.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the role of local and regional authorities in the european structural and investment funds, as the committee on regional development calls on the european commission to build on existing past and current initiatives in the field. the resolution also stresses the importance of available information for achieving the eu's objectives in the areas of economic and social cohesion. attention was also drawn to the difficulties faced by local authorities in their implementation.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the role of local and regional authorities in the european structural and investment funds because i believe that the use of these funds, which is directed at european citizens, should be made in consultation with these authorities. according to some surveys, it is precisely local and regional institutions that are closest to citizens and enjoy their trust the most, due to their geographical and cultural proximity. these are also the bodies that know the problems of local communities best and would be among the most competent bodies to shape regional priorities. they are the ones that make the connection and strike the balance between the union's objectives and their implementation by citizens. there are problems such as depopulation, the effects of climate change and the shifting balance between urban and non-urban communities, which directly affect local and regional authorities and institutions. i therefore join the call to the european commission through this resolution to involve more actively representatives of these institutions in order to seek faster and more lasting solutions to the problems facing the european union.
ppe), in written form. ‒ the report highlights the key role of local and regional authorities in the development and implementation of eu strategies. the role of urban areas is highlighted, as is the fact that eu policies have an important role to play in creating the right framework for the growth and development of the potential of urban areas in europe. the report calls on the commission to work towards identifying measures to strengthen the role of local and regional authorities in the management and implementation of the european structural and investment funds, through partnership agreements and operational programmes. i support this report.
in writing. – regional and local authorities are close to citizens and better understand local needs as well as policies and initiatives aimed at improving citizens’ lives. therefore, the role of local and regional authorities is of high importance in shaping and implementing eu strategies. i am in favour of synergies and complementarity between the esi funds and other eu programmes, in which local and regional authorities can play a useful role in attaining the objectives of cohesion policy. therefore, i vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the humanitarian situation in yemen because i am deeply concerned by the fact that security in the country is steadily deteriorating and is beginning to take on an international dimension. on the one hand, saudi arabia is waging an open war against the rebels, considering them iranian combat units, while iran is calling for an immediate halt to the aerial bombardments carried out by the international coalition led by saudi arabia. despite un efforts to bring peace to the country, intense fighting on land and air strikes continue. in addition to the thousands of civilian casualties, over a million and a half people have fled their homes. if no action is taken and no peace is achieved soon, there is a great danger that the situation in the country will escalate into a full-scale civil war and then into a regional ethnic war between shiites and sunnis.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because we all should be aware that the humanitarian situation in yemen is as critical as the situation in syria. in the 21st century it is an unspeakable shame for humanity that 16 million yemenis do not have access to drinking water or sanitation because of fighting and embargo. in addition to that, it is totally unacceptable for two million children to not have proper access to education, food and medical care. for one reason or another, the whole civilian population caught in the yemen civil war suffers from ongoing fighting, bombardment, food insecurity, dire living conditions and the disruption of essential services. in this critical situation, the eu – as the world’s leading human rights champion and aid donor – should provide emergency humanitarian assistance to the civilian population in yemen. together with the un, the eu should use all of its political and economic capabilities to facilitate peace negotiations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution because it is an initiative of the european parliament which aims to give an appropriate description of the actions of this terrorist organisation. this qualification will also provide the direction for an international response. while daesh is not a threat only to minorities in the region, some are specifically targeted because of their religion or ethnicity. the responsibility of the international community is to oppose the hatred and violence of those who justify their actions by religion, international law and unity. the resolution calls for legal recognition through the use of the word genocide and recalls the mandate of the international criminal court, which has jurisdiction over crimes against humanity. on the unity front, i welcome the call to work together with the organisation of islamic cooperation, the cooperation council for the arab states of the gulf and more generally with religious leaders to promote the protection of ethnic and religious minorities and to counter ideologically and politically radical interpretations of islam.
in writing. ‒ undoubtedly, the worst humanitarian crisis of our time is syria. тhe syrian civil war is the most complex, most violent and deadliest conflict on earth. now in its fifth year, the conflict is more than just a battle between those for or against president assad. it has acquired ethno-religious character, spread into neighbouring countries, drawn in the world powers, and facilitated the rise of global jihadist groups like daesh. more often than not, these new dimensions of the syrian conflict jeopardise religious minorities in the extensively divided country. daesh is responsible for the systemic killing of religious minorities and, to put it simply, everyone who does not share their radical views. this brutal terror campaign against religious minorities is definitely an absolute crime against humanity. in addition, the assad regime is continuing to commit genocide against its own people. more than ever, as the worlds’ leading normative power, the eu should begin an extensive diplomatic push for finding a solution. this, ideally, could happen during negotiations between syrian government and opposition in geneva this month. there, the eu could show its global role in dealing with challenges.
in writing. the actions of the 'islamic state' cause the loss of human lives every day. the delayed response of the international community has allowed the terrorists to expand their activities beyond the borders of syria and iraq. the attacks on civilians, attacks on religious and cultural grounds, the destruction of cultural sites and the trafficking of cultural artefacts have shocked the world. today, christians, yazidis, and others who do not share the ideology preached by the islamic state are being systematically eliminated. attacks on religious and ethnic minorities can safely be qualified as a crime against humanity and genocide. i strongly condemn the atrocities of this terrorist group which has driven millions of people from their homes and taken the lives of thousands more. the financial flows to isis must be stopped at all costs. in europe, we have also witnessed this destructive ideology. dozens of young europeans have gone to syria and given their lives there. let's join forces to stop the terrorists once and for all.
in writing. there is currently no common european legislation defining a uniform system for the identification and registration of domestic animals such as dogs and cats, and each country determines the ways and means of doing so. the separate national systems, where they exist, are also not linked, resulting in a fragmented environment with incomplete or missing information on the status of animals. in the context of a common market for goods and services, free movement of persons and labour mobility, the existence of a pan-european registration system is highly necessary. it would save a lot of time and money, reduce the bureaucracy involved in moving an animal to another country and, last but not least, give owners much greater certainty about the origin of their pets. not to mention, of course, the benefits of disease control and the spread of infection between animals and humans, and the reduction of trafficking and abuse in the sale of dogs and cats. a single system of identification and registration would also encourage responsible animal husbandry, as it would no longer be so easy to throw animals out on the streets, and owners could be quickly traced and sanctioned, which in turn would reduce the population of stray dogs and cats.
rapporteur on the opinion of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. two objectives have been constantly on the agenda of this parliament in recent years: economic growth and employment. none of these goals would be achievable without healthy european citizens. we all know that the main responsibility in this area lies with the member states, but the european semester can and should be used as a tool to achieve modern health systems that meet the expectations and needs of citizens. i therefore consider it extremely important that within its framework there should be an assessment of the functioning of health systems. i call on the commission to develop tools to monitor health outcomes and measure access to high-quality health services in order to reduce inequalities in this area. the european union must reaffirm its commitment to the implementation of the 2020 strategy. we must demonstrate to the european citizens that we have a plan for the future of our continent. i therefore believe that the revision of strategy 2020 should be integrated very strongly into the european semester. the environment and health sector has great potential for growth, investment and job preservation. the european semester has a key role to play in promoting the necessary structural reforms.
the rapporteur on the opinion of the committee on regional development. in its opinion on the annual growth survey, the committee on regional development calls on the european commission to better reflect the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy by improving its implementation and conducting a further review, and by proposing measures and methodology to better monitor the expenditure of european union funds related to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. in this context, the forthcoming revision of the multiannual financial framework provides an opportunity to analyse and increase the added value of european union funding. the regi commission points out the links between the objectives of the european semester process and the programming of the european structural and investment funds and considers that cohesion policy investments can play a very important role in supporting structural reforms and the implementation of the european union's strategic objectives by following up on the relevant country-specific recommendations.
in writing.– a strong and stable eu economy has at its heart active citizens with access to opportunities for employing their professional and creative potential. i therefore welcome the inclusion of employment indicators in this year’s annual growth survey. activity rate, long-term unemployment and youth unemployment are very much needed as integral elements of the scoreboard, as they would allow us to track progress on key elements of employment. we are currently observing a positive trend of increasing employment and activity, whereby the overall eu employment rate has even reached its pre-crisis level. however, regional disparities remain and much more progress is needed to reach the employment target of 75% that the eu set itself for 2020. the means for achieving this goal are also anchored in the ags, which underlined the importance of the use of funds under horizon 2020 and the newly-created efsi. unfortunately, these instruments are not sufficiently understandable and applicable for the european citizens. if we are to fulfil our ambitions for a growing and thriving europe, we must really enable people with professional drive to engage in employment and self-employment. efsi and horizon 2020 must therefore really serve the interests of the economy and be made more accessible to citizens. this is how we will start creating employment.
in writing.– the free movement of workers is a fundamental principle of the treaty enshrined in article 45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in order to help workers to effectively exercise that right – to look for a job and to work in another eu country, enjoying the same treatment as the country´s nationals in terms of access to employment, working conditions and social benefits – we need to reinvigorate and adjust eures. this cooperation network for labour mobility clearly showed some shortcomings such as limited support services and information exchange, as well as not sufficient cooperation and lack of transparency in labour markets. in this regard, i find essential the incorporation into the network of effective public and private employment services. it is important to widen to scope of information which is available on the portal, ensuring that all jobseekers can obtain comprehensive information about the existing vacancies and all related employment conditions. on the other hand the portal should facilitate the automated matching of job vacancies and cvs, which will allow employers to quickly find and recruit workers who have the right skills and qualifications. reinvigorating eures will be highly beneficial for the reduction of the unemployment rates and will contribute to a more integrated union labour market.
in writing. if we measure our economies in terms of gdp growth rates, employment, especially among young people, is a matter of individuals and their future, not of numbers and charts. and specific young people only value specific measures and results, and that's why i suggest two specific steps. first, public-private employment services. in some countries, there are employment websites and services that do better than public employment services. some 80% of the funding for employment services is public. employment is most effectively created by private investment. businesses are hiring our young people and companies need to have a stronger voice and participation in the management of employment services. secondly, erasmus for young entrepreneurs is the new employment for young people. but we need to change two things: global erasmus in the us, china, japan and elsewhere. young europeans to learn from the best entrepreneurs, then start a business and hire more young people; a demand-driven budget. the programme's budget for 2020 is just €55.3. 90% of the participating entrepreneurs are under 40 years old, and over a third of them have started their own business after participating. in view of the above two sentences, i know that there is no law, regulation, directive or institution that can serve as an excuse and justification.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am outraged by the situation which has been developing for months on the border between greece and bulgaria. for several years 2009, 2010, this border was blocked by farmers and caused huge damage to bulgarian carriers, bulgarian producers, bulgarian entrepreneurs and european ones. many truck owners from poland, the czech republic, slovakia, austria are also in this blockade and also suffer heavy financial losses. what i would like to say and ask of the european commission is that it should act quickly and resolve this blockade quickly and that the european treaties should be respected, since the treaty on the functioning of the european union is currently being violated. this cannot go on either there will be a european union and there will be freedom of movement, or there will be none. and that is my request to the european commission. otherwise, there's no need for it.
in writing. ‒ the report by ms uspakic concerns the accession of austria and malta to the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters. my group and i are opposed to the fact that the eu should not have legal competence in this area. that is why i voted with an abstention. i'm not against austria and malta joining the hague convention. i believe that as sovereign states, the governments of both countries should be able to make this decision at national level without needing approval at european level.
in writing. ‒ tax fraud is one of the areas where the union budget suffers the most. it is important that member states cooperate with each other in combating them. in addition, the eu needs cooperation with european countries that are not members of the eu but are part of the european economic community. i supported the report, but i still think that a huge effort is needed to continue signing similar agreements with other countries in europe, which are known as 'tax haven' countries. we will thus bring the rest of the continent into the union, making it a stable and economically developing place.
in writing. ‒ san marino’s agreement to cooperate with the eu on tax transparency could serve as an example to the world how the fight against tax avoidance and tax evasion should be conducted. there is no doubt that the automatically exchange of information between the eu member states and san marino will contribute to the efforts to deter hiding income and assets abroad and will promote fair distribution of the tax burden for all citizens. for the good of the union and member states, the eu should sign same type of agreement with all of its partners.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by tomáš zdechovski on croatia's accession to the convention on the protection of the financial interests of the union. the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests and its protocols aim to establish a common legal basis for criminal law for the protection of the european communities' financial interests. fraud affecting both revenue and expenditure should be punishable by effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties, including imprisonment, which may lead to extradition. the convention was adopted on 26 july 1995 and entered into force on 17 october 2002. this proposal formalises the accession of croatia to the conventions after its accession to the eu.
in writing. ‒ ms becker's report refers to the eu's eures platform, which aims to facilitate labour mobility within the union. the aim of the proposed regulation is to make eures a tool for jobseekers as well as for employers by creating a 'database' of vacancies and profiles across the eu. in the current situation of high unemployment, which is spreading across many member states, i believe that such an instrument would undoubtedly have a positive effect. i support the report, but i think it is important nevertheless to give member states the freedom to give employers the option not to publish a particular advertisement on the platform depending on the requirements of the specific position.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and further integration of labour markets, as i believe that the free movement of people in the eu is as important as the free movement of goods, services and capital, although it is the least used of the four rights. in this context, i believe that we should support legislative initiatives aimed at promoting the free movement of workers within the eu and facilitating the protection of the social rights associated with it, as this benefits both european citizens themselves and businesses and the needs of the economy as a whole.
in writing. – the proposed regulation aims to enhance the access of workers to intra-eu mobility support services, maintaining the eures network as an effective instrument for jobseekers (including traineeships and apprenticeships) and registered employers who have a stake in labour mobility within the union. i believe that better job search and recruitment services across europe are essential to fighting unemployment, especially among young people. that is why i am favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by ms de sarnez on the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures in relation to tunisia, as i believe that after the terrorist attack in sousse last june, the country needs additional eu support on its path of political and economic transition. eu foreign ministers agreed on a package of short-term measures to have a positive effect on the country's transition. the commission proposal concerns a temporary duty-free quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for olive oil exports to the eu under these emergency trade measures for a period of 2 years (1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017). however, i believe that there should be effective control and i support the idea of the commission carrying out an interim evaluation and, if necessary, proposing measures against possible infringements resulting from the emergency measures.
in writing. european agriculture is facing a crisis. although olive oil was not included in the list of goods banned from importation into russia, the embargo imposed by the federation had a wide impact on the whole sector and, as a result, european agriculture continues the worrying trend of losing its attractiveness. uncertainties in the sector make this livelihood less attractive as the scissors of the generational gap are increasingly unraveling. the illiberal free trade policies and the removal of protective mechanisms for european farmers only contribute to the consolidation of these trends. the european union must be responsible towards its neighbours, but without being to the detriment of the european farmer, who is increasingly the victim of political decisions.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is a fund that helps workers who have lost their jobs as a result of changing global trade patterns to find new ones or to acquire new skills. i am voting against the mobilisation of this fund again because i think it is not efficient and that the funds should be used differently, and i fully support measures that help stimulate the economy so that new jobs are created, but i think that giving €1 million to 400 people who have lost their jobs is not serious and is certainly not efficient.
in writing. ‒ i decided to abstain from voting on this report because i consider that it partly deals with issues that are outside the eu's sphere of competence. at the same time, the report does not contain a clear message. it's impossible to form an opinion about something so vague. while the report calls for improvement and structural reforms, it also calls for a significant policy shift. this implies a debate on the redistribution and definition of responsibilities, which must move from the national parliamentary level to the plenary level in the ep. the euro area, which at the same time may be formally referred to as a macroeconomic entity, certainly cannot be called 'one whole'. there are too many factors specific to each country to make the proposed approach illogical, because the original hypothesis is simply not true. there is no comprehensive approach to deep policy coordination within the eu.
in writing. – the annual growth survey (ags) identified three policy priorities for 2016: re-launching investment, pursuing structural reforms and responsible fiscal policies. the use of funds under horizon 2020 and the european structural and investment funds is essential for supporting growth and innovation across europe. this annual growth survey thus sets out what more can be done at eu level to help member states support growth, reinforce economic convergence, create jobs and strengthen social fairness. hence, i supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i support further initiatives to improve economic growth and employment, but nevertheless, i have decided not to support this report mainly because of its overly binding nature. this report contains some important priority issues, but despite the fact that it is mainly a balanced overall report, calling for a number of initiatives at eu level which would not only affect subsidiarity but also undermine national regulatory policy.
in writing. – following the publication of the annual growth survey 2016, which set out the priorities at european level, this report shifts the attention of the european semester to the national dimension. as discussed in the report, the bulgarian economy has been gradually emerging from the crisis, but a broad-based recovery is yet to be achieved. therefore, i welcome the resolution and i look forward to the country-specific recommendations to be presented in may 2016 by the commission based on the analysis presented in the country reports and the dialogue held with member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the single market in the context of the 2016 european semester, as i believe that efforts should be directed towards improving the functioning of the single market. better governance and more transparency are among the main positives outlined in this report. speaking of the single market, it is also important to emphasise that the european semester respects the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, which are important for the member states. however, there is also a need to strengthen existing mechanisms and instruments to improve governance.
in writing. – at the heart of europe’s competitiveness, and its biggest economic strength, is the single market, which with 500 million persons gives the eu the opportunity to be a global economic force. the report on single market governance within the european semester 2016 emphasises that europe now faces a different kind of competition – a digital one. instead of developing powerful industrial sectors locally, advanced economies could be established by adopting the latest technologies and sourcing products and services globally. during my mandate as an mep i am fully supporting the digitalisation process of european industry and the opportunities a fully operational digital single market (dsm) could bring to the eu. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ negotiations for the signing of a free trade agreement with tunisia were launched in october last year. i supported this resolution as it outlines the priority areas for these negotiations which the european commission should pay attention to when formulating its position. i think tunisia is one of the few countries in the region that has managed to become a democratic state to a large extent, as a result of the events of the arab spring. the commission should work towards an agreement that is beneficial to both parties, paying attention to the fact that exports of food and agricultural products produced in tunisia must meet the eu's high quality standards.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement (dcfta) will benefit both sides (the eu and tunisia). in the case of tunisia, it will help support economic reforms and further consolidate young democracy in that country. whereas, in the case of the eu, the deal will not only facilitate trade and economic growth but also will provide an opportunity to the union to promote democracy, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms in a neighbouring country, which is located in a very unstable north-african region characterised by extensive human rights violations, irregular migration and the presence of islamic state. namely, in this context, i supported the dcfta with tunisia because above all it will be a stepping stone for further economic and political integration of the euro-mediterranean region that will bring in long—term economic growth, stability, security, peace and prosperity.
in writing. the european union is founded on the ideas of solidarity and mutual assistance, aimed at the mutual integration of the economies of the member states. however, european producers in all sectors are increasingly subject to a series of transformations and transitions, such as the process of accession to the community. for this reason, i believe that the european union must seek and ensure the good and smooth functioning of the european single market as a matter of priority. tunisia has traditional ties with the european union, which is the country's first and most important economic partner. the commission notes that the tunisian authorities have not provided any evidence that the tunisian producers are in a comparable situation to the union producers. free trade agreements are a tool which, in my view, has the opposite effect for the european producer. there are still many mechanisms to maintain inequalities between european farmers in order to open up this single market freely. i therefore believe that another free trade agreement will only create more uncertainty for european producers and that is why i did not support the opening of negotiations for a free trade agreement between the eu and tunisia.
in writing. ‒ i fully support this report, not only because it welcomes and encourages initiatives such as better access to institutions for people with disabilities, but also because it supports efforts such as the creation of mandatory transparency of lobbying registers in so-called 'expert groups', drug research and, above all, the use of horizon 2020 funds. in particular, the use of funds underlies a number of institutional issues which in turn have a direct impact on the member states. above all, clarity on how funds are allocated is essential to ensure trust within member states and between member states within the european union.
in writing. – the european ombudsman is committed to ensuring that citizens, ngos, associations and companies are aware of their right to complain about maladministration in the eu institutions. i welcome the ombudsman’s investigation into whether the eu institutions are living up to their obligations and i believe that the ombudsman should continue urging for better transparency on the members and meetings of all experts groups expert groups, technology platforms and agencies.

in writing. – the publication of the annual report complements ecb efforts towards greater transparency by describing the actions that the ecb undertook in 2014. from a monetary policy perspective, the environment we faced in 2014 was very complex and demanding, for the year as a whole, we saw gdp growing by 0.9% in the euro area. the policy measures introduced by the ecb have contributed to lower interest rates in capital markets. even though bulgaria is not yet part of the euro area, i believe a strong euro area is an essential element of a strong and competitive european union. therefore, i support the report and the measures taken by the ecb.
in writing. ‒ a short resolution drafted by the european parliament's committee on international trade outlines its support for the european commission's decision to start work on the preparation of negotiations for free trade agreements with australia and new zealand. the resolution recognises that australia and new zealand are a key part of the eu's overall strategy in the asia-pacific region and that all agreements should be mutually beneficial to both parties. i agree, and that's why i voted for the resolution. the competitiveness of european firms on the world market should be supported by such agreements. i also welcome the commission's intention to make a preliminary assessment of the impact on the economies of the eu member states, and this is an important step in deciding on future action.
in writing. ‒ the opening of free trade agreement negotiations with australia and new zealand represents a significant step forward for economic growth and prosperity for all involved sides. an agreement will ensure eu trade reaches its full potential, particularly in the context of the eastern shift in the world’s economy. for australia, removing trade barriers with the eu, which is the country’s third largest trading partner, will definitely result in increased export growth. on the other hand, for new zealand, a trade deal with the eu will be beneficial for inward investment since the eu represents the country’s second largest source of investment. last but not least, the fta with australia and new zealand will not only highlight our common interests such as economic growth, human rights, security and peace but also facilitate political cooperation.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution, mainly because of the public health problem of citizens and the fact that the introduction of a compatible system for the identification and registration of pets throughout the eu could contribute to the tracing of the cause of pet disease outbreaks, which is inevitably linked to public health of people. the right of citizens to travel with their pets across the eu should also be protected and a common register would facilitate this movement.
in writing. i supported the text of this resolution because i believe that a collaborative approach through the building of compatible pet registration systems will help to tackle a number of the problems that exist today. experts have reported an increase in the illegal trade in pets, as well as a number of breaches of the pet travel scheme, such as falsification of documents and avoidance of checks. another problem with the pet trade is that they are often bred in poor conditions, as research has shown. 70% of new human diseases in recent decades are of animal origin and that animals commonly kept as pets are carriers of over 100 zoonotic diseases, including rabies. the introduction of a single or mutually recognised registration system and requirements would be a significant step forward in the protection of animal welfare and public health.
in writing. – dogs and cats may be moved between eu member states or imported from third countries for trade purposes or other reasons. these movements could pose a risk to both animal and human health if measures are not taken to prevent diseases from being transferred between countries. without a system for the identification and registration of dogs and cats, which is accessible across the eu, there is currently little traceability when animals are moved over borders. that is why i welcome the introduction of registration of pet animals across member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted 'abstention' on the resolution on the humanitarian situation in yemen, as what is happening in the country is deeply worrying but also complex. security in yemen is steadily deteriorating and is beginning to take on an international dimension, but at the same time we are witnessing a conflict of interest between two states - saudi arabia and iran. on the one hand, saudi arabia is waging open war against the rebels, considering them iranian combat units, while iran is calling for an immediate halt to the aerial bombardments carried out by the international coalition led by saudi arabia. despite un efforts to bring peace to the country, intense fighting on land and air strikes continue. in addition to the thousands of civilian casualties, over a million and a half people have fled their homes. if no action is taken and no peace is achieved soon, there is a great danger that the situation in the country will escalate into a full-scale civil war and then into a regional ethnic war between shiites and sunnis.
in writing. ‒ we all should be aware that the humanitarian situation in yemen is very critical. it is an unspeakable shame for humanity for 20 million yemenis to be living below the poverty line in dire living conditions without access to drinking water, sanitation, education, medical care and essential services. furthermore, because of fighting and an embargo, 2.5 million people have been displaced internally while around 125 000 yemeni refugees have fled the country. in this critical situation, the eu, as the world’s leading human rights champion and aid donor, should provide emergency humanitarian assistance to the civilian population in yemen. furthermore, together with the un, the eu should use all of its political and economic capabilities to facilitate peace negotiations. if the eu manages to put an end to the civil wars in yemen and syria then it will be a matter of time untilwe find a long-term peaceful solution in the middle east.
in writing. the situation in the middle east and its neighbouring regions continues to be an epicentre of instability with spill-over effects on europe. according to the information available since the beginning of the conflict, there are nearly 6,000 victims and nearly 30,000 wounded. i find particularly disturbing the information from unicef that the conflict has had a serious impact on access to education for nearly 2 million children and that over 3,500 schools have been closed. deprived of education and prospects for further development, these children are becoming easy targets for radicalization, and the likelihood of this leading to even more negative consequences and violence in the region in the years to come is growing. yemen is strategically located in the region, close to other conflict zones. the lack of a solution to the conflict and the will to do so have given terrorist organisations ample scope to expand and strengthen their presence in the region. for these reasons, i strongly support the call for the international community to adopt measures that will contribute to the cessation of armed action and conflict in the country.

in writing. ‒ the harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicp) are designed to measure inflation in a harmonised manner across member states. the commission and the european central bank use the hicp in their assessment of price stability in member states. as we all well know, maintaining price stability is a very crucial task since it makes a significant contribution to general welfare, including levels of economic activity and employment. in this regard, it is more than necessary for member states in the euro area to provide early provisional information on the monthly harmonised indices of consumer price. by doing this member states will have the opportunity to conduct monetary policy in the euro area that is needed and right.

member of the commission.– madam president, members ate to vote on the text of the directive on procedural safeguards for children suspected or accused in criminal proceedings. this directive is particularly important as it gives specific rights to children involved in criminal proceedings in the european union and provides for overarching protection at all stages of these proceedings. children are particularly vulnerable in criminal proceedings due to their young age and immaturity. around 1 million children in the eu are estimated to come into contact with the police and judiciary every year. they need therefore the highest possible protection. this directive is an important step forward in the construction of an area of justice in the european union. today there are large disparities in the level of protection offered in the european union applicable to children in criminal proceedings in the member states. in some cases, the level of protection is insufficient compared with the well-recognised international standards. the directive, once adopted, will significantly strengthen the procedural safeguards for children when confronted with criminal justice in the eu throughout all the proceedings. moreover, the directive will also contribute to the development of an effective model of juvenile justice. the new rules will ensure the fair trial rights for children during criminal proceedings; they will also prevent children from re-offending and will foster their social integration. i would like to congratulate and thank the parliament rapporteur, mrs chinnici, for her remarkable work and personal dedication on this file, which made an agreement on this directive possible after long and difficult negotiations. the outcome of the negotiations is a very well balanced text which endorses the principle laid down in article 24 of the charter of fundamental rights that ‘the child’s best interests shall always be a primary consideration’. notably, children will benefit from assistance by a lawyer in serious and complex cases and every time they are in detention. deprivation of liberty cannot be imposed as a sanction unless the child has been assisted by a lawyer, at least during the hearings before the court. children will also benefit from other safeguards such as assistance by their parents or other appropriate persons. they will also have the right to protection of privacy, including the possibility of having court hearings held in the absence of the public. furthermore, children will also have the right to an individual assessment to make sure that their specific needs concerning protection, education and social integration are fully taken into account. finally, the commission is also very satisfied that the text foresees that children should be kept separately from adults in police custody and pre-trial detention, unless this is not in the best interests of the child. this directive will give a strong signal that the european union strongly cares about children, the most vulnerable persons involved in criminal proceedings. therefore, i strongly encourage you to vote in favour of this directive today.
on behalf of the ecr group. i congratulate my colleague kinnichi and the shadow rapporteurs who worked on this dossier. the issue of procedural safeguards for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings is of particular importance because of the varying levels of protection in the member states and even the absence of such protection in some of them. some 1 086 000 children a year face criminal proceedings, representing 12% of all europeans facing criminal justice. on behalf of the shadow rapporteur, the honourable mr kirkhope, i would like to stress that the protection of children must be a priority for society. they are the most vulnerable of its species and need special protection. we need to be able to find solutions to legal loopholes in systems, taking into account the member states' legal systems, while creating european standards that ensure the protection of children's rights within the union. i invite member states to ensure that the protection of children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings is implemented as a priority. member states should adapt their legal systems to better protect accused and suspected children.
in writing. according to european commission data, 12% of all criminal proceedings in the eu involve children; at the same time, different practices in proceedings in the member states are observed, such as the existence of specialised criminal divisions, training of lawyers to work with children, and protection during interrogations. i support the agreed directive on common minimum standards for the rights of children suspected or accused in criminal proceedings, because these measures will lead to clearer and harmonised standards for criminal proceedings against children. in particular, i find the right to individual assessment to be a very important achievement, because no criminal proceedings are the same, especially when children are involved. the right to legal representation is also extremely important - everyone is equal before the law, and children in particular should have the opportunity for adequate protection and representation before the police and the courts. ladies and gentlemen, i believe the agreed guidelines take the best interests of the child into account. i also believe that it will facilitate mutual recognition of judicial decisions and cross-border police cooperation. these are important steps towards a pan-european judicial area that will create common rules for all member states.

author. madam president, commissioner, i am pleased that we have on the agenda an emergency resolution on the pre-electoral situation in the democratic republic of congo. the next few months are crucial for the future of the drc and the great lakes region as a whole. i would like to emphasize three aspects covered by the joint text. first, as regards the electoral process itself, i insist on the implementation of the recommendations of the 2011 election observation mission and the 2014 monitoring mission, which i had the honour to lead. it is more than necessary to hold the president and the government to account. an electoral calendar, a budget and, above all, a public commitment to respect the constitution without delay are necessary to avoid the burning of the country. secondly, on the security front, i welcome the renewal of the mandate of monusco and i support the extension of its powers to include the protection of civilians. thirdly, the regional dimension: the european union and the african union must do everything possible to maintain political dialogue with and between the countries of the region in order to avoid any escalation of tensions at the regional level.
in writing.– unfortunately, the political situation in the democratic republic of congo (drc) is very disturbing. the country’s fragile young democracy is under serious threat. according to reports from various sources, authorities in the drc are trying to break the constitution and to cancel the upcoming presidential elections in november 2016. in order to do so, congolese security and intelligence officials have initiated a severe crackdown on peaceful activists, political leaders and ordinary civilians who oppose peacefully unconstitutional attempts of ruling by president kabila, seeking to amend the constitution in order to stay beyond his constitutionally mandated two-term limit. as a leading democratic power and human rights champion, the eu should urge the congolese authorities to respect their own constitution, to guarantee the holding of transparent, credible and inclusive elections, to promote and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms. at a deeper level, the eu should expand cooperation with the un’s mission in the country (monusco) to further protect civilians and consolidate peace. undoubtedly, only stable democracy provides the natural environment for the protection of human rights and peace, and therefore we cannot allow ourselves to lose it in the drc.
mr president, i would like on behalf of the ppe to put an oral amendment to paragraph 3, first part, after the first sentence: ‘deplores external pressure attempts related to montenegro’s integration into euro-atlantic organisations’.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for tunisia marks the beginning of a new era in relations between eu and tunisia, a new approach in the euro-mediterranean political region. it has been clear that the tunisian economy needs support in particular after last year’s terrorist attack which severely damaged the tourist industry (tunisia’s main economic sector). therefore, exceptional and temporary free access to the european market will really benefit the tunisian economy. last but not least, the introduction of emergency autonomous trade measures for tunisia will facilitate negotiations between the union and tunisia on the establishment of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta).
in writing. – since 2011 tunisia has been а country in successful transition towards democracy. eu support during the period when the region is still very unstable, and the strengthening of democratic reforms in tunisia are key. a lack of jobs and opportunities was one of the main reasons for massive popular demonstrations in 2011 and many of the problems are present still today. economic growth will be embedded in rules through a trade agreement, which should enforce incentives for further economic and institutional reforms. that is why i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report because i believe that limiting the use of antibiotics in agriculture is imperative. measures must be taken because the health of the citizens is paramount to me. this, of course, must be done gradually, and it cannot be done all at once, because the spread of disease in this area could also be threatened. the use of antimicrobials is a great alternative, and their manufacturers and researchers should be encouraged. i am glad that this report provides such incentives, such as extending the period of protection for the technical documentation of new medicines.
in writing. ‒ the report on the authorisation and supervision of medicinal products for human and veterinary use is closely linked to the report on veterinary medicinal products, which i supported. in this case, we are talking about details at a technical level because of the decision taken by the commission to bring the rules on veterinary medicinal products under one regulation, replacing the existing directive. this requires the separation of medicines for animals and those for humans under different legislation and leads to the vote on this report, which i supported. i can emphasize again that the health of the citizens is always the primary consideration in choosing my position.
in writing. ‒ i support this initiative because i agree that the commission needs to tackle these issues because of the importance of 'big data' in our society today. we must insist on greater clarity and transparency when it comes to the passage of sensitive key areas such as those described in the text. with the latest proposals from the european commission in particular, there are more developments to be expected. it is essential that we can work on a solid basis to avoid ineffective legislation. we must therefore carefully evaluate all issues to find appropriate solutions.
in writing. ‒ we are currently living in a time of the fourth industrial revolution. the fourth industrial revolution has been characterised by the advance of technology and availability of vast amounts of data. looking from this perspective, it is obvious why the eu should support and accelerate the transition towards a data-driven economy in europe. availability of information and knowledge will definitely stimulate research and innovation and will create many opportunities for businesses across europe. furthermore, the data—driven economy will improve competitiveness and make citizens’ lives better. in this context, it can be argued that the data—driven economy will bring productivity growth to the eu. that is another reason why we should support it and facilitate it.
in writing. – the data-driven economy will stimulate research and innovation on data while leading to more business opportunities and an increased availability of knowledge and capital, in particular for smes, across europe. social and economic benefits associated with the integrated use of data in all sectors of the european economy and all fields of european research could be enormous. big data is an integral part of the new digital market, which i have been continuously supporting with my work as mep. that is why i am in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament's resolution on the situation in eritrea, as what is happening in the country is deeply worrying. since its declaration of independence in 1993, the country has been ruled by a single president, isaias afewerki, who has for the past 15 years led a highly authoritarian and repressive government. one of the main criticisms of the country is that it does not implement the constitution, which was adopted and ratified in 1997, violates human rights, there are many cases of torture and representatives of all religions are persecuted. the situation in eritrea is deteriorating steadily, causing many people to flee and leave the country, as evidenced by the 450,000 people seeking refuge in neighbouring countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it reflects the current situation in eritrea, its political context and the human rights violations which are seriously hampering the economic and human development of the country. in the resolution, we recall the importance of better using the european development fund (edf), which is to contribute to poverty reduction and socioeconomic development in eritrea and to contribute to the opening up of eritrea by enabling progress in democracy, human rights, governance and security. the national indicative programme, in particular its governance component, should enable eritrea to move forward in the process of democratization and to promote the country's openness and stability. we also recall in this resolution that the european parliament must be given powers of control over the edf, which still operates outside the budget of the european union.
in writing. ‒ eritrea is one of the top refugee—producing countries in the world. this is not a coincidence. the country is a notorious human rights violator. one of the main reasons for the endless migration from the country is the fact that eritrea conscripts all men and unmarried women into the so-called ‘national service’. although eritrean law limits national service to 18 months, most conscripts serve for much of their working lives. working conditions are usually very harsh: people do not get paid or they get very small amount of money; brutal torture and beating are used as a way to force soldiers to do their jobs. therefore, i call on the eritrean authorities to respect human rights and, most importantly, immediately to end mandatory military conscription, including forced labour and rampant rights abuses, and to allow freedom of worship, freedom of the media and freedom of expression.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, even though we cannot speak of any progress in the past year. the situation in the country is extremely difficult macedonia is in the most serious political crisis in years, the basic human rights of the bulgarian community are violated, there is a strong politicization of the judiciary and public administration, the media is controlled by the ruling party, reforms are stalled, and the pre-accession process itself frozen. despite the country's problems, i support its aspiration to join the european union, because european integration is a highly demanding and reform-promoting process. although i would like to see more texts related to the problems of the bulgarian community in macedonia, i am pleased with the final version of the resolution, which incorporated many of my proposals and affirmed the wording recognizing the existence of a community with bulgarian identity in the country. we also had great success in developing the part on relations with bulgaria, including wording promoting the conclusion of a treaty of good neighbourliness with bulgaria, joint celebrations of events and personalities from common history and the creation of expert committees on history and education.
in writing. ‒ i supported the progress report for montenegro, as the country has made real progress in the past year. with 22 negotiating chapters open, two of which are closed, montenegro can be described as a champion in the pre-accession process, showing a great will and desire to move towards deeper european integration. despite the progress made, the european parliament calls for further reforms to improve the quality of legislation and for further efforts to fight corruption. on the other hand, although in a separate process, montenegro has undergone swift and efficient nato accession negotiations and is expected to join the alliance by the end of the year. from a security perspective, montenegro's membership of nato is extremely important because, in addition to the serious problems in the entire region related to the growing threat of terrorism and jihadist organisations, the western balkans remain one of the main areas of expansion of russian interests.
in writing. ‒ i voted 'abstention' on the annual report on the banking union because i believe that it will be a long time before supervision is fully effective. the assumption that supervision will be able to deal with the urgent problems of weak capitalisation of individual credit institutions or even entire national banking systems is unrealistic. the report characterises the banking union as bringing many improvements for banks, but at the same time there are many aspects that need to be improved in order for it to work without backsliding for taxpayers. i also disagree with the harmonisation of deposit protection rules. i believe that this approach could have a negative effect by reducing the level of protection in some member states.
in writing. – with this report, that i have been particularly involved with as a shadow rapporteur, the european parliament gives the deserved importance to risk-reduction measures, which will prevent moral hazard. it clearly states that if the costs for bank failures and insolvencies are to be mutualised, the risk must be contained to the maximum extent possible. the report anticipates further measures to achieve a substantial reduction of risks in the european banking system. next to making sure that bail-in rules are consistently applied, it is paving the way for a review of the macro-prudential policy framework, the further reduction of national options and discretion and better handling of non-performing loans. providing a clear incentive for reducing sovereign exposures and a balanced approach towards the third pillar of the banking union, the report makes a strong statement for a prudent and forward-looking system. i welcome the report and would like to thank all colleagues for their support and i look forward to our future work on banking union legislation.
mr president, refit was designed to be a firewall and watchdog since 2012. the programme implemented over 200 actions and contributed to savings for businesses and individuals, which is great. however, this motion for a resolution does not cover very obvious items. the idea is to go simple, right? but there are 65 key documents on refit, so it is not that simple or user-friendly. the commission work programme for 2016 includes 40 refit initiatives, but not that many of them concern the reduction of the administrative burden for beneficiaries of eu funding. at the same time, original investments through the eu budget for the period 2014-2020 total over eur 250 billion. billions of those euros are absorbed by bureaucracy in the process of application, management and control of eu-funded projects. in november 2015, 92% of the meps in this chamber voted in favour of a resolution for cutting red tape, but few of those priorities are implemented in the resolution. i support the commission in that initiative, but when things are not going as planned more concrete action is required. mr president, many citizens still do not have sufficient knowledge about the values on which european integration is based, nor how the european union and its institutions function and directly influence their countries and their own activities. to help citizens understand that the european union benefits our everyday life we need to bring the european union closer to its citizens, explaining in practical terms what the eu does for each of us. enhancing dialogue about european union in our schools, associations and public spaces is essential, especially in the current situation of an increasingly globalised world which faces unprecedented challenges. teaching about the eu should reflect the complex relationship between the european union and its member states. it should be clear for all citizens that the eu has been shaped by its member states with their unique histories and diverse cultures. i believe that an intercultural approach to education policy is highly needed.
in writing. i believe that the introduction of european citizenship education in schools is extremely important because it will allow children from an early age to be familiar with their rights and obligations as european citizens and to participate fully in the political life of europe and their own country. the decline in youth voting is a particularly worrying trend, which i believe clearly demonstrates the need for civic education that introduces young people to european democratic institutions, principles and practices, and the opportunities that european integration offers them. the lack of understanding of how the eu works and its core values and principles makes younger generations of europeans easy targets for disinformation campaigns aimed at undermining the foundations of a democratic europe and weakening its institutions, fuelling populist and nationalist attitudes. this is a challenge that deserves a european response that respects national competences and educational traditions. the european dimension in education will help to rebuild the weakened link between the european union and its citizens by creating a sense of belonging to a community based on values and the rule of law. in this context, it is important to ensure that teachers are motivated to teach this knowledge to young people and have all the necessary resources.
in writing. the european union is facing increasing challenges - local, national, global, economic, political. to be able to face them and to go on stronger, it is important to feel european, to know how the union works, what it can do for us and what we can do for it. i therefore believe that knowledge and belonging to the eu should be built from an early age, and schools in all member states should promote the european dimension in education. the european parliament's report on eu education in schools provides excellent guidance on how to impart knowledge of the union's objectives and mechanisms and to encourage critical thinking about europe's priorities and values. only in this way will the younger generation be prepared to work and live as active citizens in an increasingly integrated union and a globalised world. learning about the eu in school also requires a new approach, alongside teacher training, as mentioned in the report. i believe it is key that the classroom uses interactive methods and examples of how the eu is relevant to the lives of each of us.
