mr president, commissioner, for several years now you have been talking about the need for a comprehensive policy on the refugee crisis and on migration, and it still does not work. there can be no successful migration policy with just one external border or just one agreement, as with turkey. naval operations off the italian coast have sent refugees to the balkans. the closure of the balkan route has brought them back to the gates of italy. now, new corridors will open up through bulgaria and albania. the agreement with turkey is not a benchmark for european policy, it has started to stall, creating more problems than concrete results. the new border and coast guard strategy will keep schengen europe as a fortress, but leave three countries - bulgaria, romania and croatia - out of the policy. finally, the commission proposes new ideas for dublin reform. we expected more, commissioner, you only offer cosmetic corrections. once again, the principle of solidarity will be circumvented, and there will definitely be a double standard towards some countries. you asked if the crisis is an opportunity to deal with or a disaster. there is no such dilemma, mr. avramopoulos, because the crisis has already claimed thousands of lives.
in writing. the crisis in european agriculture was caused in part by political decisions taken in brussels, the most tangible of which are the effects of the so-called russian embargo. since 2014 to date, milk prices in my country, bulgaria, have continued to decline, and bulgarian producers in the sector have reported a decline in revenues of almost 20%. the losses of the agricultural industry in bulgaria from the russian embargo, including the processing, in the various sectors reach nearly 300 million leva from august 2014 to today. despite the enormous difficulties facing our farmers, which cost billions, the european commission continues its policy of opening its doors to imports from third countries, which often receive subsidies from the country of origin and which undermine european production. the european commission must stop misleading the sector with disproportionately low aid and proposals to seek new markets in a sector with high seasonal amplitudes such as agriculture. it is high time that measures were proposed to protect the european producer from imports from third countries.
in writing. ‒ codification is a normal thing and i always support such reports, of course it should happen smoothly and without any change in substance or if such change is necessary, it should be minimal. it has become clear that this is precisely the codification that is needed to reduce the administrative burden and that will allow more acp countries to import quality goods into the community. of course, it should be noted here that most of the companies there are either owned or part-owned by companies from the union, so in this way we help the eu economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it recommends adopting the commission's proposal without amendment, the aim of which is to ensure transparency, simplification and clarity of the legislation on products originating in the acp countries and their access to the eu market. in particular, the proposal regulates the import of products originating in acp countries which are not leastdeveloped countries (ldcs), granting them duty-free and quota-free access to the union market pending the conclusion and application of the respective economic partnership agreements. this temporary instrument has been subject to numerous revisions and amendments and is clarified and simplified in the new commission proposal. the first thing to do is to increase readability and legal certainty, and that is why i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ it is our job to ensure transparency, clarity and simplification of eu legislation. therefore i support the codification and recast of council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 of 20 december 2007 applying the arrangements for products originating in certain states which are part of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states. in this sense, it is important to note that this proposal contains a straightforward codification of the existing legal text, without any significant change in its substance. on the other hand, this could serve as a basis for agreement establishing or leading to the establishment of economic partnership agreements. here it is vital to emphasise the fact that the establishment of economic partnership agreements with acp states will boost their economic growth and will promote reforms.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the draft council decision on the signing of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial means provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community, of the one part, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, of the other part, because the agreement is of great economic importance for the eu. the greenland agreement is the third most important for the eu in terms of economic value - it gives european vessels access to a wide range of fish stocks in the greenland eez, while providing eu financial assistance of €17.8 million per year for five years. the report thus ensures financial benefits for both parties and coherence of fishing activities in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation for an eu-macao agreement on certain aspects of air services, because it guarantees the right of establishment of all eu carriers. the agreement provides guarantees for compliance with eu law in the areas of competition and safety protection.
in writing. ‒ i supported the agreement on air services between the european union and the government of macao because in practice it replaces certain provisions in the existing 15 bilateral air services agreements concluded between eu member states and macao. to clarify this statement, it is important to emphasise the fact that traditionally international aviation relations between member states and third countries have been governed by bilateral air services agreements. in the long term, these agreements have broken eu laws and have promoted anti-competitive practices. therefore, the negotiated agreement with macao will solve many issues when it comes to safety, taxation and compatibility with competition rules. last but not least, it will become example for other countries.
in writing. ‒ undoubtedly, extending the minimum standard rate for vat at 15% is in the interest of the proper functioning of the internal market. this is a significant achievement, since current rules have not been updated to reflect new developments and new economic realities such as the rise of a digital industry. in this sense, extending the minimum standard rate for vat at 15% will on the one hand facilitate economic growth and on the other hand will fight tax fraud. therefore, we should support it.
in writing. – value added tax is a major source of tax revenue in the member states and as such it should be clearly and precisely regulated. with the report on the minimum vat rate, we make sure that these revenues are present. even though the amendment of the directive has come a bit too late and for several months there was no legislation on the minimum threshold for vat, i am glad that the report is being voted and i fully support it.
in writing. ‒ i support cooperation between europol and brazil because it aims to improve and strengthen joint action between them in the fight against organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime affecting several member states. the terms of this agreement include the exchange of information on criminal proceedings, on methods of combating and preventing crime and assistance in the investigation of crime. i believe that cooperation is an important factor in addressing security challenges not only for the eu and its member states, but also for the world.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that we are living in a very globalised and developed world. but today’s world is not peaceful and secure. because of increasing globalisation, the world is facing security threats and challenges that are different in scale and sophistication. in light of this, it is important to note that today’s global security threats and challenges such as organised crime, terrorism, cyber-attacks, credit card fraud, human and drug trafficking cannot be resolved by independent state, organisation or specific sector policy. therefore, we need more ambitious, more coordinated and more holistic approaches to solve them. in this context, strategic cooperation agreement between brazil and europol can be regarded as a big step forward in fight against organised crime, illegal trafficking, cybercrime, terrorism and etc. in addition, it is also important to note that security cooperation between eu and brazil is urgent since upcoming 2016 olympic games in brazil are expected to increase criminal activities in the state. in this sense, security cooperation between europol and brazil will ensure safety for athletes, delegations, tourists and guests.
in writing. – in these times of turmoil and increased threat of terrorism attacks in europe, we should use all means to strengthen our capacities to cope with the threats. brazil is increasingly relevant in the fight against organised crime, including illegal immigration and trafficking in human beings. an agreement between europol and brazil, especially months before the 2016 olympic games, is important for the enable the exchange of specialist knowledge, information as well as advice and support related to criminal investigations. hence, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that international waters must be protected from encroachment and that there must be stricter controls on illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, mineral exploitation, drilling, pollution and marine litter. i support the creation of an international instrument under the un convention on the law of the sea that will reduce the damage currently being done to the marine ecosystem by ensuring the sustainable management of marine resources in international waters.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for the resolution because there is no doubt that we should support efforts made by the un (in particular unga) to move the issue of marine biological diversity beyond areas of national jurisdiction to a point where an internationally legally binding instrument can be foreseen. in fact, it is our common international duty to suppress the increased pressure on the sustainability and conservation of the marine biodiversity caused by marine activities. in this context, i fully believe that the eu should play an important role not only in development of this new instrument but also in its implementation process because the union has experience in regulation and coordination of marine activities beyond areas of national jurisdiction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because in order to facilitate the agricultural sector and to guarantee food security in the eu, we should pay serious attention to proposals for the revision of eu legislation on zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the union of breeding animals and their germinal products (semen, oocytes and embryos). i believe that there are two important steps that have to be taken. first, we should work to ensure animal health and welfare, including transport conditions for live animals inside and outside the union. thus, the eu and all actors in the zootechnical sector will take responsibility and will tackle the inhuman treatment of animals not only within the eu but also in third countries. second, we should facilitate cooperation between breed societies and breeding operations in order to remove obstacles to the free movement of breeding animals and their genetic material.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration, as it is a continuation of the cowardly liberal policy. the report highlights as key priorities the establishment of a mandatory migrant redistribution system, the replacement of the existing dublin regulation with a centralised asylum procedure organised by european hotspots (so that a person will effectively apply for asylum throughout the eu rather than in a single member state), and more legally-legal routes for economic migrants. this is completely at odds with my understanding of how to deal with the wave of immigration that is flooding europe. my colleagues and i from the epp believe that the priorities should be to increase controls at the external borders of the european union, to increase the efficiency of the repatriation of failed asylum seekers, and to allocate more funding to europol, the european asylum support office and frontex.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a long-term strategy for a genuinely comprehensive, joint and humanitarian management of the migration crisis in europe. it is a structured and balanced document, in which the principle of solidarity underpins the proposed approach. solidarity, both internally between member states and externally towards third countries, is expressed in a series of measures, such as relocation and resettlement schemes. the document also makes recommendations for the successful integration of refugees into the eu and the consideration of vulnerable people. the report also looks at the external dimension of this policy, stressing the importance of strengthening the protection of the external borders, which also involves strengthening the union's agencies and effectively combating the smuggling of migrants. finally, i welcome the emphasis on cooperation with third countries, which remains essential if we are to tackle the root causes of migration flows and anticipate future crises as far as possible.
in writing. ‒ mr president president, ladies and gentlemen, i am grateful for the impressive support both in the libe committee and in the vote today on the amendment i proposed, that frontline countries which are not part of the schengen area should be able to participate in and benefit from the establishment of a european border and coast guard on an equal footing with the schengen countries. this is particularly relevant for countries such as bulgaria and romania, which are charged with the responsibility of defending the external borders of the european union, but which, despite meeting the admission criteria, remain outside the schengen area. in insisting on the abolition of a two-speed europe, i will continue to work for equal treatment of bulgaria and romania in the formation and operation of a european border and coast guard in all the reports that lie ahead.
in writing. ‒ undoubtedly, nowadays we are facing unprecedented migration crisis across the mediterranean. undoubtedly, we are in need of a holistic approach in order to tackle effectively the migrant crisis, its scale and the complexity of the problems related to it. in fact, such a holistic approach we can find in the roadmap proposed by the alde to get a grip of a migrant crisis. the roadmap proposes seven urgent measures such as creation of european rapid refugee emergency force (erref), establishment of european border and coast guard (ebcg), creation of european blue card for economic migrants, peace plan and marshall plan for the mediterranean region. i believe that the eu should implement these measures in order not only to grip of migration crisis but also to strengthen global approach to migration and mobility.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mrs karim because i think it stresses to a large extent the importance of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality and of enhanced cooperation with national parliaments, as enshrined in european law. i particularly agree with the call on the european commission to pay more attention to how the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are respected in the process of european legislation. i believe that national parliaments should be encouraged to be more involved in the process of monitoring compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, since in most cases only the polish and swedish parliaments send their position. i also support the initiative to check subsidiarity and to carry out a full impact assessment at the end of the legislative negotiations before the relevant legislation enters into force.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that principles of subsidiarity and proportionality should apply to eu’s common commerce policy in a proper way. this is so, because of the importance of the policy in the formation process of eu’s economic relations with third countries and regional organisations. thereby, in a long term perspective, both principles (subsidiarity and proportionality) will bring transparency in cases when the union carry out trade negotiations which on the other hand will speed up ratification procedure of trade agreements between the eu and a third party.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report by ms kaufman on the refit programme, which supports the ongoing process of checking whether european legislation is fit for purpose and focuses on the quality, not just the quantity, of legislative initiatives. i also support the proposal to enable national parliaments to evaluate new legislation. this will help to assess the challenges they face in implementing laws and regulations.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour because we should acknowledge that the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) represents an important step towards simplifying legislation and reducing administrative burdens of regulation for businesses as well as eliminating barriers to growth and job creation. looking from this perspective, we should work to ensure predictability, legal certainty and transparency of refit. in doing so, however, we should not forget that the impact of legislation on large enterprises and on smes may differ. therefore, we should propose and implement legislation that clearly states that all employees have a right to the highest level of protection regarding health and safety in the workplace, regardless of the size of the employer or the underlying contract.
in writing. – unnecessary bureaucracy tarnishes the image of the european union and is a burden for businesses and citizens. it also slows down economic growth and the creation of new job opportunities. i strongly support the necessity to cut red tape, remove regulatory burdens, simplify and improve legislation, so that the eu policy is able to deliver results faster and more efficiently. therefore, i welcome the refit report and i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i agree with some of the key issues it highlights. we need better and better rules if we want our commercial sectors to grow and to be able to support the creation of new businesses, which are often key drivers of innovation. in view of the principle of subsidiarity, i believe that the report does not seek to interfere with our work in the juri committee. the results of impact assessments before taking hasty steps in terms of policy and over-regulation, and the focus on an effective enforcement mechanism, are crucial issues. they will not only contribute to a more favourable economic environment across the eu, but also achieve a level playing field.
in writing. ‒ ladies and gentlemen,i support the report on better regulation of the single market as it is a good basis for achieving a holistic and integrated approach that does not place undue burdens on the manufacturing sector, innovation or trade, but contributes to the creation of a sustainable market as a prerequisite for the long-term economic development of the eu and the prosperity of its citizens. building a single market is at the heart of the european project and continues to be a means of boosting economic growth and job creation in the eu. the achievement of the european single market and the digital single market requires a strong commitment and shared responsibility of each european institution towards open and transparent regulation that takes into account the positions of all stakeholders at european and national level. a key step in improving regulation in the single market is to eliminate unnecessary regulation, red tape and their negative effects. simplifying access to the single market and taking advantage of the digital revolution are key factors in achieving a competitive regulatory environment that supports jobs and business in europe. in addition, as we work towards the creation of technology-neutral and future-oriented market regulation, we should also focus our efforts on raising awareness of existing single market services targeting businesses and citizens, such as solvit, adr and odr.
in writing. ‒ the eu is the biggest player on the global trading scene because we are the world’s largest single market with transparent rules and regulations. in fact, the single market has brought tremendous benefits for european citizen and businesses but it has not always operated smoothly. the full potential of free movement of goods, services and capital has been unexploited due to missing legislation and lack of enforcement. therefore, i believe that we should work to implement single market regulation, regulation that is based on the principle of subsidiarity and aims before all to be effective and efficient. this necessarily means that we should create a competitive regulatory environment which in practice will facilitate but not frustrate production, innovation and commerce. in a long-term perspective, a competitive regulatory environment will bring economic growth to the eu and prosperity to its citizens
in writing. – as a firm supporter of policies which encourage and support the development of smes and also a member of the imco committee, i welcome the report that analyses how to make the whole policy cycle more efficient in the interest of smes and consumers. establishing a functioning european single market which supports production, innovation and trade is of utmost importance for the stimulation of growth across the eu. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
i have supported this material because when i travel around the czech republic as a member of the european parliament and debate with children about the eu in different schools, i feel the imbalance of information and knowledge among our young generation. some schools place a certain emphasis on public affairs and eu-related issues, while others underestimate them. i believe therefore that we should encourage member states to promote the dissemination of eu information in their school systems. i don't think this is about propaganda and celebrating the eu. i think that we should not do that in any case, but young people should have enough information to decide for themselves how to approach the european integration process and whether to support it, but i feel that they simply do not have that information. so if this material leads to young people in europe having more information, then this material has fulfilled its role.
mr president, in the last few years the european union has been going through a severe economic and financial crisis and all efforts have been directed towards overcoming it. but it is also suffering from a crisis of citizenship. according to the latest eurobarometer data, 44% of citizens feel that they do not have enough knowledge about the functioning of the european union, while 52% feel that their vote does not matter. i find these statistics alarming. it is no surprise that people feel increasingly distant from brussels and what is happening and being decided in the european capital. to regain its legitimacy, the european union must inevitably reconnect with its citizens. that is why i supported the report on the study of the european union in school. the young people must be taught to read european integration critically, they must know not only what the role of the member states is in the development of the european union, but also how the union influences political processes at national level. the european union affects every aspect of our lives, european citizens, especially young people, need to be aware of the added value of our membership of the european union.
in writing. - i did not support this report and i will explain why. i think we should leave training and training programmes to the member states and not claim powers that are not provided for in the treaties. i am a supporter of subsidiarity and i do not think we have the power to impose such advice as in this report on the study of the eu in schools in europe. and look at the reasons that are laid out in this report - to prevent euroscepticism! i don't consider myself a eurosceptic, and my view is that the eu as a political and economic community provides many advantages that a country like mine would not have, in particular the common market and free trade. however, i believe that studying the eu and the history of the creation of the union in order to strengthen the european identity of citizens, as stated in the report, is not what my constituents are fighting for - we want a europe of nations! not a federal europe!
in writing. ‒ mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i supported the report on 'teaching the european union in schools' because i believe that the measures it proposes will improve the awareness and interest of european citizens in european measures that affect their lives. the introduction of a study of the european union will lead to a better understanding of its institutions and their interrelations, the mechanisms and timing of their work, and to an improvement in awareness of the rights which the union grants to its citizens and the means of protecting them. last but not least, learning about the european union will remind children in europe of the historical reasons for its creation and the need to preserve it in the name of our common area of justice, freedom, security and solidarity.
in writing. ‒ i support the european parliament's report on european union education in schools. i had the opportunity to participate in its preparation as rapporteur for the european people's party. i am convinced that the european union should be studied in school not in terms of how it works, but in terms of the rights and freedoms it provides for young people. each member state should develop a methodology based on its own experience, because only by knowing and overcoming history can we explain the reasons for the existence of the union as it is today and the benefits of our membership. the member states are responsible for their education systems, but the union supports them in setting common objectives and exchanging good practice. one of these aims and ideas is to include europe and the european union in school curricula. the european parliament's committee on culture and education believes that there is a need to deepen the consideration of eu-related issues in order to bridge the gap between europe and its citizens. the eu must become more visible and understandable to its citizens.
in writing. ‒ i believe in the need for a european dimension in education, given the enormous impact of the eu on citizens' daily lives. the eu needs to be more visible and better integrated into the curriculum and extracurricular activities - this would help to promote a greater understanding and commitment to its core values. the eu is going through a crisis of its democratic legitimacy, but this would be a logical way to restore and strengthen the union's link with its citizens. the report also highlights the important role of the 'erasmus+', 'europe for citizens' and 'creative europe' programmes in promoting education and training, language skills, active citizenship, cultural awareness and intercultural understanding. these programmes undoubtedly contribute to strengthening european citizenship and it is necessary to provide appropriate financial support for these programmes.
in writing. ‒ ladies and gentlemen, the eu is facing unprecedented challenges that need to be addressed at european and national level, but most importantly, these responses need to be supported by citizens. unfortunately, according to the 2014 eurobarometer, citizens have limited knowledge of the eu, of the work of its institutions, of the general policies that protect their rights and well-being. moreover, euroscepticism is growing and the number of citizens who feel distanced from the european project is increasing. in these circumstances, it is necessary to start a dialogue about the eu in schools in an organised way. while education is a competence of the member states, the eu can promote cooperation between them and support and complement national action in this field. the previous pan-european programmes in the education sector and the current erasmus+ programme have contributed to a considerable extent to the eu's integration processes. action at eu level is needed to bring a european dimension to our children's education so that they can know not only the geography, history and culture of europe, but also that they are citizens of a great union of established freedoms and values. member states have an interest in making the eu more visible and understandable to their own citizens, and should therefore not oppose the initiative to teach the eu in schools.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report, because mobility in vocational education and training (vet) is a source of genuine and diverse learning experience. unfortunately, just a small percentage of young people currently in professional training are involved in a mobility programme during their training. experience-oriented education, and of course the learning and training mobility within it, incorporates inputs from the business environment to enable participants to react in a flexible way to the rapidly changing world and labour market demands. individuals need to be motivated to engage in mobility and to take up lifelong learning through efficient and sustainable financing tools and themes. erasmus+ proved to be the most successful mobility programme, but we should do better in organising, facilitating and promoting mobility in vet and ensuring full recognition of the knowledge and skills acquired in the context of vet. it also has to be clear that the modernisation of vet systems for lifelong learning and mobility require active involvement and commitment from all stakeholders.

mr president, erasmus+ is one of the european union's most successful programmes and a symbol of its own. the opportunity to live in another country, to experience a new culture and to interact with different people is a great opportunity for both professional and personal development of young people. experience abroad is a proven plus in finding a new job. this is why mobility opportunities should cover different target groups. i support the report which calls for the promotion of mobility in vocational education and training. unfortunately, in the new erasmus+ programme, it is being left in the background. the differences in the procedures for the recognition and accreditation of work experience abroad in the different member states also create additional complexity. increasing mobility in this area will help to increase the attractiveness of vocational education. young people who have chosen the vocational training path should have the same mobility prospects as those of students in higher education. currently only 1% of them participate in mobility schemes. i believe that erasmus+ should provide equal opportunities for all.
in writing. ‒ 'erasmus+' is perhaps one of the eu's greatest successes and we must therefore closely monitor its implementation and citizens' feedback on its improvement. vocational education and training is promoted through various eu instruments and mobility is an important element in character building and experience gaining. the report i was asked to follow on behalf of my conservative group gives some good ideas, such as calling for better accessibility to existing vocational education and training mobility initiatives, especially for families in economically disadvantaged situations, and measures to facilitate labour market integration. at the same time, however, there is a focus on this mobility across sectors, which i do not think should be the goal. it is also proposed to create a european standard for mobility in vocational education and training, without specifying what exactly this entails. it is important that we listen to the concerns of citizens in this regard and see where the problems lie - whether in the red tape and paperwork or in the inaccessibility of such programs for many people with low incomes. in the end, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the report recognises the erasmus+ programme as a success for mobility, but tries to identify its shortcomings. mobility is key to the social integration of young people to make them more competitive in the labour market. however, excessive bureaucracy in educational institutions undoubtedly represents an obstacle to the effective implementation of the erasmus+ programme. action is needed to stimulate the number of successful applications. the youth unemployment rate in the eu as a whole currently stands at 22.1%. this raises the question of the mismatches between skills and labour market requirements, illustrated by the high unemployment rate. the report calls for account to be taken of socioeconomic constraints that impede equal access to vocational education and training, including mobility. it must be ensured that these programmes are accessible to all citizens without any discrimination. the creation of a common european education area would contribute to the creation and development of a stronger european identity and a stronger sense of citizenship.

member of the commission. mr president, madam minister, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your work. thank you again for this enlightening debate. i think that everyone here today agrees on one thing, namely that turkey is a strategic partner for the european union. this is due to the geostrategic location, this is due to the number of inhabitants. it is therefore clear that the european union has a very vital interest in finding a sensible form of cooperation here. cooperation with turkey has - and this is obvious - its ups and downs. but it is also clear that this cooperation must be very comprehensive. and the situation with turkey is complex. for example, it is very important in the economic field, which has hardly been mentioned today, because europe is by far turkey's most important economic and investment partner. we have about 600 000 employees in europe who are employed by turkish companies. turkey is europe's sixth most important partner. so it is necessary to find a reasonable form of cooperation here. the upgrading of the customs union, for example, is therefore an important task which we have been working on intensively for over a year and a half. the current challenge of the refugee crisis has given this form of cooperation a new impetus, and this is also quite obvious. we have developed an action plan that includes a number of different elements. visa liberalisation is an issue, and visa liberalisation has been on the agenda. the aim was and is to speed up this question. but visa liberalisation does not mean that the next step is automatically accession, as is sometimes assumed. because we have visa liberalisation with many countries around the world, and yet no one is thinking about this country becoming a member. on the other hand, yes, we have a mandate from the european council to conduct accession negotiations here. this is an open mandate since 2005. we are called upon to conduct these negotiations and to reach a result, because the mandate says: we must conduct negotiations open to results. and, frankly, it is my professional prerogative to bring such negotiations to an end. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i have heard many times today how important it is to address and take account of the rule of law in turkey and to ensure that it is upheld. but i can also tell you that this is only possible if we have accession negotiations, because only then will we have leverage, because only then can we make demands. it is a qualitative difference whether i am negotiating accession or whether i am dealing with my neighbour and identifying common points. the commission has a duty to do this, and we have an obligation to do it at this stage. i have therefore noted with interest the comments made by count lambsdorff and others. but, as i said, this is something that is not our job at the moment, but it is our job to implement our mandates, to ensure that we have stability in the region. and i believe that this can only be ensured by having a very close network of cooperation with turkey. this can then also ensure that the current refugee problem, for example, can be addressed and solved in an appropriate way. i can also take this opportunity to tell you that the turkey facility has already started. the occasional statement from turkey that she has not seen a penny is simply not true. it is correct in that we do not pay turkey, but we finance projects in turkey that serve to cover the additional costs and expenses of turkey in terms of accommodation, food, school attendance and to make a significant contribution, including a contribution that the refugees, especially in eastern turkey, have a possibility to stay in the region in order to return immediately to syria, if the security and political situation permits. we are therefore concentrating our expenditure on ensuring that we use the funds appropriately here, primarily in eastern anatolia. initial activities have been launched in this respect. we have spent some 55 million euros to ensure that 350 000 people have food for at least six months. the european union has already made a major contribution to the development of the european union. these are the things that are essential. we should focus on these, and they also help to improve the mutual trust between turkey and europe. there's no question that there's sand in the gearbox. but between partners, between neighbours, it is necessary to have a relationship of trust. we should be interested in that together. and as things develop in the future, the negotiations just happen.

in writing. ‒ i have voted for the text because one of the five headline targets of europe 2020 is to reduce poverty by lifting at least 20 million people out of the risk of poverty or social exclusion by 2020. in order to achieve these goals, firstly we should work to increase the incomes of poor households by improving the effectiveness of social and employment policies. secondly, we should effectively reduce the household costs of poor households; in particular we should fight energy poverty through targeting existing renewable and energy efficiency projects on energy poor households. in light of this, we should work to make energy affordable to all eu citizens. i believe that the fight against poverty in practice is a fight for the future of the eu and millions of europeans, thereby it is our moral duty to lead it to successful end.
in writing. – the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion has increased in most member states, bulgaria being one of them. overall, 24.5 % of the eu population were at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2013. the primary aim of the report is to see how energy policies and consumer prices can have impact on poverty, especially with regard to disadvantaged groups. there is no doubt that reducing, and even abolishing, poverty should be on top of our agendas. hence, i vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported my colleague deva's report because i share his view that private initiative is the main engine for the development of an economy. support for it in developing countries will lead to an accelerated transition from developing countries to developed countries. the problem is also noted that almost always the aid is received by the large firms, and smes are usually subject to more regulation and pressure, while at the same time they employ more than half of the employed in these countries, which is a problem that needs serious attention. an example of how to attract investment in these countries is also shown, namely through public-private partnerships - a way that has proven effective. i hope that the measures in this report will help those countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the resolution because it clearly recognises the importance of the private sector in development and the primary objective of eu development cooperation in reducing poverty. the private sector has the potential to contribute to a sustainable, efficient and long—term development, because economic development is a key to eradicating poverty. of course, this aim could be completed only by promoting human rights and by strengthening democracy, good governance and the rule of law. the european union should strengthen corporate social responsibility, and the public-private partnerships within the post-2015 development agenda should have a strong focus on poverty reduction.

rapporteur.– mr president, let me first of all welcome president hoyer, thank commissioner moscovici, and simply convey my very deep gratitude to all those who worked on this report. as you have seen, this is a comprehensive analysis, it takes a lot of technical work. so both to the shadow rapporteurs, and to all those from the secretariats that worked on this report, i would like to extend my very heartfelt gratitude. now as to the substance, in the light of the extraordinary challenges confronting the european union and member states at present, it is even more urgent that the bank fully commits to implementing its core task: to support projects that contribute to the balanced development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion. the fact that in 2014 the eib successfully implemented one of its most ambitious business plans, amounting to eur 80.3 billion, is undoubtedly a most important achievement. however, virtually 60% of all projects signed in 2014 were allocated to the top five eu economies. in this regard, there is an urgent request for the bank to substantially step up its technical assistance and financial advice in order to overcome insufficient project-generating capacity and low levels of borrowing in some member states. the draft resolution also notes the lack of meaningful follow-up to previous parliament resolutions. in this regard, i would like to highlight some such issues and invite president hoyer and commissioner moscovici to respond. regarding transparency and work with intermediaries, already in 2013 parliament called on the eib to refrain from cooperation with financial intermediaries having a negative track record in terms of transparency, tax evasion or aggressive tax planning practices and abusive transfer pricing, or concerning substantial local ownership. it also encouraged the eib to make funding contingent upon the disclosure of country-by-country tax-relevant data and called on the bank, jointly with the commission, to establish a stringent public list of criteria, ensuring the proper selection of financial intermediaries. regarding parliament-bank cooperation, parliament repeats its call for regular dialogue between its relevant committees and the bank, similar to the practices with the ecb, and strongly encourages that an interinstitutional agreement be concluded without further delay. as to bank supervision, another previous call envisages putting in place effective prudential banking supervision of the eib. regrettably this and other calls have not been taken up by either the commission or the eib so far. as for the european fund for strategic investments, the draft resolution specifically calls on the eib to ensure that the efsi is not indirectly used as a means of increasing the eib’s capital, to regularly review the bank’s involvement in efsi, and to show that the conditions on additionality laid down in article 5 of the efsi regulation have been met. so far it remains to be demonstrated that the fund is in fact generating additional investments beyond the usual financing arrangements. i do trust that this resolution will contribute to further enhancing the key role of the eib, as the bank of the european union, in achieving the union’s strategic political objectives in the immediate future and in the longer-term perspective.
member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank you for the very fruitful, high-quality and very calm debate we have had today, which shows that we are really dealing with a project of general interest. the current economic and financial situation calls for determined political action. we are convinced that the eib's activities are a crucial component of the european union's efforts to restore sustainable growth and employment levels in europe, in particular through the partnership between the commission and the eib in implementing the €315 billion investment plan for europe, the juncker plan. i welcome again the report by parliament on the activities of the eib and i am pleased that fruitful cooperation between the commission and the eib is continuing. a few words on two subjects which have been frequently raised: transparency and the fight against tax evasion, cohesion and convergence. i will also speak about greece, since this subject has been raised, although it is not quite in the system, but i know that it is of great interest to werner hoyer. on transparency and tax evasion, i would remind you that the commission adopted in january 2016 a package to combat tax evasion, which reflects the discussions that took place in the framework of the oecd and the g20 - this is what is known as beps - but also the discussions in the european parliament on the fight against aggressive tax planning. for the commission - and this is what i said at the informal ecofin council in amsterdam eight days ago - we had to go further and this package was a package, a global package which had to be adopted as such. i am really counting on the dutch presidency to do this, and rightly so. in this context, the commission is working intensively with the eib to explore how the eib's policies could evolve to reflect the new measures we will be implementing. i would like to make a few comments on the subject of cohesion and convergence. we want the convergence of the european economy, of the euro area. this is our priority. the euro area is a tremendous success. it has protected the economies that have made this choice, but there is still a problem of dynamics, which is also a problem of fair sharing. the eib and the juncker plan are major tools for the recovery of the european economy, but we cannot have a political criterion in the choice of investments. of course it is preferable, of course it is desirable - and of course the eib and the commission are working on this - that the projects selected cover a whole range of sectors. it is obviously desirable - the eib and the commission are obviously working on it - that all countries should be covered by the juncker plan and i think it is very good that we already have 22, 23 or 25 countries already covered by projects. but the logic was a logic of projects. it's a quality piece of work. the aim is to encourage those who are able to innovate and those who are able to carry out projects in the sectors which are the priorities of the juncker plan. projects, i mean here, must be chosen for their own merits. they must prepare for the future and it is not doing any country any favors to think that there must necessarily be some form of credit spraying. there is a capacity for invention and innovation in all countries of the european union, regardless of their size. that is what must be sought. a word on greece, since the subject has been raised, i do not want to evade it, we are in the middle of the news. i think, and the commission thinks, that we are really in a position to get close to an agreement. there is no doubt that one or more steps still have to be taken, but much has been done and we must not pretend that a new crisis is brewing, when we have come very close to defining the necessary measures and the necessary reforms. i hope we can reach an agreement quickly. the commission will in any case be very determined to do so. we must work on this with great calm, with great objectivity and with a shared will that a reformed, a strengthened greece will return to growth and be able to create jobs. the juncker plan and the eib, which is a major contributor, play a key role here. yes, we need growth all over europe, all over the euro area, and to do that, we really need to make sure that the reforms come through in greece, quickly, in a very determined way. in conclusion, i would say that the juncker plan is on track for us, in the sense that the projects financed - and this is the criterion - are really additional projects, in the sense that they are projects with a higher risk than before. i am accustomed to saying - werner hoyer knows this - that the main criterion for the success of the plan is not so much quantity as quality. the question is, is there a culture shift? is there a change in the culture of economies, with the ability to carry projects, and a change in the culture of european policies, in what we do at the commission, in what we do with the eib, to make sure that it is risk that is encouraged? we must be vigilant, it is not about giving in self-satisfaction. i think that the juncker plan does not cover the whole subject and i am inclined to think that if it succeeds - which is what i want and what i believe - it will have to be extended. this is not a three-year case, but a much longer case. our investment deficit won't stop in mid-2018. but without being complacent, i think that with this plan we are doing a useful job of filling the investment gap that europe is suffering from. this is again the key to raising our potential growth, raising our actual growth, creating many more jobs, reducing unemployment. that is our common objective in all the benches of this house, in the commission, in the bank and in the member states. that is why, once again, we are faced with a debate which i regard as a debate of general interest.
president of the european investment bank. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, let me begin by thanking mr pirinski very much for his report and commissioner moscovici for his very close and fruitful cooperation and support, which we continue to enjoy. i think that more than 40 members of the european parliament have taken the floor today, and i am expected to answer each and every detailed question. i promise you that every issue that has been raised today will be answered by our services or by myself within the next couple of days or weeks, because you deserve the answers. let me concentrate on about seven points which i would like to raise. first of all, i would like to thank mr liberadzki - i think he is not here anymore, but i would still like to thank him - because he pointed out that this is the eu's bank, and we are the eu. if you mandate a bank in europe or outside europe with jobs that need to be done on behalf of europe, then you are well advised to give that job to the eu's bank to those whom you can control, steer and have influence over, and whom you can require to stick to the principles and criteria which the european union sets for lending and the granting of guarantees. in this context, i would like to say that greece is of course a country of specific concern to us, because we have seen over the last few years how difficult it is. we are the bank that was the strongest there before the crisis; we stayed there during the crisis - as the only one, practically; and we are very active now that the crisis is, hopefully, over soon. we have even changed the business model of the bank for the case of greece a little bit - our other centralized model for lending and granting of guarantees is not deployed in greece any more, because we have strengthened our presence on the ground as we want to reach the customers, the clients, the companies and the corporates directly with our staff. third: transparency, ncj policies, and everything that has to do with that. we have received the message and understood mr pirinski, and we will follow it up. we support the commission with all their efforts in this field. this is going to be very difficult in detail, because sometimes you move between the legitimate and the legal; sometimes the devil is in the use of illegitimate but legal means, and that sometimes poses very difficult challenges to a bank and to many other actors. sometimes you wish the legislator would step in and clarify the situation not only what is legal, but also what is legitimate. the next point is the interinstitutional agreement. i completely agree that it is high time to bring it to a conclusion i spoke to several members of the leadership of this european parliament today and we are resolved to bringing this to a conclusion very soon. i want to have that done before the summer break, because this issue should be discussed in substance after the summer break when we have analyses of what the first year of the juncker plan has brought. the key thing is and it has been raised by several people that we must make sure that we have a balanced approach to all member states of the european union. what does that mean? well, of course, the eu bank does not have quotas that is completely impossible, because we go for economically viable and sustainable projects and we observe criteria which are also ecological and of course social, and if these projects do not appear on the list of proposals, then there will not be such a programme. we will not give grants just in order to be present in the country if there is not a good project. but let us look at the realities, and i would like to remove the myth of a lack of balance in the activities of the bank in the european union. if you look at the total investment supported in 2015, the four countries with the highest percentage of activity are latvia with 13.8% of gdp, slovakia with 12.9%, greece with 11.4% and slovenia with 11.4%. at the end of the list you find romania with the 0.3%, bulgaria with 0.3%, ireland with 0.3% and the czech republic with 0.4%. now let's go to the exposure of the bank: where is the bank the most exposed? well, the highest exposure is in cyprus at 15.3% of gdp, slovenia at 11.7%, portugal at 11.0% and hungary 9.9%. at the end of the list are denmark at 1.1%, the netherlands at 1.7%, germany at 1.7% and the uk at 1.9%. this is the reality, and it shows the balance sheet of the bank as an expression of the spirit of solidarity in this european union. anything else is a myth. on the question of steel production in china: what we have heard today in the european parliament, unfortunately, is complete nonsense. the bank has never had and does not have any steel project in china, and the only one that has ever been brought to our attention as an idea by the chinese has been rejected by us. so it is a propaganda thing that we have heard here today; it is not supported by facts. i would like to conclude by saying, on social issues and social housing, that this is a very important point that we have sped up quite a bit, also in connection with the migration crisis, because migration solutions must not go to the detriment of those people in need who also need social housing. so, therefore, we see this as one big area where we have done some considerable stepping up of business. more can be done, however, also in combination or in cooperation with the member states or regions that are interested in that. probably, in some countries, it is not really known on the national level what we do on the regional level, in particular when it comes to migration and to social housing. finally, i would like to say: don't overdraw our capabilities. when the bank was founded in the 1950s in the treaties of rome, no one would have thought that we would one day be an sme bank. but nowadays we need this tool because of lack of access to finance for smes, and we used it for over 300,000 smes last year. that is 30% of our business volume. an additional business volume percentage of 27% is expected to go into climate-related lending. of course, everyone thinks that 11.15% or more of lending should go into innovation and research and development. if you add that up and then come also to the question of digitization, which we have not touched upon here today but which is the key ingredient for preserving or restoring europe's competitiveness in the next couple of years, you easily end up above 100%, and that can't work either. we have to have a balance in this respect as well. we are trying to achieve this with your help.

in writing. ‒ this resolution comes on the eve of the forthcoming revision of the brussels ii regulation on jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and matters of parental responsibility, which is the competence of the legal affairs committee, of which i am a member. it is recommended that the legislative gaps be closed and that cooperation between all member states (with the exception of denmark) be improved in the best interests of the child, following a number of petitions received on the matter in the committee on petitions. i support some of the elements of the resolution, considering that the call for action in the best interests of the child is undeniable, but i think we should not transfer more responsibilities to the commission but should keep them in the national parliaments as it has been the case so far. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ freedom of movement, residence and work is the greatest boost to our self-esteem as european citizens. to be successful, this right must be combined with many others. today's focus is on our parental rights. the brussels iia regulation has shortcomings and a number of petitions received in the european parliament very clearly demonstrate this. there is still much to be done to improve coordination and cooperation between the 28 national child protection systems. i will not forget the painful example of the adoption without parental consent in the uk of a bulgarian child, which strongly engaged the committee on petitions. policies and measures in one member state have an impact on all the others. so, along with what my colleagues are calling for today, i want to highlight two things: 1) in the forthcoming revision of the brussels iia regulation, consider introducing an explicit obligation for the host state in a parental rights case to inform the competent authorities of the state of which the child is a national of all the steps taken in the proceedings; 2) the european commission to provide an information campaign to make citizens aware of their rights and the institutions to which they can turn in a timely manner for assistance in the event of cross-border parental rights disputes.
in writing. – nowadays, we see an increase in international and cross-border marriages, and this trend is expected to grow significantly in the near future: 13% of the marriages in eu are considered ‘international’. it should by no means be children who pay the price when eu member states fail to cooperate and protect children’s best interests in legal proceedings such as cross-border parental custody disputes or adoption decisions. children are the future of the european union – its main but most fragile pillar – and that is why i welcome the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fourth railway package proposed by mrs zille, because it will make this market more open and more competitive. the empowerment of the european railway agency to issue licences and certificates to all cross-border hauliers will greatly facilitate the work of railway hauliers operating in more than one member state, while local hauliers will be able to submit their applications to the local authority. the possibility of creating a 'one-stop-shop' service, acting as a single entry point for all applications, is the right step to reduce red tape and administration and thus facilitate business. of course, for these things to happen, the national agencies and the european railway agency will have to work closely together, which is up to the local authorities, but the agency should not be allowed to do everything.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of a single railway system in the eu has so far, i dare say, failed. i therefore hope that by adopting this package we will be taking the first steps towards achieving the ultimate goal. reducing red tape, introducing single application window and allowing rolling stock manufacturers to certify their products with a single application should help the development of a single railway system. the abolition of national rules always leads to ferment on the part of national carriers. it is therefore good that this transitional period of three years after the entry into force of the regulation is introduced, which can be extended once by one year.
in writing. – efficient transport is a critical component of economic development and is essential in meeting the challenges of mobility. transport availability affects development patterns and can be a boost or a barrier to economic growth. removing the remaining administrative and technical barriers in the railway sector is an important step forward, establishing the conditions to be met to achieve interoperability within the union rail system. that is why i support the report and the improvement of coherence in the national legal frameworks for the interoperability aspects of the internal market for railways.
in writing. ‒ a single rail market is good, of course, we have to work for the accessibility of the rail network in all member states. there's always a "but". this is security. we cannot put the european railway agency in charge of safety and then take the responsibility off the shoulders of the local associations. we need to think about this, especially as we're seeing huge holes in security, and instead of trying to strengthen it, we're going to allow it to be weakened. in addition, the security certificates in different countries have different requirements, which are high in some member states and negligible in others.
in writing. ‒ i support the agreement reached on the fourth railway legislative package. i think that the use of rail transport should be encouraged, not only because it is more environmentally friendly, but also because technological advances make it safer and more comfortable. the agreement reached is a success for passengers and railway companies in europe and a major step towards the creation of a single european railway area. increased competition in the sector will improve the quality of passenger services and make them more accessible and attractive. the removal of technical and regulatory barriers will improve safety and reduce the final cost to passengers, while exploiting the potential for job creation.
in writing. i supported this report because i strongly support the creation of a stricter and clearer regime when it comes to benchmarking. we need clearer rules to avoid fraud, like the recent libor manipulation scandal. when investing, one should be able to do so without fear of red tape and other burdens. clear rules and a differentiated approach are needed to move forward on the right track, especially given how many countries in the eu alone rely primarily on continuous investment flows. i also welcome the differentiation towards third countries, which have often been unfairly given an advantage over some member states for purely political reasons.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014, section iii commission and executive agencies, as for the 21st consecutive year the european court of auditors has failed to provide a clear statement of the actual expenditure of the eu budget. the error rate in commission payments remains very high at 4.4%, with a maximum error rate of 2%. on the positive side, the report makes many recommendations on how to improve budget implementation and calls on the commission to establish a new approach to the management of eu investment and expenditure that better aligns the budget with the eu's long-term strategic objectives.
