in writing. the milk market in europe is experiencing a difficult period of low prices and very low profit margins. the milk market observatory recently warned that the current downturn and low prices in the milk sector show no signs of recovery. in the last few months, the price of raw milk has been 13% lower than the average price over the previous five years, whilst the price of whole milk powder has continued to fall - it is 5% lower - and the average price of skimmed milk powder and butter has also fallen. this downward trend in milk prices demonstrates that the existing cap instruments and the measures taken towards dairy farmers are not effective in this area and cannot deal with the crisis in the dairy sector. i expect the council and the commission to present details of the steps that need to be taken in the immediate and long term to relieve the pressure on milk and milk products producers.
in writing. news of earthquakes in the dairy sector is now a daily occurrence. and while bureaucrats may take this for granted, thousands of dairy farms across europe are going bankrupt. these are small and medium-sized family farms which cannot respond to all the market trends that accompany the dairy sector. the milk market watchdog recently warned that the current downturn and low prices showed no signs of recovery. in the last few months, the price of raw milk in europe has been 13% lower than in the previous five years. in my country, bulgaria, the purchase price of milk in some regions has fallen to 15-16 cents, which producers rightly take as a mockery of the labour and investment involved. and for some of them, it's their main and/or only livelihood and source of income. in some regions, such as mountain areas, this is the only economic activity possible. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the cap. this aid should be targeted at specific dairy products specific to each country, rather than those covering the needs of only some of the member states.
in writing. alongside the €500 million financial package to support european farmers, the commission proposed a set of measures to tackle the crisis in the dairy sector, such as the implementation of voluntary agreements on milk production and supply, a temporary increase in state aid, a doubling of the intervention ceilings for skimmed milk powder and butter, advertising campaigns and an increase in international trade, export credits, etc. however, the crisis continues to deepen, dairy farmers are accumulating losses and debts and are threatened with bankruptcy. the average european milk price is below 28 cents/litre, while production continues to grow. the milk production in the first two months of 2016 was 7,4% higher than in the same period of the previous year. it must be clearly emphasized that the main cause of the current situation is overproduction! it is not possible to stabilise the market without limiting milk production in the countries which have increased it after the abolition of the quota system. the measures to temporarily withdraw quantities of milk from the market are not working. the dairy farmers in mountain and less-favoured areas most affected by the crisis need specific support measures, such as buying-in incentives and co-financing of transport costs with european funds, to protect them from bankruptcy and to preserve dairy production in these areas.

in writing. – strong data protection principles are in place in the eu in order to protect citizens’ rights and privacy. in the eu data protection is considered both a fundamental right and a key component of a digital single market. cross-border data flows between the eu and the usa are the highest in the world. personal data exchanges across the atlantic not only boost economic growth but also represent a crucial element of eu-us cooperation in the law enforcement field, and in particular the cooperation between the eu and the us in the field of ‘national security’. nevertheless, large-scale us intelligence collection programmes affect transatlantic data flows and specifically the fundamental rights of europeans, their right to privacy and protection of personal data. we should work in close cooperation with the us administration in order to implement the eu-us privacy shield framework as soon as possible. this framework ensures legal certainty on how personal data should be transferred from the eu to the us. however, in order for the privacy shield agreement to enter in force, the eu should encourage the united states to commit to legislative reform of surveillance laws within a reasonable time. these reforms should be in synchronisation with the protection of personal data under the eu charter of fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ i support the report on poverty through the lens of gender equality. according to the latest eurostat data, the number of women in poverty remains consistently higher than that of men, with some 64 million women currently in poverty compared to 57 million men. i believe that gender equality achieved in the labour market by increasing social and economic well-being benefits not only women but also the economy and society as a whole. the budgetary constraints imposed by the commission and implemented by the member states, in addition to the economic crisis of the last few years, have increased inequality and affected women in particular, exacerbating the problem of poverty among women and leading to their increasing exclusion from the labour market, leading to social exclusion and lack of participation in public life in terms of access to education, culture and information, justice and primary health services. i believe that gender equality provides a tool to combat poverty among women, as it has a positive impact on productivity and economic growth and leads to greater participation of women in the labour market.

in writing. – according to statistics there are now more than 65 million women living in poverty, compared to 57 million men. the draft ini report focuses amongst others on the root causes of female poverty, the scope of women’s poverty in the eu and the impact of social exclusion through poverty on the living and working conditions. it concludes, amongst others, that female poverty is caused by a variety of factors: stereotypes, pay gaps between men and women, lack of work—life balance, and all kind of gender— based discrimination which affects mainly women. i vote in favour of this issue to be able to enable a better and fairer handling of issues concerning gender equality.
in writing. ‒ the creation of a single market is perhaps one of the most important things the eu is trying to tackle, and any attempt to sabotage it must be stopped at an early stage. i understand member states trying to keep 'foreign' players out of their national markets for fear of competition, but i can only assure them that the single market is in everyone's interest. i hope that the review of non-tariff barriers will be completed in time and that the ways of removing them described therein will be effective. i'll be watching this review with interest.
in writing. ‒ mr president,the removal of customs barriers through cooperation and the sharing of common values is one of the greatest achievements of the european project. however, within the single market, non-tariff barriers still exist that prevent europe from reaching its full potential. the report on non-tariff barriers rightly focuses on the actions that should be taken to improve the efficiency of the single market. among them is the call for member states to abandon protectionist measures and open up their internal market to the more competitive european market. to achieve this, the commission should strengthen the enforcement and advocacy of these principles. in this way, it will ensure that member states comply with the rules relating to the single market, rather than creating new, additional legal provisions on matters already covered by existing legal rules. finally, all member states, the commission and the european parliament must unite around the removal of existing non-tariff barriers. in this way, our market will become more accessible and competitive for our businesses and our citizens. as final consumers, our citizens will experience tangible benefits from the removal of non-tariff barriers through more competitive prices and increased benefits in a fully functioning single market.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the main difficulties faced by companies or citizens when engaging in cross-border trade. the existence of still too many different national provisions poses a serious challenge for companies and individuals to engage in cross-border trade. different countries introduce additional barriers to their markets, which often discourage firms, especially smes, from expanding their activities.
in writing. – i am a strong supporter of a free market economy, nevertheless i understand the importance of regulation in the european free market economy. i vote in favour of the regulation of non-tariff barriers in the single market to help improve our european single market. the report provides the definition, understanding the ntb as being a disproportionate or discriminatory regulatory action which results in a burden or cost to be borne by a firm which seeks to enter a market and which is not borne by firms already in the market, or a cost which accrues to non-national firms which is not borne by domestic firms. at the same time it recognises member state’s right to regulate and to defend public policy objectives, while ensuring that regulatory measures are proportionate. this is vital for understanding the need for a better regulation of non-tariff barriers in the single market.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the single market strategy as it provides ways to improve and harmonise the single market. the expected gains from completing the reform of the single market amount to almost eur 3 trillion, and will also lead to the creation of new jobs and the reduction of high unemployment rates within the european union. the report contains many concrete proposals that can lead to improvements in the functioning of the single market in a targeted way, such as a platform to combat undeclared work or the fully electronic public procurement system proposed by the member states. i also fully support the ultimate objective of the reform of the single market which has been initiated, namely the removal of unfair barriers for individual member states within the single market.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i support the proposals in the report on the single market strategy, as i believe they will have a positive impact on the internal market and in particular on start-ups, smes and consumer protection. i am confident that the measures envisaged, which include simplifying vat rules, reducing the costs of registering businesses and creating a digital single market, are important and progressive steps towards further integrating the single market. the fragmentation of the single market remains one of the main obstacles to achieving sustainable and structural economic growth. we must therefore intensify our efforts to build a strategic approach to the single market that becomes a driver of sustainable development and job creation and ensures a highly competitive social market economy at a time when unemployment rates remain high. this report will make a significant contribution to a more ambitious single market strategy by presenting concrete proposals for certain policies and focusing our efforts on building a deeper and fairer internal market that is both modern and progressive.
in writing. – i supported the resolution because the eu single market has brought tremendous benefits for both european citizens and european business. yet the full potential of free movement of goods, services and capital has been unexploited because of ever changing environment of the market. therefore, the eu should adapt new ideas and measures proposed by the new single market strategy in order to stimulate competition, trade, efficiency and quality on the market. the new single market strategy aims to improve mobility for services providers, ensure the growth of innovative businesses and enhance access to goods and services throughout the eu. most importantly, the strategy focuses on helping business, and in particular smes, micro-enterprises and start-ups. these business are not only the backbone of eu economies but also are the main engine of growth and job creation within the eu. in this regard, we should support the single market strategy because it aims to unlock the full potential of the eu single market by promoting entrepreneurship and development.
in writing. ‒ the resolution adopted today is the european parliament's response to the strategy proposed by the european commission to modernise the single market. europe has come through the global financial crisis at a high price. member states' economies continue to languish due to youth unemployment, low growth rates and lack of investment. the single market is at the heart of european integration, but there are still too many obstacles, especially for small and medium-sized businesses and start-ups. few of them go beyond the local or regional market and operate at european level. the european parliament's attention is therefore focused on their needs for simplification of regulatory requirements, access to finance and promotion of innovation. with 423 votes in favour, the european parliament supported the objectives of the strategy and gave a clear signal that it expected it to be successfully implemented soon.
in writing. ‒ completing the single market has always been and remains a key political priority in the european integration process. the report calls for a fairer single market, stressing that a genuine single market should provide benefits and protection for citizens, consumers and businesses, in terms of better quality, greater variety, reasonable prices and safety of goods and services. as regards smes and start-ups, it is important that their capacity for innovation is supported in every way possible, as they are the backbone of the european economy. the strategy adopted is expected to help europe grow economically.
in writing. – the single market strategy is the commission’s global roadmap to unleash the full potential of the single market with the objective of creating a modern, more innovative, deeper and fairer single market. its focus lies in particular on aspects aimed at helping businesses (especially smes, micro-enterprises and start-ups) to scale up their activities, grow and stay in the single market. i support this initiative and report especially in creating call for a simplified vat approach in the e-commerce sector; a call for facilitating smes access to eu funds.
mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate my colleague, mr cristian preda, on his excellent report. as we adopt the 2030 sustainable development goals, as we prepare to revise the cotonou agreement and as the european union faces an unprecedented migration crisis, it is more crucial than ever to redouble our efforts to ensure that policy coherence for development becomes a real mode of action and delivers results beyond the concept stage. i would like to emphasize four elements. first, policy coherence for development must contribute to the establishment of the rule of law, democracy and good governance in developing countries, in order to serve the objective and the ambition of sustainable outcomes. without stable democratic states, development aid is poured over plants that have no roots and are therefore unable to bear fruit. secondly, i would like to stress the key role of national parliaments and the european parliament on the one hand and of the union delegations on the other in ensuring not only horizontal but also vertical coherence of policies. this role needs to be strengthened, particularly in the formulation of policies by parliaments and implementation by delegations. thirdly, ownership is a key issue. in reality, the cdp is about ensuring that in the medium term, each directorate-general, each ministry, each region, each embassy or delegation embraces the objectives of european development policy. efforts must be continued in this direction. fourthly and lastly, i support the rapporteur's idea of a european summit on policy coherence for development. this should allow for concrete recommendations and a renewed commitment to the dpc as a genuine modus vivendi and operandi in all the external dimensions of the union's action. in conclusion, mr president, let us not forget that policy coherence for development is essential to safeguard the union's capacity for action, credibility and budgetary effectiveness. in this sense, i believe that the momentum that was initiated in 2015 through the european year for development to better integrate european citizens into this policy and these debates must continue to be maintained.
last week, the lower house of the german parliament adopted a declaration condemning a grave act of violence, a grave crime against humanity, namely the armenian genocide committed by the young turk government in 1915. and it is the restoration of this historical justice that is provoking an inexplicable reaction from the turkish president and the turkish prime minister. a reaction which shows a complete disconnect between all the so-called european values and the policy which is currently being pursued in turkey and which covers up the crimes committed at that time by the young turk government, whose successor is now claimed to be the turkish prime minister and president. this is the kind of behaviour that shows a deeply flawed policy on the part of the so-called current leaders of the european union, who are making too many concessions to an undemocratic authoritarian government such as the one in ankara.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the eradication of illicit trade in tobacco products: protocol to the world health organisation framework convention, as ratification of the protocol by the european union and its member states will accelerate its entry into force. so far, only nine countries have joined the treaty, while 40 are needed to bring it into force. and if the eu ratifies the protocol, that will add another 29 countries to it. the protocol will benefit public health and strengthen the international fight against illicit trade in tobacco, tax evasion and organised crime.
in writing. ‒ i support the resolution on endocrine disruptors. i believe it is extremely important and necessary for the european commission to publish the scientific criteria necessary to identify and reduce exposure to substances that lead to hormonal disorders, as they lead to serious adverse outcomes. even the un environment programme/who report has classified endocrine disruptors as a global threat. of concern is the growing prevalence of endocrine disorders in humans. there is new evidence that edcs can have a serious negative impact on reproductive health (cancer, infertility) as well as on thyroid function, brain function, obesity and metabolism, and on insulin and glucose homeostasis. i welcome the decision of the european commission to publish the criteria by the end of june 2016.
in writing. – eliminating the illicit tobacco trade in the eu is a crucial issue for several reasons. it harms public health policies and threatens a legitimate business which causes losses to all tobacco traders within the eu. the illicit trade of tobacco funds organised crime as taxation for such products is high and therefore generates high profits to the smugglers. the eu and member states lose roughly eur 10 billion in lost tax and customs revenue each year making this a serious problem that has to be dealt with. therefore, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the automotive sector employs over 10 million people and probably many more. in my country, more and more manufacturing jobs are being created in the automotive sector, which is something i can only be happy about. given that this sector is one of the largest value-added generators and that manufacturing also constitutes a major part of the budgets of the member states as well as of the eu, we are obliged to maintain and strengthen competitiveness in this sector and to maintain our global leadership in this sector.
in writing. – the cars 2020 action plan suggests that more internationally harmonised vehicle regulations should be implemented, compared to the 1958 agreement so that non-tariff barriers are removed. the automotive industry is an economic sector of great significance to european gdp, accounting for more than 12 million jobs thought the eu. i voted in favour of the revision of the 1958 agreement, so that the european union and its parties could achieve the necessary amendments.
in writing. there is nothing more natural than, once a country has joined the eu, to join the trade agreements that the union signed before its accession. in that spirit, i support this recommendation and the signing of the additional protocol.
in writing. ‒ the eu-columbia-peru agreement has been provisionally applied with peru since 1 march 2013 and with colombia since 1 august 2013. the agreement liberalises trade in agricultural and industrial products as well as in services. it also contains provisions on the origin of goods, technical barriers to trade, sanitary measures, competition, intellectual property and public procurement. looking from this perspective, it could be argued that it opens up markets for eu, colombian and peruvian exporters, eventually bringing annual savings of more than eur 500 million. however, in order to take into account croatia’s accession to the eu on 1 july 2013, the parties had to agree on the additional protocol to the eu-colombia/peru trade agreement. in 2015, colombia and peru signed the additional protocol to the trade agreement. in light of this, we should work to ensure that respective internal ratification procedures are completed by the commission and the council in order to enable croatia to benefit fully from the wide network of trade agreements the eu has with third countries. in addition, we should work together with peru and colombia to extend free trade agreements to other members of the andean community (ecuador and bolivia) this is an important step for enhancing trade between the two geopolitical regions (europe and andean).
in writing. – as officially an eu member state it is only normal that croatia undergoes the legal steps to enable its participation and open its market to the trade agreement. this accession will highly benefit both the country of croatia, colombia and peru and will show development in the relationships between the parties of the agreement. hence, i vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the decision to use enhanced cooperation in the area of jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of judgments on the property regime of international couples covers both the property regime between spouses and the property consequences of registered partnerships, and is merely a procedural decision. the main problem here is that the decision to allow enhanced cooperation for the first time requires member states to join both instruments (of partnerships and of marriages) simultaneously. however, a number of member states are not familiar with the institution of 'partnerships' (cyprus, bulgaria, romania, slovakia, poland, lithuania, latvia), bulgaria being one of these countries, but they will have to adopt the two regulations on the implementation of enhanced cooperation if they want to adopt the regulation on matrimonial property regimes applicable in the member state concerned. in addition, they will have to recognise the effects of the institution of the 'partnership', which is not recognised by their domestic law and may be considered to be contrary to their public policies, in particular in the field of private international law, as well as to their domestic law, in accordance with the fundamental principles of the member state's legal system. for these many reasons and the lack of clarity as to why these two proposals go hand in hand, i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. – bulgaria is one of the 17 member states that addressed a request to the commission to propose a decision authorising the establishment of enhanced cooperation between themselves in the field of property regimes of international couples. the proposal brings more clarity for international couples managing their property and i fully support it.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the eu's accession to the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products to the who framework convention on tobacco control. this report deals specifically with the provisions on obligations relating to judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the definition of offences itself. the protocol will benefit public health and strengthen the international fight against illicit trade in tobacco, tax evasion and organised crime. to this end, the measures proposed by the protocol and implemented by the governments of the states will target the chain of production and distribution of tobacco products. the protocol requires the establishment of a dedicated global supply tracking system within five years of the entry into force of the protocol, with the secretariat of the who framework convention on tobacco control as the centre and main administrator of this information exchange system.
in writing. ‒ i supported the legislative resolution on the conclusion of the protocol on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products to the framework convention on tobacco control of the world health organisation. illicit trade in tobacco products damages both the eu budget and that of the member states in the form of unpaid taxes and duties. curbing the illicit trade in tobacco products, which are largely of unclear composition, produced outside the eu and in contravention of tobacco control policies, will help to regulate the distribution of tobacco products within the european market. this will ensure a higher level of protection of the public health of european citizens and at the same time help to combat tax and customs evasion. i believe that the envisaged international cooperation based on specific legislative procedures and the establishment of a global monitoring and tracing regime will enable countries to control tobacco products produced and imported into their territory. this will limit illegal imports and create a precondition for preventing tax fraud and organised crime.
in writing. ‒ eliminating illicit tobacco trade should be a top priority because it is related not only to tax avoidance but also to the health of eu citizens. so far the fight against illicit tobacco trade has been conducted on the basis of the 12-year anti-illicit trade agreement between the european commission, member states and philip morris international (pmi). our shared efforts have delivered an 85% reduction in counterfeit cigarettes. unfortunately, the agreement ends at the end of this year and the reduction in the flow of counterfeit cigarettes has been replaced by a huge increase in so-called illicit-whites – branded cigarettes manufactured outside the eu for the sole purpose of smuggling. nowadays tobacco smuggling represents the foundation of illicit trade of tobacco products in europe and in order to address these issues we should immediately ratify the world health organisation protocol on the illicit trade in tobacco. the protocol aims to tackle tobacco smuggling in particular by encouraging and enhancing international cooperation, valid information sharing, technical and law enforcement cooperation, mutual legal and administrative assistance. some 16 countries have ratified the who protocol, including five eu member states; it is time for the eu to join the international fight against illicit tobacco trade and to make tobacco industry fully transparent.
in writing. ‒ approximately one in ten cigarettes are sold illegally in eu member states. the european parliament has approved by a large majority the protocol on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products to the world health organisation's framework convention on tobacco control. the protocol is one of the main global initiatives in this field and aims to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. it provides new tools to combat cigarette smuggling, aiming at establishing a global tracking and tracing system. the majority of illicit tobacco products in the eu come from third countries. therefore, effective action to tackle this cross-border problem requires global and coordinated action. i believe that bulgaria, like the eu, has an obligation to fight against the smuggling of tobacco products, which leads to tax evasion and increases the health risk caused by the lack of control. that is why ratification of the protocol is a step in the right direction.

in writing. ‒ the eu's programme on policy coherence for development is of paramount importance because it will enable the institutions to achieve better coordination and greater effectiveness of their programmes and policies in developing countries. it is essential that this programme be integrated into all policies related to the achievement of the un millennium declaration as embodied in the un 2030 agenda for sustainable development, because the main problem at international level is the lack of coordination and inconsistency in development policies. despite the importance of this, i decided to vote 'abstention' on the report on policy coherence for development, as i fear that the implementation of the new programme will increase regulatory measures and impose new burdens on our citizens and businesses.

in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn) aims to leverage private investment in agriculture in order to improve food security and nutrition by helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa by 2020. the eu and member states have a key role to play in transforming nafsn into a genuine instrument of support for family farming and local economics in sub-saharan africa. investment in family farming aims before all to boost domestic food production in order to build self—sufficiency, which consequently will decrease the level of food imports /humanitarian aid dependency. i supported the resolution because the eu and member states should support agriculture in sub-saharan africa through national development funds which grant subsidies and loans to family farms. in order to facilitate the process even further, the union should provide education and training to family farmers. last but not least, the eu should work to promote the formation of farmers’ organisations that help farmers possess on the market their production in a way that safeguards the profitability of their production. fighting hunger is a priority enshrined in the first millennium development goal. the eu should continue to contribute significantly to this goal.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the assessment of international accounting standards because it included greater accountability for three organisations that are partly funded by the eu - the international financial reporting standards foundation (ifrs), the european financial reporting advisory group (efrag) and the public interest reporting and disclosure oversight board. it also addresses some general issues regarding the approval process of ifrs financial reporting standards in european law. the committee's position is that the application of ifrss cannot delay or lead to a shift or distortion of competition between market participants. i agree that the approval process of ifrss should be in line with the criteria set out in the international accounting standards regulation.
in writing. – international financial standards are a key component for the effective functioning of the internal market as well as the capital markets. in order for them to continue to do so, parliament, the commission and the council should develop standards for reporting and endorsing the processes. such a development will result in much better results of the appropriateness of the accounting and reporting principles. i voted in favour of the report and support the international accounting standards evaluation.
in writing. ‒ the report on peacekeeping operations the european union's commitment to the un and the african union looks at the eu's participation and contribution to peacekeeping operations in conflict zones and failed states. i decided to support this report because i share the rapporteur's view that the european union should contribute where its contribution will provide the greatest added value, such as by providing training, equipment and logistical support. it is vital that the eu continues to cooperate with its international partners to ensure long-term stability, security and peace in conflict zones, but in no case should this be done by extending the remit of the european external action service to areas such as security and defence or by creating a joint european military contingent. any increase in the powers of the european institutions in such areas would take away from the sovereignty of the member states and i would vote strongly against it.
in writing. – nowadays the political situation and security landscape in africa are very unstable and fragile. sadly, africa has the highest number of inter—state and intra—state conflicts in the world. in the last decade, the number of failed states and ungoverned spaces on the continent has increased, leaving many people affected by poverty, lawlessness, corruption and violence. importantly, disappearing borders within the continent reduce security (statehood), provide opportunities for criminal activity particularly smuggling, fuel violence, help emergence of terrorist and insurgent groups such as al-shabaab and boko haram. it could be argued that insecurity and instability in africa directly affect europe in terms of migrant crisis, smuggling and terrorism, etc. in order to prevent this negative trend, the eu should increase its contribution to peace support operations in africa and expand its collaboration with the un and the african union in a more active manner. in particular, the eu should focus its efforts to enhance conflict prevention and to promote capacity building in support of security and development. expressed in other words, to guarantee the protection of people and to stimulate the stabilisation process, the eu should rely on a holistic approach to peacekeeping operations. a stable and secure africa means a stable and secure europe.

unfair trading practices are a stifling factor for producers and processors. in europe, 99.1% of enterprises in the food and drink sector are small and medium-sized. unfair trading practices such as price-cutting, delayed payment and unconditional return of unsold goods are destroying a sector that is losing its attractiveness in part because of these practices. these practices create imbalances and threaten not only people with fragile livelihoods but also the functioning of the single market as a whole, because they would create conditions for price undercutting, which is a prerequisite for malformations and closures of local businesses. by pressuring producers, these practices also deprive consumers of the right to make an informed choice about whether producers are paid a fair wage for their production. measures must be proposed at national level to guarantee a fair income for producers, because they are essential to maintaining food security in the european union. i therefore strongly believe that the european union should propose binding measures to protect loyal traders and to stop or minimise unfair practices.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, as it focuses on the range of unfair trading practices that are spreading across the european union, while also highlighting good practices in the member states to improve the fight against these practices through legislation or other initiatives. a large number of countries have already taken measures that contribute to combating unfair practices. however, the so-called 'fear factor' still exists, which prevents many traders from taking legal action for fear of damaging their trading relationships with partners.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i support the report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, as free and fair competition, balanced relations between all market participants and strengthened and effective enforcement of sectoral legislation at european level are key to the proper functioning of the food supply chain. unfair trading practices have a negative impact in particular on small and medium-sized enterprises, as they reduce their ability to invest in innovation and to seek ways to expand their business. following the recent commission assessment report, a large number of countries have recognised the damage caused by unfair trading practices and have taken regulatory measures to address it. but there is still room for improvement. the report makes clear recommendations to member states to improve national legislation so that laws can be applied in practice in an adequate and effective manner. taking into account national specificities and characteristics, i welcome the measures taken by the commission to combat unfair trading practices. these measures are aimed at ensuring a more balanced market and overcoming the current fragmentation within the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, as i believe it is important to ensure that european competition law takes account of the specificities of agriculture, ensures the well-being of producers and consumers, creates the conditions for a more efficient market that allows consumers to benefit from a wide choice of quality products at competitive prices, while ensuring that primary producers are incentivised to invest and innovate without being displaced by unfair trading practices. a solution must be found to stop the abuses of dominant traders, even if it does not always meet the legal definition of abuses, namely unilateral change of backdated contracts, flat-rate charges imposed by suppliers of the 'pay to stay' type, late payments of more than 60 days, arbitrary discounts that the big chains charge themselves in case of early or timely payment, forcing suppliers to use explicitly named third-party companies to produce packaging, labels, etc. independent national regulatory authorities in the food sector should provide effective mechanisms to combat such unfair trading practices.
in writing. – unfair trade practices are practices that grossly deviate from good commercial conduct. utps in the food supply chain is a major problem, particularly for farmers, producers and smes. i firmly believe in the need for free and fair competition and, therefore, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain to overcome the existing imbalances and inequalities in the relationship between producer-supplier-large trading chains, where farmers are put at a disadvantage compared to the much stronger trading operators. the resolution is in line with the agri committee's efforts to protect the position of farmers who are most vulnerable when negotiating trade terms with the rest of the food supply chain. not only can they not expect to earn a fair return, but they are forced to sell below cost and, in order not to lose their customers, very often do not file complaints. it is clear that the existing competition and fair trade legislation is not sufficient to tackle the vicious practices in food supply chains. i therefore welcome the proposal to establish a framework for pan-european legislation to tackle unfair trading practices. such legislation is becoming increasingly necessary in the context of the deepening crisis in various sectors of agriculture - milk and milk products, pigmeat, fruit and vegetables. the common agricultural policy supports the creation of producer organisations which can contribute to strengthening the position of farmers through the possibility of concluding collective supply contracts.
i did not support this report because i believe that the legal vacuum we are in, pending a legislative proposal from the european commission on genetically modified organisms and an improved regulation on their placing and production in the european union, creates preconditions for ambiguity and sending wrong signals to citizens. i think that this report unfortunately does that. i also disagree with the call for the commission to use its new scientific opinion mechanism to place greater emphasis on risk-based risks and benefits in relation to the adoption or non-adoption of new technologies, products and practices. agriculture is the sector that provides all of us with food. innovation in this field must be carried out in the spirit of measures which protect and improve human, animal and plant health and the environment. the risk-based approach model hinted at in this report is not applicable to the proven european legislative framework and i believe this is the union's strong advantage in maintaining a sustainable feed production model and maintaining standards that are beneficial for citizens and the environment.
in writing. the world population is constantly increasing. in contrast, less and less land is used for agriculture, and at the same time there is a trend towards an ageing population and fewer people working the land. that is why we need to make it easier for innovation in this sector to reach farmers, no matter how big or small they are. and conversely, farmers need to have quick and secure access to research centres. at the same time, we have to be very careful with so-called gmo foods, because yes, they provide a quick solution to the problem, but that solution comes at a cost to human health. i supported this report and hope that by doing so i can help to develop agriculture in europe.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the eu. it is extremely important not only to meet the growing demand but also to control the many negative factors that affect the agricultural sector. environmental change, crop yield losses, soil quality and yields are among the main challenges that could be addressed by integrating technologies. they need to be applied to every type of agriculture to make it more productive and sustainable. in the meantime, a key priority should be to continue the practice of precision farming, which demonstrates how technological intervention reduces resources used and increases yields. long-term planning and financing of this sector is essential to achieve lasting improvements in the sustainability of agriculture, reductions in production costs and improvements in competitiveness.
in writing. – the european union is becoming a world leader in agricultural technology, innovation and sustainability. in order for the eu to meet the rising food demand various initiatives would have to be accomplished by 2050. healthy food and optimal nutrition in the production still remain among the biggest challenges for the eu as well as for the rest of the world. actions need to be undertaken within a short period to ensure that needs of land availability, water shortage and the increasing energy demand will be met by 2050. in my work and activities as a member of the european parliament, among other initiatives, i fully support that technological solutions and innovation, which are our best chance to meet the upcoming demands.
i supported this report because i believe that sustainable use of available resources in agriculture is the key to moving in the right direction. i would like to highlight the role of marine and ocean natural resources, such as sapropyl, which have a huge potential to improve soil health and composition and hence agriculture. the black sea basin is rich in this sediment, which can be used to create biological soil improvers and fertilizers. they, in turn, create the conditions for the expansion of certain agricultural sectors, such as organic farming, and have a highly beneficial role in maintaining soil health and quality. i am calling on the bulgarian administration to establish a public-private partnership to support the extraction of this sediment from bulgaria's black sea economic zone. the sapropel is a response to the growing need for innovative soil improvers and its extraction is an investment in better agriculture, in the development of industry and in the involvement of scientific institutions in real economic processes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on promoting innovation and economic development in the future management of european farms. the food and agriculture organization of the united nations (fao) estimates that the expected increase in the world's population to 9.1 billion by 2050 will require a 60% increase in food production by that date and a 24% increase in crop yields in developed countries. that means we need to make farms more modern and innovative so that we can increase production, but also make it more environmentally friendly. the report also stresses that farmers should be given more freedom in the choice of innovation and in its implementation. i think that's right, because the manufacturer is the best person to judge the benefits of using a technology.
in writing. – it is of paramount importance to sustain agricultural production in order to improve the economic prospects of producers. i am convinced that economic development and sustainable production go hand in hand. the new innovations and research play an essential role in fulfilling both the objectives. hence, i vote in favour of the better economic development of disadvantaged regions such as mountainous and outermost regions as well as small and medium-sized farms, as this is crucial for the better implementation of a stable, sustainable future.
madam president, many of us in this house have long called for the genuine integration of migration into the union's external policies and for genuine migration diplomacy. it is now a matter of conceptual design. the challenge now is to make this fundamental change in our approach a reality. i would like to emphasize three elements in this connection. first, there is a need for a thorough reflection on the financing. on the one hand, the good practices already in place in the selected and so-called priority countries deserve to be better valued; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. we need to reduce the number of priorities to have a greater impact. secondly, yes, africa is a key continent. in the area of migration management, support for border controls between african countries and for intra-african migration management should be strengthened. as regards the causes of migration, it is imperative to achieve results in development cooperation. this requires a real effort and we are doing it: finding an approach and incentives that work and not neglecting other tools, economic and commercial, as levers of reforms related to the rule of law and human rights. a general remark: beware of the message that will be sent to all the other countries that are not priorities at the moment. and a particular question: what role for african regional organizations? finally, two questions on the implementation of the action plan adopted in valletta: what measures have been proposed to exploit the human and financial potential of the african diaspora in europe? what about cooperation between the countries of sub-saharan africa, the countries of the southern mediterranean and the european countries?
the unprecedented migration crisis of the past few years has clearly shown that no country can cope alone and therefore both coordinated pan-european action and close cooperation with third countries are needed. so i think that the european union needs to take three concrete measures to reduce the migratory pressure on europe. first, we have to distinguish between economic migrants and refugees. those seeking a better life can take advantage of legal ways of entering the european territory, but no legislation allows them to enter the european union illegally by trying to cross borders unregulated. we must dispel the hope that europe will give them the same support as it has given refugees fleeing war. the european union must also step up the return of illegal immigrants to their countries of origin. i therefore welcome the enhanced role of the european border and coast guard in this regard. but for the new service to work effectively, the european union needs to sign readmission agreements with countries of origin quickly. finally, i believe that the possibility of creating hotspots outside europe should be reconsidered. i believe that this measure will reduce the migratory pressure towards europe, because only those who are entitled to international protection will be able to reach the member states following the approval of their application under european law. addressing the migration crisis requires new measures and approaches by the european union, and enhancing international cooperation is an important component of the union's action package in this regard.
the european commission's proposals and policies in relation to the illegal migrant crisis can be described as a stunning failure. the failure was the thesis that all illegal immigrants can be invited and accepted on the european continent because they claimed to be refugees, when in fact a large number of them are illegal immigrants. the failure was the idea that you could allocate these people, first temporarily, then permanently, because you didn't allocate anyone with those allocations. the deal with the dictator erdogan, besides being a failure, was also a grave hypocrisy, because you are making a deal with a dictator in the name of human rights, who daily violates human rights and who daily crushes the principles of liberal democracy. the promise to pay billions of euros from the pocket of the european taxpayer as a ransom for this man has also failed. this proposal will fail, and now i have another proposal for colleagues who defend the thesis that they can accept all illegal immigrants. give an example, take a family home and show us how it's done.
in writing. the european commission has identified migration pressure as the 'new normal' and presented a new partnership plan with third countries. i welcome the efforts to build a long-term strategy to deal with the problem, because the evidence is clear that there is no prospect of the migratory pressure on europe stopping or easing in the coming years. this plan recognises that this will be the main problem of the eu and the next generation of european citizens. this is the problem, and perhaps the only one, that we cannot solve by achieving a better standard of living and economic growth in europe. the better the conditions here, the more people will want to come to us. more than half of the immigrants in europe do not come from conflict zones. in the years to come, the eu will be a haven for climate refugees, who we don't talk about much yet. we must therefore promote better living conditions in african countries and support their economic and social development. this investment is necessary to safeguard our european standards, rights and freedoms. i welcome the package of specific agreements, arrangements and measures and hope that the launch of this long-term strategy will be welcomed and supported by all european governments.

in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the european commission estimates that some 70 million europeans do not have sufficient literacy and numeracy skills, and almost half (45%) of the eu population does not have sufficient digital skills. this is more than a state of emergency for the beginning of the 21st century. despite the huge unemployment in europe, more than 40% of employers say they cannot find workers with the necessary knowledge and skills to grow their business. let us add that a huge number of young people with a university education cannot find a job or work in places that are far from their education. so, something is wrong with the education system and it needs to be changed immediately and seriously. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal for a new skills agenda for europe. a comprehensive approach and the use of all effective tools are needed to address the skills gaps in the labour market that are currently known to exist. young people should be the focus of the programme for understandable reasons, but this alone will not solve the problem of the mismatch between the requirements and the real skills of the workers who are now in the army of the unemployed. let us invest in all of europe's human resources, in training the skills needed today and tomorrow.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, honourable members, i am here today to reply to your oral question on the very important topic of european union administration. you ask, in particular, if the commission has analysed your suggestion for a regulation for an open, efficient and independent european union administration, and whether the commission has any plans to put forward its own proposal. you ask for the reasons that have prevented the commission, thus far, from acting on its right of initiative in this field. let me assure you from the start that the commission is extremely serious about its commitment to guaranteeing that citizens can interact with a european administration that is open, independent and efficient. that is why the commission has, for instance, set up the transparency portal. this portal provides citizens with direct access to information and will help them to be better informed and better prepared to follow and participate in the eu decision-making process. i also want to mention the commission inter-service group on public administration quality and innovation. this group is working to enable, among others, national administrations, and therefore european businesses, fully to tap the potential of the internal market, joint economic governance and the structural funds. apart from these more recent initiatives, and as you know, the commission has a well-established set of horizontal rules which govern its administrative behaviour – as, i would expect, does parliament. this includes the general provisions of the code of good administrative behaviour, as well as a range of provisions on staff and financial regulations, on data protection and access to documents, to name but a few of the areas covered. all of these horizontal rules are a reflection of the existing legal principles of good administration, such as non-discrimination, impartiality and fairness, and the right to have one’s affairs handled within a reasonable time, etcetera. as the eu administers a range of diverse and mostly highly specialised activities, it also relies on sector-specific rules. citizens and businesses concerned by such specialised activities are guaranteed specific administrative rights. examples here are numerous: we have specific rights in competition law, and in relation to novel foods, the authorisation of medicinal products, gmos, trade defence, etcetera. the commission has analysed your suggestion for a regulation for an open, efficient and independent european union administration against these existing horizontal and sectoral rules, principles and practices. as a result of that analysis, the commission is, at this stage, not convinced that the benefits of using a legislative instrument that would codify administrative law would outweigh the costs. codification is a complex and delicate exercise that can often have unintended consequences. in having to clarify the relationship and to ensure consistency with these more detailed rules, codification would require the revision of the considerable volume of existing eu legislation. even where done with care and a sense of proportion, codification may still lead to problems of delimitation between the general and specific rules – not making legislation any clearer or litigation any easier for citizens and businesses affected. codification would remove the flexibility required to adapt to particular needs. these challenges and difficulties are also confirmed by the draft regulation. the text does not identify what the gaps and inconsistencies in current law are, and therefore what the justification is for coming forward with horizontal legislative solutions as a proportionate answer to deal with them. it also does not assess the concrete impact of the provisions it contains. while the text is said to be without prejudice to existing rules and rights under specific union legislation, it provides for no legal mechanism to ensure delimitation between the general and the specific rules. it rather seems to suggest that a case-by-case analysis would continue to apply. lastly, there is the matter of ways to identify administrative activities of the institutions and bodies that would be subject to the new rules. instead of engaging in a highly complex exercise of codification, with uncertain value-added, the commission is of the opinion that we should continue to address concrete problems where they arise, analyse the root causes and then take the sort of action that is needed. the commission analyses each case of alleged maladministration, and will try to rectify any error that has been made. it also engages constructively in the context of all inquiries by the european ombudsman. that being said, at this stage the commission is not aware of any pattern of cases of maladministration that could be addressed through a general administrative law. i am, as is the commission, therefore grateful for the work you have done, and will continue working with you on all options and good arguments as to how we can improve our citizens’ life.
on behalf of the ppe group. i would like to congratulate mrs hautala and the legal service of the european parliament, who have put so much effort into the preparation of this important document for the european administration. the european parliament has repeatedly called for the adoption of a regulation on the administrative procedure of the union. so far, the european commission has remained deaf to our appeals. let's hope this time he makes the effort to make that proposal a reality. the treaties and the charter of fundamental rights provide for the right to good administration. but for citizens to exercise this right, they need clear, effective, predictable and accessible procedures in their dealings with the european administration. the benefits of such legislation are undeniable: on the one hand it will fill the gaps in the union's legal system and increase legal certainty by giving citizens and legal persons clearer rights, and on the other hand it will help to establish trust in the work of the european administration, thus strengthening the union's legitimacy. with our proposal we are answering important questions such as the opening of administrative proceedings, time limits and remedies. i believe that an important element of the proposal is the reaffirmation of the fundamental procedural rights which aim to make the european administration an open, efficient and independent administration. the protection of fundamental rights, such as the right to be heard, the right of every person to have access to documents concerning him or her, the requirement to provide the necessary information to the parties, are only some of the legal remedies available to citizens.
on behalf of the ecr group. for us in the european conservatives and reformists group, the issue of an open, efficient, independent administration of the european union is essential, both for european citizens and for the proper functioning of the european union institutions. despite several initiatives by parliament and the texts of the treaties calling for an open, efficient and independent european administration, the european commission has not yet made a proposal for a regulation on the subject. a common european administrative law relating to institutions, bodies, agencies and services would apply to the institutions of the european union and should cover aspects ranging from conflict of interest to simple and intelligibly drafted administrative acts. this would not only serve european citizens but also the institutions themselves and make them more accessible and understandable to the citizens of the member states. i am curious to see what proposal the european commission would put forward and what place parliament's views on the subject would have in it.

in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the requirements for the presentation of official documents in the european union. i find the proposal made by the european commission to be extremely effective in terms of reducing the administrative costs of citizens, facilitating the processes of legalisation and certification of cross-border documents. the recognition of certificates supports one of the fundamental rights of european citizens - the free movement of people across borders. i believe that all the administrative obstacles to the mobility of europeans can be avoided by building a single european framework, which includes clearly defined practical tools of the internal market information system and multilingual standard certificates. strategically, the positive outcome can be expected to be an increase in the professional skills and competitiveness of european citizens, taking into account the existing single european qualifications framework, and a significant easing of the procedures for training abroad.
in writing. ‒ on 9 june, we adopted by a large majority in parliament a relaxed set of rules on the free movement of european citizens by simplifying the requirements for certain official documents. following these rules, administrative formalities such as 'legalization' and 'posting' of documents such as birth certificate, marriage certificate, death certificate, criminal record certificate, etc. will be abolished. new multilingual versions will be developed to avoid the need to translate official documents. the rules will be fully applicable from 2019. unfortunately, at this stage, such a text has not yet been adopted for documents relating to the legal status of enterprises, diplomas and documents proving disability. this could become a reality in two years' time when the scope of the regulation is reviewed. i believe that citizens should have as few administrative obstacles as possible to their movement within the eu.

member of the commission. – mr president, let me start by expressing my thanks to ms metsola and, through you, to the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) for having given us the opportunity of this debate to reflect about how the european institutions, and particularly the commission, can better inform the european parliament about negotiations for international agreements. as you know, in the context of the new inter-institutional agreement for better law-making, parliament, the commission and the council have made a commitment to meet within six months of the entry into force of the inter-institutional agreement, in order to negotiate improved practical arrangements for cooperation and information sharing. this trilateral approach reflects the fact that the obligation to inform parliament fully and immediately falls on both the commission and the council, in accordance with their institutional roles. for example, it does not fall on the commission to inform parliament about decisions taken or texts adopted by council. but let me reiterate the importance that we, in the commission, attach to our obligations under the treaty and to our existing commitment under the framework agreement: we are committed to providing parliament with full and immediate information at all stages of negotiations for international agreements. the commission stands by this commitment and monitors its implementation closely. the framework agreement established the practice that information concerning international agreements should, as a general rule, be provided to parliament through the responsible parliamentary committee. in line with this sector-specific approach, the commission has instructed its services to arrange directly with the relevant parliamentary committees the modalities for the provision of information and documents, to allow for optimal solutions in this area. the commission believes that our obligations are, generally speaking, well respected and that commissioners and their services are doing their part to ensure that parliament is well informed. this includes the provision of confidential information and documents and the specific arrangements set out in the framework agreement. as regards specifically the work of the civil liberties committee, commission services have established a practice of providing regular updates to the committee on pending international agreement. commission representatives have always been willing to come and give an update on ongoing international negotiations, either in camera or in a public meeting, as appropriate. likewise, practical arrangements for informing parliament about re-admission agreements have so far included regular presentations by senior commission officials to the civil liberties committee in ordinary meetings. the commission is ready to provide such information whenever requested, be it in public or, when appropriate, in a restricted meeting. the commission is also open to discussing with parliament whether and how practice can be improved. i am looking forward to hearing your concrete proposals, which will fit into the trilateral approach that parliament, the council and the commission, are to start soon.

ppe), in written form. ladies and gentlemen, there are about 16 million international couples in europe who are married or living in a registered partnership, and at least 650 000 of them end their marriage or partnership each year. decisions on matters relating to the matrimonial property regime and the property consequences of registered partnerships are therefore of paramount importance to european citizens. at present, it is very difficult for international couples to understand which courts have jurisdiction and which law applies to their personal situation and property. the rules vary considerably from country to country and sometimes lead to conflict situations. international couples affected by a division of common property face complex issues, in particular as regards the applicable law, the choice of court, and the recognition and enforcement of judgments. the adoption of this regulation will avoid legal differences between the 18 member states participating in enhanced cooperation. this will help european citizens avoid legal uncertainty and the associated costs when dividing their property in the event of divorce, separation or death. the decision by the member states to enter into this enhanced cooperation is particularly timely and i am pleased that it contains much of the 2013 ep recommendations, especially as regards regulatory security and clarity.

in writing. ‒ as you know, the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to provide support for workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or as a result of a continuation of the global financial and economic crisis. in this regard, the main aim of the fund is to help people who lost their jobs to reintegrate into the labour market. i supported the resolution because we should mobilise the fund to support belgium’s submitted application egf/2015/012 be/hainaut machinery for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in the economic sector classified under the nace revision 2 division 28 (manufacture of machinery and equipment n.e.c.) in the region of hainaut (be32). in this case, 488 redundant workers, as well as 300 young people from the hainaut region are not in employment, education or training and the egf is expected to support them and give them new opportunities to reintegrate into the labour market. another reason why we should support the mobilisation of the fund is that belgian authorities have implemented all necessary measures to activate and receive the egf fund.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to provide support for workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, as a result of the continuation of the global financial and economic crisis or as a result of a new global financial and economic crisis, and to assist their reintegration into the labour market. the report notes that following the announcement by caterpillar belgium s.a. on 23 february 2013 of the opening of a collective redundancy procedure at its production site in gosli, most of its 1399 workers were the subject of an egf/2014/011 be/caterpillar application, and underlines that the eno region faces a difficult labour market situation with an unemployment rate of 14,5% (5,9% above the national average), 1236 jobs closed in 2013 and 1878 in 2014, as well as a high level of long-term unemployment. the report argues that the egf should not replace measures which are an obligation for undertakings under national law.

in writing. i supported this report because of the important message it conveys, recognising human trafficking as a serious transnational crime. the report recognises the importance of a coherent approach to the internal and external dimension of eu policies to combat trafficking in human beings. i support the fact that it distinguishes between the concepts of trafficking in human beings and smuggling of migrants, as the two concepts require different legal and political responses. i believe it is of the utmost importance to pay particular attention to the fight against trafficking in human beings in the eu's political dialogue with third countries, as well as through cooperation programmes and in multilateral and regional fora. i have always stressed the need for coherence between internal and external policies, which implies the development of partnerships with third countries in the field of combating trafficking in human beings, in line with the union's fundamental values. i welcome the fact that the report recognises and supports the work of the eu coordinator for combating trafficking in human beings and calls for joint action between the eu, member states, third countries and international actors to establish more coherent and effective cooperation to establish systems to identify, protect and assist victims of trafficking.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on combating trafficking in human beings in the eu's external relations. trafficking in human beings is one of the most serious forms of human rights violations. this serious crime must be addressed in a holistic manner, with an emphasis not only on sexual exploitation but also on forced labour, organ trafficking, forced begging, forced marriage, child soldiers and trafficking of babies. the eu must direct its foreign policy instruments to break this lucrative and immoral model and increase protection for victims of crime. according to the united nations office on drugs and crime, 70% of the victims are women and girls, mostly from eastern europe, 53% of trafficking is for sexual exploitation and 40% of trafficking is for forced labour. i believe that financial investigations, which track, seize and confiscate property derived from criminal activity, and anti-money laundering actions play a crucial role in the fight against this crime.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on the fight against trafficking in human beings in the european union's external relations. worldwide, some 36 million people are trapped in modern forms of slavery. it is also a fact that 10,000 children have disappeared without a trace in europe since the start of the refugee crisis, allegedly as victims of traffickers. in the light of these data, the eu has no choice but to take the lead by committing to measures that directly attack the traffic networks and their root causes. this is a global problem and the eu must therefore increase its financial and technical assistance and improve europol's effectiveness.
in writing. – the european union is faced with one of the greatest challenges in its history in the face of the refugee crisis. from the refugees who are illegally smuggled in europe by criminal organisations, through the men that work years without payment to the women forced into prostitution, these activities devaluate all basic human rights and permanently damage victims and their families. the coordination between member states on all aspects of human trafficking should be enhanced. i voted in favour of the report of ms lochbihler on ‘modern day slavery’, which aims to fight money laundering in the eu and hold accountable eu companies that tolerate forced labour in their factories of supply chains.
vice-president of the commission. – madam president, i would like to offer my most sincere thanks to the rapporteurs for the excellent work they have done. we look forward to engaging further so we can reflect as we prepare to submit our proposal for the midterm revision in the coming months. we have an obligation to complete this work by the end of the year and we will do all we can on our side to meet that obligation. it is an opportunity to examine the implementation of the multiannual financial framework (mff) and, as the rapporteurs have said, this is not a usual period in the history of the european union. since 2008 we have gone from one crisis to another. we have had a financial crisis, an economic crisis in the eurozone, hitting greece the hardest, the migration crisis, terrorism and now, very recently, we have experienced the earthquake of the referendum in the united kingdom. in this context, what we have in our hands is, for the first time in the history of the european union, a smaller budget than the one we had before. needs have gone up and resources are tighter. this puts us in a position that requires collaboration between parliament, the commission and our member states to make the best out of the budget: to answer the questions that both the rapporteurs have framed about how to help our economies and our people, especially the young people who are jobless in europe; how to make sure that we have the capacity to address the flows of people coming, seeking rescue or out of hopelessness; and how to make sure that the external challenges of europe are buffered appropriately with the use of our budget. these are not easy questions and i can say that there are areas where there is very strong agreement and there are areas where there would be a lot of work to do. where we are in agreement is that we have to expand the flexibility of the budget. i say that every time i have the chance. i thank parliament for what you have done to negotiate flexibility in the mff, which is what has saved us in recent years, and i am sure will do so again in the years ahead. we also have to simplify our rules, to use the revision of the financial regulation to make it easier for money to get to where it is designated to go. we have, broadly speaking, an agreement on the fact that we have to sharpen the link between money and priorities and make sure that we address top priorities with top euros. there are also very difficult questions and i am not going to shy away from those. the expectations in council and in parliament in terms of what we would deliver are quite diverse. we have to work on finding a way to bridge this divergence. we also know that the monti group is due to produce its report on own resources, and that is going to be an incredibly sensitive – and yet critical – issue for the future of the european union. from the commission side, i can tell you that we are working with all we have to make the budget deliver more, bigger and better results for our people, to stretch every euro to the maximum and to use our great creativity and flexibilities to do more with the money we have. i want to address a particular point that ms thomas brought up – the issue of legitimacy and accountability to parliament in respect of the instruments which help us to do more, like the turkey facility, but which fall outside the oversight of parliament. i believe we need to address that: to give parliament a role, to bring parliament into the decision making, and to be sure we do the best with the money we have because we will have parliament’s eyes looking over everything we fund from the sacrifice of our taxpayers. our commitment to bridging these difficult issues and to bridging the divide is genuine and we count on your being on our side as we go along this difficult road in the months to come.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security in the eu, as it is necessary to increase the security of the internet and of the private networks and information systems that underpin the functioning of our societies and economies. achieving this objective requires member states to improve cooperation among themselves and requires critical infrastructure operators and key service providers such as e-commerce platforms, social networks and others, including public administrations to take appropriate steps to manage security risks and to report serious incidents to national authorities. currently, the capacity and readiness levels of the different member states are very different, and given that networks and information systems are interconnected, the overall network and information security of the eu is weakened by those member states whose level of protection is insufficient. in order to ensure a level playing field and to close the legislative gaps, the statutory obligations imposed by this directive are necessary.
