in writing. ‒ i fully support the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european border and coast guard and repealing regulation (ec) no 2007/2004, regulation (ec) no 863/2007 and council decision 2005/267/ec. this proposal transforms the existing frontex agency into a new and more competent agency called the european border and coast guard. the new agency will support member states where there are clear weaknesses and gaps in the protection of the eu's external borders, help manage the flows of migrants and the return of those refugees who have been denied asylum, and overall ensure internal security in the union. separately, the european border and coast guard will provide resources, equipment and expertise to the member states representing the union's external borders in order to be able to react quickly in case of weakness or breaches at our external borders.
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement reached on the creation of the european border and coast guard corps, which responds to the need to strengthen the union's external borders to better protect the internal mobility and security of european citizens. the extension of the mandate of the agency to support member states and the conditions for deployment of the rapid response team are to be welcomed. these are crucial elements for frontline states such as bulgaria, which, although still not part of schengen, has done its part to protect the union's external borders and internal security. implementation must be as rapid as possible. the agency will not solve all the problems, but it must be the tool of a new impetus to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past and to have a genuine common border management. adequate resources, including for emergency response, and adequate training of border and coastguards are needed. this training must be continuous, european and at the highest level, using all existing tools.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report's proposal to create a european border and coast guard, as it is an important step to tackle the growing migration crisis and the threat of new terrorist acts on eu territory. the decision to establish a european border and coast guard agency is important because it will guarantee the protection of the external borders and the free and safe movement within the eu's internal borders. i support the mechanism of 'shared responsibility' and collective action between member states and the eu, which is an essential contribution to increasing solidarity and accountability of national governments and european institutions and an important prerequisite for the protection of the eu's external borders and the management of migration flows. the mechanism will support frontline countries that are exposed to strong migratory pressures. countries that border the eu but are not part of schengen will be able to rely on rapid and adequate assistance to deal with sudden migration crises at their borders through the deployment of coastguards or maritime guards. the esdp is a pan-european system that will ensure the respect of the fundamental human rights of asylum seekers and assist member states in returning migrants who have entered the eu illegally to their countries of origin, without interfering with the decisions taken by national states.
in writing. ‒ on 6 july, my colleagues in the european parliament and i voted 483 to 181 in favour and 48 abstentions in favour of the creation of the european border and coast guard agency. although it passed under the shadow of 'brexit', it is a very important and positive vote for bulgaria and the eu. the new agency will succeed frontex and will have 1,500 professionals from eu member states. bulgaria will start its participation with 40 staff. the agency receives a modest budget, but it will grow in the future. if this corps had existed earlier, the most acute phases of the refugee crisis would not have happened. perhaps when we look back in 15 or 20 years, we will see that the european army had its beginnings in this very modest new unit. instead of constantly arguing about whether we need more europe, let's just take the steps that european citizens clearly support.

in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the creation of the european border and coast guard, because i believe that this new structure will contribute to more security at the european external borders, such as bulgaria. with the establishment of the agency, the responsibility for border protection will no longer be solely that of frontline parties, but will be the fruit of solidarity and cooperation between all member states. the establishment of a permanent pool of border guards and experts to be deployed rapidly in the event of strong migratory pressure at the external borders will ensure that bulgaria is not left alone and can rely on the support of european partners when necessary. the possibility of acquiring technical equipment will also facilitate and speed up the agency's response to emergencies. it is of the utmost importance that the return operations of migrants will be facilitated, which will inevitably reduce the pressure on europe, especially from economic migrants who are not entitled to international protection. last but not least, for the first time we are talking about a european coastguard, which is extremely important for the protection of our black sea border. the european border and coast guard is a step towards a more secure europe that will be able to respond to modern challenges. and a secure europe means a secure bulgaria.

in writing. ‒ i support the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 883/2013 as regards the secretariat of the supervisory board of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). the long-term building of financial stability in the eu is precisely about the fair allocation and use of funds. the secretariat of the olaf supervisory board should strengthen its independence. this will ensure the efficient functioning of this service and thus significantly reduce any financial disruption in the european union. european funds need open relationships, transparent financial accounts and accurate accountability of their leaders to demonstrate financial stability. these instruments will only be able to be implemented through appropriate regulation, which will ensure the independence and proper functioning of olaf. the european anti-fraud office should be based on the public financial interest. i therefore believe that the independence and immunity of this office, as well as the prevention of conflicts of interest, will only be successfully guaranteed if they are clearly expressed in the new regulation and in future administrative cooperation agreements.

rapporteur. – mr president, ms mogherini, last year we had an own-initiative report on the role of the united european union in the united nations system, which was a change from our usual procedure, but this year we are coming back to the traditional form of our annual recommendation to the council. the objective of these recommendations is to feed into the preparation of the eu priorities for the next un general assembly session each autumn, which the council normally adopts in july. we agreed on 22 compromises on the basis of 220 amendments and our opinion of the david committee. i would like to thank all the colleagues involved, the shadow rapporteurs, the political advisers and the members of the eu-un working group. the renewed un general assembly recommendations report gives us a chance annually to voice the opinion of the european parliament in times of great challenges. this is even more important in the light of the conflict on the eu’s doorstep, europe’s growing exposure to hybrid warfare, cyber-terrorism, foreign fighters, unprecedented waves of migrants, and the blurring of the distinction between external and internal threats. it also empowers our institution to present its opinion via the council to the un general assembly, not only on matters of migration, peace and security, and the fight against terrorism as mentioned above, but also on issues such as non-proliferation and disarmament, human rights, democracy and the rule of law, development, climate change, and the eu and reform of the un system. parliament’s recommendations to the council in the report are, among others, to continue to support multilateral attempts to find lasting political and peaceful solutions to ongoing conflicts in the middle east and africa; to support the ongoing comprehensive efforts to strengthen us-un peace operations and the organisation’s ability to address conflicts; to reiterate its unequivocal condemnation of terrorism and its full support for actions aimed at the defeat and eradication of terrorist organisations such as the so-called isis/daesh; to support un efforts to prevent non-state actors and terrorist groups from developing, manufacturing, acquiring or transferring weapons of mass destruction and conventional weapons; to promote greater support for the work of the united nations refugee agency in implementing its international mandate to protect refugees; to reiterate clearly and firmly that all human rights agreed under the eu charter are universal, indivisible and independent and that respect for these rights must be enforced; to continue to advocate for freedom of religion or belief; to call for the repeal of laws criminalising blasphemy or apostasy; to serve as protection against the persecution of religious minorities or non-believers; to work towards the implementation of sustainable development goals on the 2030 agenda for sustainable development; to ensure that the eu remains at the forefront of the fight against climate change and to cooperate further with the un in this area; to ensure swift implementation of the position taken at the 2015 un climate change conference in paris; to support a comprehensive reform of the un security council on the basis of a broad consensus; to promote the revitalisation of the work of the general assembly and improve the coordination and coherence of action by the un institutions. the council will adopt the conclusions on 18 july for the general assembly opening in september. therefore, if approved in plenary, parliament’s recommendations will be forwarded to the council for official consideration in the council’s priorities for the next un general assembly meeting. i hope that next year we will be a bit earlier, because there are only 10 days now for the council to consider parliament’s opinion. as you know, there was a postponement because of considerations related to the uk referendum.

challenges, in increasing administrative capacity in health, education, employment and labour mobility, and in creating new partnerships. at the same time, the report states that the interreg budget of around eur 10 billion represents only two per cent and eight tenths of the cohesion policy budget and unfortunately does not respond to the major challenges facing european territorial cooperation. the member states and the managing authorities are invited to establish structured and appropriately organised monitoring systems and evaluation plans with a view to better evaluating and disseminating knowledge of the achievements of interreg. the report encourages the use of interreg programmes to respond to the challenges of the refugee crisis and the exchange of good practices programmes by complementing grants. the report also notes the role of the european territorial cooperation groups in promoting european territorial cooperation. calls on the commission and the member states to make full use of the possibilities offered by interreg to facilitate cross-border labour mobility by adapting, if necessary, the administrative and social regulatory framework; interreg programmes should, in line with agreed priorities and complemented by other appropriate funding, support the challenges related to migration and promote effective integration policies. in this context, the report highlights the possibilities of european territorial cooperation and its potential to be developed in future territorial cooperation programmes and to underpin future cohesion policy based on the needs of the specific territory.
mr. chairman, commissioner, being born in the balkans is not always a bad thing. the harsh reality there allows you to see the most rational solution, however difficult and complex a question or a problem may seem to you. i would like to say that i am very sorry to hear that there are voices in this chamber calling for a reduction in cohesion policy. my dear colleagues, cohesion policy is not a cake that we can cut out whenever we want. behind it is the european budget, behind it is the multiannual financial framework, behind it are national budgets, tailored to finance hundreds of projects. hundreds of regions are counting on us. do we want to shoot ourselves in the foot? i want to ask these same voices: what would be left if we restricted this policy? stories, my colleagues, only stories. and people have heard enough of them. i'm sure this room has heard many things, but this time the voice that will prevail is the voice of reason. there are certainly issues that we should raise, but they are not about cohesion policy. they're about excessive bureaucracy or why 70% of horizon goes to six countries. i'm sure this time the voice of reason will prevail.
the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, thank you for your comments on the report on territorial cooperation. i thank all the colleagues who have expressed their views during the debate in the regi committee, where we have worked very hard on this report. i would like to emphasise once again that european territorial cooperation has proven its effectiveness and potential beyond the traditional framework of regional policy: in areas such as the single market, digital technologies, employment, mobility, energy, research, why not specialisation, smart specialisation in individual regions; in the field of education, culture, health, the environment. i am convinced that european territorial cooperation has the potential to develop in the future. in future cohesion policy after 2020, it can be the basis for a specialisation according to the needs of the territory, the potential of the specific territory and on the basis of strategic planning for the development of the territory, whether it is a cross-border or a territory in which we have a specific specialisation. territorial cooperation can give further impetus to the general idea of the european union. european territorial cooperation has potential for future development and i am convinced that such debates will lead to the future development of the idea of territorial cooperation.
in writing. the eu trust fund for africa is an important instrument for strengthening stability in africa and addressing the root causes of irregular and forced migration. the continuing flow of migration clearly shows that the migration crisis cannot be contained without a lasting stabilisation of the eu's neighbouring regions. africa has the world's fastest growing population, and its relative share is expected to reach 25% of the world's population by 2050. the european union must continue to support the security and development of the countries in the region. member states need to do more to meet their formal commitments, but it is also important to increase the flexibility of the eu budget to allow for more emergency response. despite its great potential, europe cannot tackle the root causes of migration problems on its own. the commission should also be able to provide the necessary support to the member states in the implementation of the union's external action programmes. international law applies equally around the world, and other high- and middle-income countries could do more by increasing their financial support.
a question asked by raising a blue card. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, do you not think that this meeting should have paid more attention to the role of the dictatorial regime in turkey in the migrant crisis? and don't you think that we should have turned back more and asked about sanctions on turkey, which, just as russia annexed part of ukraine, for the second time annexed territory from a sovereign state? i would remind you of the annexation of cyprus and the current invasion of syria by turkish armed forces.
thank you madam president. by all accounts, this year’s g20 summit was dominated by a new and overriding awareness. the rising anger of people at the ravages that present-day neoliberal globalisation has caused in their lives. media reports have claimed that australian prime minister turnbull actually called on leaders to ‘civilise capitalism.’ some of this awareness has found its way in the final communiqué, which states: ‘quality employment is at the centre of the g20’s domestic and global agenda, together with reducing inequalities and promoting inclusive labour force participation.’ these precisely are the big issues (in capital letters) that president junker and his commission must directly tackle with the utmost urgency and full priority, or see the european project disintegrate under the tidal wave of widespread and completely justified popular protest.
in writing. the g20 summit took place in an extremely sensitive environment for the world and europe. it is impressive that the topics discussed at the forum were of direct relevance to the european union and this clearly shows the range of challenges we all face. the need for more sustainable and high-quality economic growth, punitive measures against tax havens in the world, the need to invest in new technologies and take action against global warming were discussed, alongside the fight against terrorism and the international refugee crisis. in this context, i believe that the g20 was a great opportunity for the european union to reaffirm the need for comprehensive global action to share responsibility for resolving the refugee and migration crisis and addressing its root causes. and we should not overlook the fact that the final document of the meeting stated that the results of the referendum in the uk add uncertainty to the global economy. the forum also highlighted the important role played by bilateral and regional trade agreements and i believe that the european union should work towards the early ratification of an agreement to facilitate and liberalise international trade.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report as it highlights the role of multi-level governance in the strategy-making process, the role of the eu urban development programme in creating synergies and strong links for efficient use of resources, and the role of monitoring and evaluation as an important part of smart specialisation strategies in the 2014-2020 programming period.
in writing. i supported the report on cohesion policy and the r & d and innovation strategies for the smart specialisation initiative (ris3) because i believe that technology and innovation are a key prerequisite for economic growth for both the regions and the eu. cohesion policy provides instruments to promote research and innovation development by using local and regional assets, which can bridge the gaps in innovation progress between regions. i believe that through regional focus, strategic and effective planning and use of public research and innovation investments will support not only well developed areas but also less developed and rural areas, will give impetus to strengthening employment and growth at local level and will help to strengthen administrative capacity at local and regional level.
in writing. ‒ research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation are particularly important in times when the eu needs to create smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in order to tackle financial and social crises across the union. i supported the resolution and it is important to note that for the 2014-2020 programming period, member states are required, for the first time, to develop national and/or regional smart specialisation strategies by involving national and regional managing authorities and stakeholders such as higher education institutions, industry and social partners, in an entrepreneurial discovery process. therefore, research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation should be designed by a strong governance system and should stimulate private investment in research, technology and development.
in writing. i gave my support to this resolution calling on eu countries to improve the implementation and monitoring of 'intelligent specialisation strategies' (ris3 or s3) because i believe that s3 can fill some of the gaps in cohesion policy. although eu cohesion policy is a highly important mechanism whose main objective should be to eliminate existing socioeconomic disparities between the different european regions, a large part of the european structural and investment funds has failed to be attracted by rural and other less developed regions, which experience difficulties in the preparation and implementation of regional strategies. in this context, i firmly support the call of this resolution to develop the administrative capacity of disadvantaged regions. it is through improvements in administrative capacity that rural and less developed regions, such as those in my country bulgaria, will be able to identify their strengths and priority areas for development in a way that maximises the potential of their population, creating new skills, knowledge, innovation and jobs.
in writing. ‒ with increasingly fierce competition worldwide, it is crucial for the eu to continue to improve its innovation capacity. ris3 contribute to the efficient use of eu funds and unlock the potential of all regions, help the eu to tackle innovation gaps and increase its competitiveness. the report emphasises the need for a regional approach to implementing ris3 and calls for the eu and member states to periodically monitor the implementation of the strategies. ris3 strategies are a valuable tool for bridging innovation gaps and for boosting jobs and growth in europe.
in writing. – i voted in favour because one of my priorities is to encourage innovation at all levels. i believe that ris3 aims to create knowledge- based growth not only in well-developed areas, but also in less-developed and rural regions. the report sends a support signal from the eu to ris3 strategies, calls for them to be improved and also to for lessons to be learned from the strategies already initiated in order to achieve the best results in the forthcoming years in this area.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by ms iskra mikhailova on european territorial cooperation best practices and innovative measures, as this policy is part of the european union's cohesion policy, which is of paramount importance for bulgaria and its economic and social development. with an allocation of eur 10.1 billion for the 2014-2020 programming period, european territorial development aims to support overall cooperation between national, regional and local actors, with a focus on cross-border cooperation and support for border regions. mrs mikhailova's report is important for two main reasons. firstly, it calls for a substantial budget increase in the next programming period to increase investment in border regions, as they are particularly affected by the current refugee crisis. secondly, the report calls for the implementation of territorial cooperation programmes to be simplified in order to make them more accessible to the various actors and thus increase the impact of the invested funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on european territorial cooperation best practices and innovative measures, as i consider the etc to be an important instrument of cohesion policy, whose purpose is to solve problems that go beyond administrative boundaries and require common solutions. over the period 2014-2020, more than eur 10 billion has been allocated to cross-border, transnational and interregional cooperation programmes. the appropriations under these instruments have contributed to better regional connectivity, mobility and access to services, knowledge and innovation transfer, enhancing the competitiveness of smes and strengthening regional identity. the commission has also been able to demonstrate that it is able to meet the challenges of the environment, better manage risks and respond to disasters, and to strengthen institutional capacity building and social capital, strengthen cross-border network structures and create new partnerships. i support the call on the commission and the member states to work towards preserving the ets as an important and positive instrument for the european integration process, with the ets being given a more important role in the context of cohesion policy after 2020.
in writing. ‒ i supported the text because european territorial cooperation (etc) is one of the most important goals of cohesion policy for 2014-2020. the etc makes a significant contribution to strengthening the eu’s objective of territorial cohesion through integrating diverse sectoral policies on territorial scale. in this regard, it could be argued that the etc has a significant european added value. it contributes to peace, stability, economic development and regional integration not only in europe but also in the world (in the framework of enlargement and neighbourhood policy). therefore, etc’s potential should be further developed beyond regional policy in areas such as the single market, the digital agenda, employment, mobility and energy, research, education, culture, health and environment. the commission and member states should consider preserving etc as an important instrument, allocating it a more distinct role within cohesion policy post-2020 and significantly increasing its budget.
in writing. european territorial cooperation is one of the two important objectives of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, although only 2.8% of the cohesion policy budget is earmarked for this purpose. i supported mrs mikhailova's report, which sought to support territorial cooperation between member states, also taking into account that 38% of the european population lives in border areas. the overall objective of cross-border cooperation is to reduce the impact of social borders in order to reduce regional disparities and remaining barriers to investment. i believe that better cooperation between bulgaria and the neighbouring member states would contribute to improving the economic, social, cultural and territorial development not only of the balkan region but also of the eu as a whole. the importance of cross-border labour markets, which are highly dynamic in terms of job creation, is also growing. member states should make use of interreg programmes to facilitate cross-border labour mobility and to encourage, where necessary, the adaptation of the administrative and social regulatory framework, as well as to enhance dialogue at all levels of government. european territorial cooperation needs to be improved, as a small number of european citizens still benefit from all the opportunities offered by the eu's internal market and freedom of movement.
in writing. – i supported this resolution as for 25 years the etc has been a key instrument to achieve territorial cohesion through support of a number of programmes and projects with strong european added value. it has made significant progress in a number of key sectors – connectivity, innovation and knowledge, to mention a few. the report in question takes the measure of these developments.
in writing. ‒ i supported the interim report on the inquiry into emissions in the automotive sector, which was drawn up by the committee of inquiry dealing with the case. i support the fact that the report is based on technical information and data and does not contain any political findings or statements. i agree that full cooperation between the european institutions and national governments is needed to achieve better results.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because there is no doubt that the committee of inquiry should have full support from the conference of presidents and the bureau, the commission and the governments, parliaments and competent authorities of member states. all support is needed for committee’s actions and initiatives leading to the accomplishment of the mandate given by parliament in its decision of 17 december 2015.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the eu-china agreement in connection with the accession of croatia. this technical report reflects the need to adapt the agreement following the accession of croatia to the eu and the enlargement of the customs union. this update concerns the reduction of the european customs duties for certain types of products and the increase of the import quota for other agricultural products.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to conclude an agreement with the people's republic of china on the modification of concessions in the list of the republic of croatia in the process of its accession to the european union, as it is in line with eu practice in previous enlargements and in line with the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt). i support the compensatory adjustments for china envisaged by the commission in relation to losses from the withdrawal of concessions by croatia, as they are proportionate and in line with previous practices within the wto.
in writing. ‒ with croatia’s accession on 1 july 2013, the eu enlarged its customs union. the european parliament gave its consent to the compensatory agreement with the people’s republic of china and i supported the resolution. the agreement will respect the trading rights of the people’s republic of china and on the other hand is a sign of the eu’s attachment to the wto’s multilateral rules-based trading regime. the compensatory agreement will enable croatia to benefit fully from trade relations between the eu and the people’s republic of china (eu and china now trade well over eur 1 billion a day). last but not least, the compensatory agreement could serve as a basis and a proof that china meets its wto obligations and trades.
in writing. – as a member of parliament’s delegation for relations with china, i am following closely the relationship between the european union and china. the eu is china’s largest trade partner and china is the eu’s second largest partner. with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union enlarged its customs union. consequently, the european union was required under world trade organisation (wto) rules to enter into negotiations with wto members having negotiating rights related to the tariff schedule of croatia in order to eventually agree on a compensatory adjustment. that is why i am fully supporting the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation to conclude an agreement between the eu and uruguay on the modification of the concessions in the list of the republic of croatia in the process of its accession to the european union. the report is technical and reflects the need to adapt existing agreements following the enlargement of the european customs union following the accession of the republic of croatia to the eu.
in writing. ‒ with croatia’s accession on 1 july 2013, the eu enlarged its customs union. in the light of this, the european parliament should give its consent to the compensatory agreement with the eastern republic of uruguay. the agreement will respect the trading rights of the eastern republic of uruguay and, at the same time, it is a sign of the eu’s attachment to the wto multilateral rules-based trading regime. it is important to note that the eu will incorporate in its schedule for the customs territory of the eu 28 uruguay’s specific high-quality beef quota (eu regulation 481/2012, 48 200 tons). last but not least, the compensatory agreement will enable croatia to benefit fully from trade relations between the eu and the eastern republic of uruguay (worth eur 1.603 million in eu exports to uruguay and eur 1.131 million in eu imports from uruguay).
in writing. – with the accession of the republic of croatia, the eu enlarged its customs union and was therefore required under wto rules (article xxiv:6 of the gatt 1994) to enter into negotiations to the eastern republic of uruguay regarding the tariff schedule of croatia in order to eventually agree on a compensatory adjustment as the eu’s external tariff regime results in an increase of tariffs. i voted in favour as trade is one of the key policies for the eu and for the benefit of eu citizens. furthermore, this proposal has no financial impact on expenditure, but has a financial impact on revenue.
in writing. i supported the report on the proposal to appoint mr lazaros stavrou lazarou as a member of the court of auditors, as mr lazarou has the necessary qualifications and experience as a member of the court of auditors since 2010. mr lazarou has written many specialist reports and i am confident that he will continue to contribute constructively to the work of the court of auditors.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the proposal for the appointment of mr juan alejandro tavares gonzález de figueredo as a member of the court of auditors, as i believe that mr figueredo has the necessary experience in the fields of public finance, budgeting and strategic management.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this draft regulation as it relates to statistics on external trade with third countries and to the functioning of the eu in relation to the conferral of delegated and implementing powers on the commission to adopt certain measures. it's important that there's a thorough discussion. fortunately, following the publication of the outcome of the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making, the draft regulation has been revised accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i did not support this report, although we have seen a thorough consultation process in the form of a dialogue not only with the member states but also with the national regulators. the regulation has been interpreted to replace directive 2008/92/ec. under this regulation, member states will have to collect and report statistics on industrial and household gas and electricity prices. price data will be reported every six months for different consumption volumes and will cover energy prices, access charges, fees and charges and their sub-components. despite the strange first impression, this report deals only with factual reporting and imposes other obligations on member states. the sovereignty of the member states in matters of policy therefore remains intact. that's why i decided to support this initiative.
in writing. i supported the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices and repealing directive 2008/92/ec of the european parliament and of the council on a community procedure to improve the transparency of gas and electricity prices for industrial end-users, as i believe that access to data on natural gas and electricity prices is in the interest of the household end-user. this step would improve the quality of the survey of electricity and natural gas prices for the household sector, the inclusion of components such as excise duties, and ensure price comparability across member states. i believe that access to data for the household and non-household sectors would help to improve the cost breakdown methodology and the accuracy of the overall average share of transmission and distribution costs.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because the collection of the electricity and natural gas price charged to industrial consumers and households should become obligatory for all member states. this step is necessary in order to continue to achieve a wide market coverage and high quality of price data. the price data on gas and electricity prices are needed for monitoring the internal market for energy, and the impacts of various policies in the field of energy, such as support for renewable energy sources. this is particularly important in the context of the energy union strategy, which obligates the commission to prepare reports about energy costs and prices every two years, starting in 2016.
mr president, i have supported this report, i consider it important. for me, building an internal energy market is not just a matter of economic advantage and strengthening the eu internal market as such, but it is also a matter of energy security, which is particularly geopolitically important for smaller countries that were formerly under the influence of the soviet union during the communist era. in short, the better the internal energy market, the less dependent we will be on energy from outside the eu, for example from russia, and the better able we will be to negotiate better terms with our external partners. the advantage of this material, which is why i endorse and support it, is that it leaves it up to the individual states to choose their energy sources, including nuclear energy. nuclear energy is not banned here, which i think is very correct and sensible.
mr president, the report we are voting on today is entitled 'towards a new concept for the energy market'. i would question that. my country bulgaria had to decommission a total of four reactors from a nuclear power plant that served the needs of a number of countries in the region in order to join the european union. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the capacity of the electricity market in the prc. the commission notes that the project is not a public-private partnership, but is a public-private partnership. any delay takes away the opportunity to create jobs in one of the poorest regions in the european union. how will economic growth in europe be achieved if the cost goes into building new and new infrastructure rather than making full use of projects already underway? that's what every bulgarian citizen pays for every day.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this file because, although it contains some good ideas, it refers to the overall top-down approach. when we talk about energy markets, especially with recommendations for better cooperation, we must not forget that geopolitical challenges across the european union vary widely. when discussing policy, these regional specificities must be taken into account immediately. in addition, there is an even more fundamental challenge infrastructure. bulgaria is one of the eu member states that is struggling with these similar challenges. the solution to overcome these obstacles is not to introduce both centralised and decentralised structures. market distortions and inappropriate investment in new facilities must be avoided, and if these are eu-led, we will put the whole system at risk. incorporating more renewable energy is a good approach, and i strongly support it. nevertheless, the eu's approach to defining the energy mix policy will ignore regional specificities and only disrupt the functioning of the whole structure.
in writing. i supported the report on a new energy market concept as i believe it is a successful step towards achieving and guaranteeing the eu's energy independence. it is necessary to establish a long-term and transparent concept that includes and protects both national and european objectives and interests, striking a balance between security of supply and price sustainability. the integrated single energy market will help overcome europe's energy dependence on russian gas and oil imports, which will provide a prerequisite for achieving and negotiating better terms with new and potential eu energy partners. i believe that a coordinated renewable energy policy between the eu and national energy policies will promote the production and consumption of energy from renewable sources, help to integrate the energy market, reduce the prerequisites for energy poverty and promote the fight against climate change.
in writing. ‒ i supported this dossier because it represents a good ideological approach to tackling the heating and cooling problems across the eu. i have some concerns about the possibility of getting some significant short-term effects, but in the long run, this is the only viable strategy if we want to improve the system and preserve the environment, considering the resources. it is clear that an assessment of the situation will have to be made for each member state, as the challenges vary drastically.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu heating and cooling strategy and i share the view that there is a need for a significant increase in funding for heat remediation activities for whole housing complexes, especially those built using large panel systems as a construction method. more funds from the european energy efficiency and renewable energy fund should be allocated to this purpose. it should become a priority, especially in view of the fact that the owners of the buildings concerned are generally unable to bear the associated costs and that the support from the national state is insufficient. it should also be emphasised that the greatest potential for efficiency gains in the new countries that joined the eu after 2004 is offered by the thermal remediation of buildings. this is a good way to ensure that energy is used more efficiently and to achieve a significant reduction in co2 emissions. the outdated thermal power plants in housing complexes must be replaced by small, high-efficiency thermal and power plants.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i think it contains many positive elements. special attention is paid to the role of smes for the european economy and cohesion policy, reducing red tape and encouraging financing. i am not only in favour of linking support for smes to the integration of migrants and refugees.
in writing. i support the report on the implementation of the thematic objective 'enhancing the competitiveness of smes'. it is fundamental to achieving the objectives of the cohesion policy and europe 2020. it accurately represents the concentration on cohesion policies and provides an effective tool for creating operational programmes with a better focus on investment priorities. last but not least, it explains the importance of smes as the main generators of job vacancies, the basis of the economies of the member states and the sector that most successfully develops the service sector. we continue to push for less red tape, easier access to a variety of sources of funding and greater precision in the criteria and selection of smes for support. although it's the fastest-adapting sector, it's also the most vulnerable because it doesn't have a lot of turnover. cohesion policies would further support the growth of the regions in the member states. it is also important to create the conditions for specialised training to ensure sustainability and management capacity.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are essential to the economy of eu regions in terms of both employment and competitiveness. during the 2014-2020 programming period, cohesion policy will provide additional support for smes, with support for the 2007-2013 period doubling to reach eur 140 billion. by 2020, smes are expected to provide industrial production amounting to at least 20% of the gdp of the member states. the report calls on the commission, when formulating cohesion policy for the period after 2020, to increase funding for the competitiveness of smes.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution as i believe that it is favourable to smes. the report introduces thematic concentration in the cohesion policy programming 2014-2020. through thematic concentration, operational programmes appeared to be better targeted towards a limited number of strategic goals, in particular in terms of growth enhancement and high quality job creation potential for smes.
i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs bresso, on her report on the european union strategy for the alpine region. at the same time, however, i would also like to draw attention to the need for a similar approach and strategy for other mountain regions in the european union, and in particular the balkans. the mountain regions, as we know, are disadvantaged compared to other regions, they are more flexible and we need to approach them in a special way. in her report, ms bresso called on the european investment bank to explore the possibility of creating an investment platform for the alpine region and also called for the creation of a project channel for the region that would attract investors. similar steps should be taken towards other mountain regions of the european union, and in particular towards south-east europe, where mountains are an important link in cross-border cooperation. i therefore call for equal access to quality financing for all mountain regions in the european union, for quality investment and growth in them, so that there is no europe at two or even three speeds.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the eu strategy for the alpine region. it covers seven countries, five of which are eu member states, and 48 regions with a population of over 80 million. the aim of this strategy is to promote the beneficial interaction between mountain and surrounding lowland and urban regions. from a financial point of view, the strategy does not require the use of additional funds, but rather builds on the potential of the esi.
in writing. ‒ i expressed my support for the report on the european union strategy for the alpine region, as i believe it provides an answer to common issues for the region, in line with the major european objectives of 'europe 2020' in the field of sustainable development, the environment and energy. proposals for the responsible management of sustainable and competitive tourism, the diversification of tourism products and supply in order to overcome the seasonal nature and improve the quality and innovation in tourism are of key importance for the development of the alpine region. at the same time, protecting the remarkable lake system that runs through the alpine and pre-alpine plains, preserving and restoring the biodiversity of ecosystems by providing an appropriate monitoring, information and management system for the natura 2000 network, requires sustainable nature management. it enables the countries of the region to invest in joint projects at european, not just interregional, level and to promote the achievement of sustainable development of the alpine economy and the sustainable use of alpine resources. i hope that the experience gained from the implementation of the strategy will soon be used in other mountain areas of the community.
in writing. ‒ the report calls on the eib, in cooperation with the commission, to explore the possibility of creating an investment platform for the alpine region that would allow for the mobilisation of funds from public and private sources; calls for the creation of a gas pipeline project for the region that would attract investors; encourages the creation of clusters and cooperation between public and private enterprises, universities, research institutes and other stakeholders to promote innovation.
in writing. – i supported this report as it underlines the importance of financial instruments, of encouraging innovation and new technologies in key areas of the economy, while preserving also forms of traditional economic activity. it supports the diversification of tourism, stresses the importance of improving transport and energy connectivity, as well as of protecting and enhancing the biodiversity in the alpine region.
in writing. ‒ i voted abstention on the report on the eu trust fund for africa: the implications for development and humanitarian aid, as i am generally in favour of giving money to african countries for development and stabilisation in the region, but i cannot agree with the criticism in the resolution that member states are not contributing enough money to this fund. at a time when member states are still emerging from the economic crisis and need to invest continuously to deal with the refugee crisis, countries should not be obliged to give more money. on top of that, the latest reports of the european court of auditors have many comments on the use of european funds, especially in north africa. the reports criticise european programmes for having weak controls on spending and for having little impact on investment. that is why i believe that before the union can start to provide large amounts of development and stabilisation funds, it must establish robust control mechanisms to reduce the misuse of european public funds.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report as it contains constructive recommendations to improve the effectiveness of the emergency trust fund for africa. the instrument was set up at the valletta migration summit in november 2015 and symbolises the eu's commitment to tackling the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration. i support the call in the report for member states to align their contributions with the union contribution in order to enable the eu trust fund to develop to its full potential. it is also essential to ensure that the eu trust fund reflects the principles of policy coherence for sustainable development and complementarity between all development stakeholders. i believe that the rules for funding projects with eu trust fund funds should be determined on the basis of shared values and common interests. therefore, particular emphasis should be placed on the respect and promotion of human rights, including women's rights. empowering women and ensuring their active participation in the political, economic and social development of countries of origin is a key element in strengthening stability in africa and will contribute to better managing migration.
in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa (eutf) is a very important development tool that pools together resources from different donors in order to enable a quick, flexible, and collective eu response to the different dimensions of an emergency situation. in particular, the eutf aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration by promoting resilience, economic opportunities, equal opportunities, security and development in 23 countries across three african regions (the horn of africa, the sahel and lake chad basin; and north africa). however, to achieve its goals and to be effective, the eutf should provide a better balance of funding for recipient country governments and especially for reliable civil society actors, who tend to be more aware of societal deficiencies which are in need of support.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution because i would like to support development and humanitarian aid. in times of unprecedented levels of irregular migration, this trust fund aims to support the most affected african countries, to help foster stability in those regions and to promote tighter africa-eu cooperation on issues of migration management, security and development. the eutf aims at addressing the root causes of destabilisation, displacement and irregular migration in three regions: the horn of africa, the sahel and lake chad, and north africa.
in writing. ‒ working families are facing new challenges in work-life balance. this report provides suggestions for the commission to consider in modernising and adapting the current eu legal and policy framework on childrearing and maternity. i and my political group are strong supporters of the family and its values and believe that there should be freedom in finding a balance between family and professional life. however, many of the things proposed in the report are contrary to the principle of subsidiarity, and some paragraphs suggest even more men staying at home to encourage women in working life, which is not an eu job and is a personal choice that cannot be put into a legal framework. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i support the report on creating conditions in the labour market that favour work-life balance. equality between men and women is a fundamental principle enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which must be guaranteed in all areas, including with regard to work-life balance. well-designed and implemented policies to achieve this balance should be seen as a significant improvement in the working environment, as they contribute to good working conditions and to social and occupational well-being. i believe that a good work-life balance is a driver for economic growth, competitiveness, equal participation in the labour market, gender equality, reduction of the risk of poverty and solidarity between generations.

mr. chairman, mr. commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, over the past few years, the republic of the philippines has made significant progress. it is no coincidence that the european union granted the country gsp+ status at the end of 2014. in terms of human rights legislation, until recently, the country has been a model for other countries in the region, having ratified eight of the nine major conventions, but also being one of the first countries in asia to speak out against the death penalty. unfortunately, after the presidential election, the situation in the philippines has changed dramatically. state policy has taken on authoritarian dimensions. the unprecedented murder of 1,800 suspected drug dealers without trial or evidence of alleged crimes is an undemocratic act that we must oppose. i call on the philippine government to end extrajudicial executions and to abide by the international instruments that the country has ratified. it is necessary for president rodrigo duterte to guarantee a fair and independent judiciary and to engage in dialogue with international leaders and organisations to return the country to the path of democracy.
in writing. ‒ mr hala-aho's report updates the eu travel document standard, established in 1994, to speed up the process of returning non-eu nationals who are living illegally in the eu and do not have valid passports or identity cards. many european countries have extraordinary difficulties in returning these people to their countries of origin in a safe and legal manner. today, only 40% of eu irregular migrants are returned, as many non-eu countries do not accept documents issued by different eu countries, as many of them differ and do not meet the security and authenticity requirements. in order to speed up the return of irregular residents and increase the reliability of travel documents, it was necessary to update the legislation and to propose a common format for a european travel document. the new document will use all the security features used for european visas and will include personal information such as name, age, gender, distinctive signs and will clearly indicate that the document is valid for one trip only until the person arrives in the third country.
in writing. ‒ i support the european commission's proposal for a standardised travel document for the accelerated return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the european union. i believe that this document would make the administration and data processing easier. in view of the refugee situation, such a travel document would contribute to facilitating information systems and to a clearer view of the volumes of illegally staying citizens and border security. recognition of this document by the parties could limit abuses of asylum systems in europe and strengthen european citizens' confidence in eu asylum and immigration policy.
in writing. ‒ i have always stressed that the flow of refugees to the member states of the european union is a mixed flow of asylum seekers and illegal economic migrants. i am pleased that we have succeeded in making the return of those who do not qualify for international protection a priority for the european union. in most cases, these people do not have valid identity documents. member states are experiencing major difficulties in returning them. the data show that less than 40% of return decisions are actually implemented. the single european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals is a tool we aim to improve this. it will reduce the administrative burden and the deadlines. efficiency is key here. for a well-managed migration policy, the system must be both swift and fair. this will make it easier for countries to help and for refugees to get the help they need.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the prospectus to be published for the offer to the public or admission to trading of securities, as it is key to the proper functioning of the common capital market. the report aims to improve access to finance for companies of all sizes, in particular smes, and to reduce barriers, while maintaining adequate investor protection. the report simplifies the rules for the drawing up, approval and publication of prospectuses when securities are offered to the public or traded on a regulated market. this will greatly help smes, as they often face excessive costs in drawing up prospectuses in order to access capital.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report establishing provisional measures in the field of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece, as i do not support the measures proposed by the commission for the resettlement of refugees, as well as the eu-turkey agreement on the exchange of refugees and the provision of financial assistance. i've been against mandatory refugee quotas from the beginning, which won't work, and more and more countries are refusing to take in refugees. according to ms. keller's report, the goal of the one-for-one refugee exchange scheme with turkey is for each syrian returned to help another syrian fleeing war and persecution. i am categorically against this measure, which is itself conflicting and discriminatory - how can some syrians have the right to asylum and others do not, but also the syrians sent by turkey are in no way threatened by war and persecution, because they are already in a safe country. under international law, a refugee fleeing war should be held in the first safe country and as close as possible to his home country so that he can easily return after the conflict is over, which is not the case for refugees coming to the eu. refugees come to the eu to stay.
in writing. i supported this report because it represents a concrete expression of solidarity with member states or third countries affected by a mass influx of migrants. this proposal for a council decision amending decision (eu) 2015/1601 allows member states to subtract from their transferee numbers the number of syrians admitted to their territory from turkey through resettlement, humanitarian admission or other forms of legal admission. the european parliament's report recognised that the implementation of the different resettlement schemes, humanitarian admission or other forms of legal admission would alleviate the migratory pressure on frontline member states. this will also make it possible to replace the dangerous and illegal migration flows of syrian nationals to the eu with safe and legal ways of migration. last but not least, i welcome the swift adoption of this report by the european parliament. this will support and accelerate the adoption of measures to deal with emergency situations, such as the current one, characterised by an increased flow of migrants, in accordance with the treaties on the functioning of the union.

in writing. – small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and mid-caps form a substantial part of the eu economy. access to finance for smes has been a long-standing objective of the eu policy agenda. as a substitute member of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, i am working towards easing access to finance for smes, and the capital markets union (cmu) can provide a good opportunity for them. that is why i fully support this report.
in writing. ‒ i supported mr krasnodembski's report as it highlights the important role of smes in job creation. currently, 85% of jobs in the union are created by smes and that is why their activity should be encouraged. the rapporteur stresses that in order to achieve a stable environment for business development and increase its job creation potential, national and european policies must prioritise addressing skills issues (shortages, mismatches, brain drain), regulatory uncertainty and administrative burdens, and the problem of undeclared work. the rapporteur also stresses the need to ensure a level playing field for smes in terms of their competitive position compared to large corporations. small and local businesses are particularly disadvantaged in the current over-regulated and bureaucratic administrative system.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on the search for the best way to harness the job-creating potential of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the sector needs a lot of support to continue its successful development. this support will mean tackling youth unemployment levels and the unprecedentedly high rate of unemployment in general. we need to clearly identify the main challenges we need to overcome in order to create more job opportunities. these include skills shortages, insufficient assessment of future skills needs, mismatches between skills and needs, brain drain, unnecessary regulatory burden and regulatory uncertainty in all areas, lack of dialogue between market stakeholders, limited access to finance and public procurement, insufficient capacity for innovation and access to new technologies, insufficient support for smes under public investment policies, the grey economy and fraud, and the privileged position of mncs. the solutions are rooted in promoting a strong entrepreneurial culture, developing forms of cooperation between member states, appropriate training and changing legislation in member states.
in writing. – as a member of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection i work for cutting red-tape for businesses and removing barriers for accessing markets. i voted in favour of this report, which promotes the conditions for smes’ development and for decreasing the administrative burdens and difficulties they experience.

in writing. ‒ mr president president, ladies and gentlemen, unfortunately discrimination on grounds of sex, nationality, ethnicity or religion continues to be a barrier in the daily lives of too many europeans. i therefore support the conclusions of the report on the application of the employment equality directive. in order to effectively exercise the principles of equality and fundamental rights and freedoms in the field of employment, member states should systematically ensure that all existing legal texts comply with the principle of equal treatment. i expect them to encourage the work of national labour inspection bodies and to develop policies to raise awareness of victims of discrimination in employment, as workers are often not aware of their rights, the competent authorities to which they can turn, or the possibilities of obtaining support and legal protection.
in writing. i support the report on the implementation of the employment equality directive, adopted 15 years ago, whose ultimate aim is to create a level playing field in employment equality. the data from the fourth eurobarometer show that more europeans are tolerant of groups at risk of discrimination and are better informed about their rights in the event of discrimination than in the previous survey, conducted in 2012. there are still challenges to implementing the directive. i believe that member states should show greater commitment to the implementation of the principle of equality between women and men in employment policies and should develop gender-neutral occupational classifications and evaluation systems as mandatory measures to promote equal treatment. i also call on the member states to encourage employers to hire young people, while ensuring and respecting equal treatment in terms of pay and social protection.

my dear mrs. the chairman, mr. commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, unfortunately the problem of match fixing is widespread not only on our continent but also far beyond it. along with doping, it ranks as one of the most serious problems of our time. according to interpol data, in the one-year period between june 2012 and may 2013 alone, there were reports of match fixing in 70 countries, and that was in football alone. the international football association has reported that organised crime makes over €13 billion from this type of activity, and sees it as a safer alternative to drug trafficking, prostitution and human trafficking. according to interpol, sports betting attracts around one trillion euros a year, with nearly three quarters of that amount betting on football. although football and tennis are the most commonly affected sports, unfortunately, in recent years similar practices have been observed in boxing, basketball, handball, and volleyball. the commission considers that the measures provided for in this decision are in accordance with the opinion of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, i believe that the council of europe convention on the manipulation of sports competitions has the potential to become one of the most important, if not the most important, documents and instruments in this field. to this end, however, it is necessary to take steps to ensure that it is signed and ratified by the member states. i believe that efforts must be made to overcome the existing obstacles to its ratification in order to combat this harmful practice effectively, and not just read declarations.

in writing. ‒ i supported the ratification of the paris agreement adopted under the un framework convention on climate change as an important step for global action against climate change. the european parliament's consent opens the way to overcoming the double threshold and the entry into force of the paris agreement before the cop 22 climate change conference in marrakech from 7 to 18 november 2016. i believe that early ratification of the agreement is a top priority for the eu. a situation where the agreement enters into force without the eu being a party to it should be avoided, as the eu is a global leader in climate action policies and the world's largest financial donor.
in writing. ‒ today, the european parliament ratified the largest and first binding agreement of its kind against climate change. a large majority in the plenary of 610 votes for (90%) supported the text. it was a historic vote, ensuring that the paris agreement to combat climate change will be in force by the end of the year. the agreement commits parties for the first time to take concrete measures to limit global warming to below 2°c. europe is a global leader in the fight against climate change, and today we confirmed that. let us not forget that this is only the beginning of a long journey and it is up to all of us to make this agreement a success.

in writing. ‒ ladies and gentlemen, today, in the presence of the un secretary-general, we adopted a resolution on the eu's ratification of the paris climate agreement - a historic act, because the conditions for the agreement's entry into force will be met. it has been ratified by 63 parties to the unfccc (at least 55 if required) and accounts for around 52% of global greenhouse gas emissions (55% if required). as of today, the seven eu member states that have completed national ratification will be added, thus fulfilling the second criterion. thus, only nine months after its signature, the paris agreement can enter into force, whereas it took almost eight years to ratify the kyoto protocol, the agreement's predecessor. this is clear evidence that the world is ripe for global action to combat climate change, whether it's in developed or developing countries. i would remind you that in paris, the countries agreed to limit warming to 2°c, set a target of even 1.5°c, and in the second half of this century, strike a balance between anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases and their reabsorption by the earth and the seas. a truly historic moment in saving the planet.

in writing. ‒ the main aim of the fund is to help people who have lost their jobs to reintegrate into the labour market. the eu should mobilise the fund to support finland’s submitted application egf/2016/001 fi/microsoft for a financial contribution from the egf, following 2161 redundancies in microsoft mobile oy and 8 of its suppliers and downstream producers in finland. the main reason behind the redundancies in microsoft is the declining market share of its mobile phones. they link the workforce reductions to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation by recalling that the eu share in the ict sector employment has decreased, while the share of china and the united states has increased. ict plays a key role in the finnish economy, with 6.7% of employees working in the ict sector in 2014 – the highest percentage amongst all member states. the egf is expected to support redundant workers through further education, training or entrepreneurship. another reason why i supported the mobilisation of the fund is that the finnish authorities have implemented all the necessary measures to activate and receive the egf fund.
in writing. in recent years, many european and foreign companies have closed their offices and branches in eu member states as a result of the short-sighted neoliberal economic policies pursued at european level. in the information and communication technology sector in particular, this is leading to the loss of many skilled jobs and is further undermining the eu's global competitiveness in the creation of innovative technological products and services. given the difficult situation faced by european citizens who are being made redundant by companies that are gradually closing down their operations in europe in the context of aggressive globalisation and a severe financial and economic crisis, as is the case with the finns working at microsoft, i believe that the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund is one of the initiatives that the european parliament must support. this fund will provide finnish workers who have recently joined microsoft with access to the necessary advice, guidance and financial resources to help them discover and develop their skills and mobility in a way that they can quickly return to work and overcome the economic difficulties they now face.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to provide support for workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns. in this regard, the main aim of the fund is to help people who have lost their jobs to reintegrate into the labour market. in light of this, the eu should mobilise the fund to support sweden’s submitted application egf/2016/002 se/ericsson for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in the economic sector classified under the nace revision 2 division 26 (manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products). in this case, 918 redundant workers eligible for the egf contribution will have new opportunities to reintegrate into the labour market. it is important to emphasise efforts undertaken by swedish authorities to break traditional gender barriers, including encouraging male beneficiaries to find jobs in the health sector. furthermore, we should welcome the swedish authorities’ efforts to provide a personalised package of training programmes and coaching that will enable most of the redundant employees to find high-quality new jobs. i supported mobilisation of the fund because the swedish authorities have implemented all necessary measures to activate and receive the egf.
in writing. financial support from the european globalisation adjustment fund should be provided to european workers in the information and communication technologies (ict) sector to avoid the risk of them becoming structurally unemployed as a result of the irresponsible liberalisation of the european internal market. in recent years, the trend in the ict sector has been increasingly towards domination of asian producers as well as contractors, due to the low cost of factors of production in this region, such as labour. the swedish company ericsson, in order to remain competitive, followed this trend by closing jobs in sweden at the expense of opening new ones in asia. all this left skilled workers in a situation of structural unemployment, as their skills were no longer in demand on the local swedish market. in this context, i am convinced that if we want the eu to develop in the field of ict and to have no structural unemployment, we must help through the european globalisation adjustment fund workers like those who worked at ericsson until recently.

in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the proposal for a directive on provisional legal aid for suspects or accused persons in custody and legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings, as judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the union is based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions. the application of this principle implies that member states have mutual trust in their criminal justice systems and in the way in which the rights of suspects and accused persons are protected, but differences exist in national practices, including in the interpretation of the right to a fair trial and the provision of effective legal aid. this can be an insurmountable obstacle to the maintenance of fair and effective judicial cooperation in criminal matters and in this sense the proposal for a directive is a positive step towards ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states and the related costs. the criteria for granting legal aid bring greater clarity without leading to full harmonisation, as it would be impossible and unnecessary to provide for detailed legislation at union level, given the differences in the level of costs of legal proceedings in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because there is no doubt that for those suspects, accused and requested persons who lack the necessary financial means, the right to legal advice and legal aid is the only way to take advantage of their right of access to a lawyer. unfortunately, there is a difference in the quality of legal assistance offered by member states. for one reason or another, in some member states fees for the lawyers are too low so that they are not willing to devote enough time and effort to providing high quality legal aid. therefore, the provision that allows suspects, accused and requested persons to show their preference and wishes with regard to their legal aid lawyer should be taken into account and included in the directive. provision should also be made for replacement of the legal aid lawyer, if the suspected, accused or requested person has lost all confidence in the lawyer and can motivate this on verifiable grounds. thus, we will not only reinforce the right to legal aid for suspects, accused and requested persons but will also ensure that they face a fair trial.
in writing. i supported mr young's report because i believe that european citizens who are suspected, detained or charged in a case, as well as those who are wanted on a european arrest warrant, should have the opportunity to seek legal redress before the european courts, even when they do not have sufficient means to provide themselves with legal counsel whenever justice requires it. i believe that the scope of the directive should cover both temporary and ordinary legal aid in all situations. in order to ensure the quality of legal aid provided, states should take the necessary measures to ensure the quality of the service provided in relation to legal aid and to ensure the proper application of the law in a fair process. different interpretations of the right to a 'fair trial', including through the mediation of legal aid, recognised in article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and article 6 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, hamper the provision of cooperation in criminal proceedings. this is why the draft legal aid directive must be adopted as soon as possible.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this dossier because i believe it enhances the rights for citizens and make the text clearer, in particular with the inclusion of the right to ordinary legal aid and not only to provisional legal aid. furthermore, i consider very important the inclusion of a means test and a merits test, which may be used to determine whether a person is eligible for legal aid.
