in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council implementing decision approving the conclusion by the european police office (europol) of the strategic cooperation agreement between the ministry of public security of the people's republic of china and europol. there are clear operational needs for europol's cooperation with china. the information to be exchanged may include expertise, general situational reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation proceedings, information on crime prevention methods, training and advisory activities, support on individual criminal investigations. i believe that china is increasingly important as a source, destination and transit country in the fight against organised crime, such as facilitated illegal immigration, drug trafficking, crime, counterfeiting of euro, infringements of intellectual property rights, corruption in sport, as well as cybercrime and money laundering activities. i support this strategic cooperation agreement with china as it would support and strengthen the fight against organised crime and contribute to enhancing cooperation in the field of international law enforcement.
in writing. ‒ the eu and china are two of the biggest traders in the world. china is the eu’s second largest trading partner and the world’s second fastest growing economy. nevertheless, according to europol, china is increasingly relevant as both source and transit country for organised crime, such as human trafficking, drug related crimes, euro-counterfeiting, intellectual property rights infringements, sport corruption, money laundering and cybercrime. looking from this perspective, the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and china is of great importance because it would aid and reinforce the international fight against organised crime and would contribute to enhancing international law enforcement co-operation. last but not least, it will create a good environment for the development of relations between china and europe.
in writing. i support mr morris' report, as the conclusion of the present europol-china strategic cooperation agreement is of the utmost importance to the eu. the exchange of information on expertise, common situational reports, strategic analyses and information on criminal investigation proceedings will contribute to the fight against illegal migration, trafficking in human beings, organised crime and infringement of intellectual property rights. bulgaria is one of the countries that are the final or intermediate destination of chinese products infringing the intellectual property rights of world-renowned brands. in recent weeks alone, the customs agency has seized over 15,000 watches on suspicion that the items are counterfeit and infringe on the rights of over 25 trademarks. over 1,000 children's toys and 58,000 pairs of work gloves were also seized on suspicion of being counterfeit. the origin of the goods established by the invoices is the people's republic of china. i have supported this agreement because its conclusion would improve and strengthen the fight against organised crime and would contribute to enhancing cooperation in the field of international law enforcement.
in writing. – as a member of the delegation for relations with china in the european parliament i supported this implementing decision. its purpose is to authorise the conclusion of the mutual cooperation agreement between europol and china. i believe that it will benefit both parties as it involves the exchange of operational, strategic and technical information.
in writing. ‒ the cotonou agreement, which underpins the european union's relations with 79 african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries, expires in 2020 the most comprehensive agreement the european union has signed with these countries. it institutionalises and gives a commercial and economic character to the relationship, as well as a political one, within the framework of the general assembly between the eu and the acp. i supported the resolution on the future of acp-eu relations beyond 2020 as it sets out what the future relationship between the two regions should be, namely to improve the efficiency of cooperation and adapt to the challenges of the 21st century. the resolution also calls for the fight against fraud, corruption, poverty and inequality to be eradicated and for the principle of developing country ownership of sustainable development initiatives and projects to be translated into a donor-recipient mentality.
in writing. ‒ acp-eu cooperation is a valuable and important achievement that has strengthened the ties between peoples, states and their parliaments over the past 40 years. adaptation to new challenges is needed to make the partnership between the two parties more effective. i call for the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals (sdgs) to be placed at the centre of the new agreement, and for strong monitoring mechanisms to be established to ensure that the implementation of the agreement contributes to and promotes the sdgs. i believe that cooperation should be in areas of common interest where mutual benefits can be expected, not only in economic terms, but also in terms of peace and security, human rights and the rule of law, good governance and democracy, migration, the environment, climate change and other areas related to the well-being of the acp and eu populations.
in writing. ‒ traditionally, acp-eu relations are on a good level. i supported the resolution, it is important to note that at the core of our current relations is the acp-eu cotonou agreement (2000-20), which aims to promote economic links, trade exchanges and political cooperation at different levels (national, regional and multi-regional). looking from this perspective, it could be argued that acp-eu cooperation is a valuable and unique achievement that has strengthened not only bonds between acp and eu peoples and countries but also has raised public awareness of development issues (promotion of sustainable development, eradication of poverty and inequalities). however, in order to improve the effectiveness of acp-eu cooperation and to address new global challenges such as climate change, poverty, inequalities, migration, peace and security, a new structure (agreement) should be adopted that maintains partnership and relations with the acp countries after 2020. the new agreement should primarily be a political project based on the principle of ownership and clearly leave behind the donor-recipient mentality. the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals (sdgs) would be placed at the centre of the new partnership in order to achieve better results when addressing global challenges.
in writing. the eu's relations with the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries are currently governed by the cotonou agreement, which expires in 2020. given that over 80% of the world's least developed countries are from the acp region and that africa in particular is showing signs of destabilisation that pose an immediate risk to european security, i believe that the form of cooperation between the eu and the acp should be renewed. the new form of cooperation, through the joint parliamentary assembly, should exercise effective control over the funds allocated to acp countries to avoid the possibility of local elites benefiting from them alone. moreover, greater autonomy should be given to local and regional governments and their capacity should be helped to be built so that they can participate in all stages of acp-eu activities from planning to implementation. only in this way will small producers and farmers and civil society be provided with a favourable environment for development and access to quality financing.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the relations between the eu and acp countries need adapt to the political, structural and demographic changes of recent years. in this regard, a framework needs to be established for implementing the new agenda 2030 and achieving the objectives of sustainable development. this report calls for the fight against poverty to remain an overarching objective of acp-eu cooperation.

we are coming together today because europe is looking more and more like a project that lacks enthusiasm. everyone has expectations of the european union, but few have emotions. and we need the enthusiasm of young people to give strength to our project. europe very often looks like an autumn leaf, too exhausted by all the crises. only the enthusiasm of young people can turn the autumn of europe into a spring. through this freedom, young people must experience firsthand the meaning of a united europe, so that they are not so easily swayed by rumors of its untimely end. they're the ones who will most likely defend the project, and they need to know why. sometimes even one day is enough to make you feel something is worthwhile. if an 18-year-old spends even two days in another country, he will know that the absence of borders or their free movement within the european union is an important achievement and one that we must not lose. this free card seems like maybe a little something. yes, it doesn't solve our big problems in the middle east or our relationship with russia, for example, but it can change the lives of many people who will go out, who will blend in with the rest of the world, who will create connections and networks that they will need and will be useful to in the future. not all young europeans have the money to pay for this 'pass'. for many of them, europe is still a foreign country, and if this idea can bring down an iron curtain in front of them, then this project would be a great success.

in writing. ‒ the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important international agreement aimed at finding solutions in situations where the courts of two countries (in the case of parents of two different nationalities) declare themselves competent and each of them gives custody of the child to the parent who is its national. the convention establishes that the competent authorities are those where the child is resident. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of children who have been abducted. the eu now has exclusive external competence in this area and therefore member states no longer act on their own. in this report i propose to give austria and romania the right to accept the accession of peru to this international agreement.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for peru's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. a major problem in cases of international child abduction is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries in cases of parental separation. the convention will help to find a solution at international level to such situations in order to avoid the subjective award of parental rights to the parent who is a national of the state of the court. the court having jurisdiction and the law applicable at the time of the adoption of the convention shall be that of the state in which the child is domiciled. i strongly support the establishment of a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty, which seeks to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and retention across international boundaries by providing a procedure to bring about their prompt return. the treaty has been ratified by all eu member states. in light of this, it is important to note that the eu now has exclusive external competence in this field as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13, which means that member states no longer act on their own account. however, the paradox is that the convention does not provide for autonomous action by international organisations. in this sense, a council decision is necessary to authorise the member states, in particular austria and romania, to accept the accession of peru. therefore, i call both the eu and member states to welcome and accept the accession of peru to the convention because in this manner children’s rights will be protected and preserved.

in writing. ‒ i support the report on the proposal for a council decision authorising certain member states to accept, in the interest of the european union, the accession of the republic of korea to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the convention establishes a system of cooperation among contracting states aimed at settling cases of international child abduction. in many cases, these problems arise because of a separation between parents. if the mother and father are from different countries, it is possible that one of them takes advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries in order to secure the exercise of parental rights over the child. i welcome the accession of south korea to the convention. the commission, together with civil justice experts from the member states, has assessed the functioning of the judicial system of south korea and the country's readiness to implement the convention and considers it desirable that the convention enter into force between the european union and south korea. i support this because the hague convention system works more effectively when more countries join it. there is a significant korean community in europe, which increases the importance of the acceptance of this accession.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty, which seeks to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and retention across international boundaries by providing a procedure to bring about their prompt return. the treaty has been ratified by all eu member states. in light of this, it is important to note that the eu now has exclusive external competence in this field as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13, which means that member states no longer act on their own account. however, the paradox is that the convention does not provide for autonomous action by international organisations. in this sense, a council decision is necessary to authorise the member states (except denmark, which is excluded from the union’s civil justice policy, and czechia, ireland and lithuania, which have already accepted the accession of south korea) to accept the accession of south korea. therefore, i call both the eu and member states to welcome and accept the accession of south korea to the convention because in this manner children’s rights will be protected and preserved.

in writing. ‒ fighting hunger is a priority enshrined in the millennium development goals. as the world population continues to grow, much more effort and innovation will be urgently needed in order to sustainably increase agricultural production, improve the global supply chain, decrease food losses and waste, and ensure that all who are suffering from hunger and malnutrition have access to nutritious food. the eu is a champion among donors in the eradication of hunger and malnutrition and is committed to reduce the numbers of people who face hunger and malnutrition by at least 7 million by 2025. however, progress in reducing malnutrition remains too slow; 795 million people in the world currently do not get enough food to lead a decent and active life. therefore, the eu should continue to support and invest in smallholder farmers to boost food production, achieve nutrition security and sustainable agriculture. in addition to this, the eu should assist smallholder farmers in the development and access to local markets, local value chain and local food processing facilities. in order to facilitate the process even further the union should provide education and training to smallholder farmers.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the european public prosecutor's office and eurojust. it is based on two oral questions by the libe committee on the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office (article 86 tfeu) and the possible reform of eurojust. the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office touches on the subject of member states' sovereignty, as its purpose will be to investigate and punish financial fraud and other crimes affecting the financial interest of the eu. at present, only the national authorities of the member states have such powers within their territories, and existing european agencies such as olaf, europol and eurojust do not have the powers to conduct a european investigation. my group and i believe that at this stage the best results in the fight against crime affecting the eu's financial interests can be achieved at national level and through the existing frameworks for coordination and cooperation between member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, as it is crucial that the eu and its member states detect and prosecute fraud affecting the eu's financial interests in an effective and dissuasive manner, thus protecting the taxpayers of all member states contributing to the union budget. organised cross-border crime has increased over the past decade and is committed by highly mobile groups operating in multiple member states and committing different types of crime. in this context, i welcome parliament's support for the establishment of an effective and independent european public prosecutor's office (eppo) in order to reduce the existing fragmentation of national law enforcement efforts to protect the eu budget, thereby strengthening the fight against fraud in the european union. the eppo should be able to exercise its powers in accordance with the applicable law. the european public prosecutor's office should be able to provide the necessary support to the eppo in the event of a dispute arising from the use of the national unit.
in writing. ‒ back in 2013, the commission presented a proposal to reform eurojust, together with a proposal to establish a european public prosecutor’s office (eppo). in general, the commission’s proposal for the establishment of eppo aims to provide support to eurojust in the fight against fraud to the eu. thus, it also aims to increase the democratic legitimacy of eurojust. close cooperation between eurojust and the future eppo on an operational and administrative level is essential to ensure effective and efficient work in practice. in this context, compatible provisions in both regulations are essential for legal certainty and consistency and will help to realise the full potential of eurojust and the eppo. moreover, in order to ensure judicial coordination from the outset of investigations and prosecutions, eurojust and the eppo should inform each other of relevant cases. therefore, strong information exchange between eurojust and eppo should be developed.

in writing. ‒ in light of the recent caterpillar and alstom cases, the first point that needs to be taken into account is that the eu should immediately mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egaf) in order to support workers who lost their jobs and give them new opportunities to reintegrate into the labour market. furthermore, the eu and its member states should find a common vision for european industry because the sector is shrinking and cannot maintain its global competitiveness. today european industrial production accounts 24% of world production while during the 1990s it accounted for 36%. unfortunately, declining industry (deindustrialisation) of europe has resulted in job losses for employees, failure of smes and economic decline. therefore, the eu should develop consistent and comprehensive industrial policy, which aims to reindustrialise europe. importantly, reindustrialisation of europe should be based on digitalisation (in particular the integration of smart technologies and robotics into industrial value chains), sustainability, energy efficiency and adequate resources. member states should join efforts and facilitate the emergence of joint industrial projects. in general, reindustrialisation of the eu will create jobs, economic growth and regional integration.

in writing. ‒ the report refers to the closure of the caterpillar plant in belgium, which would result in the collective redundancies of over 2000 employees and put an additional 7,000 jobs at risk, and to the closure of the caterpillar 'monkstown' plant in newtownabbey, northern ireland, which would result in the loss of 250 jobs. the report calls on the commission to mobilise the european social fund and the european globalisation adjustment fund rapidly to reintegrate workers made redundant by caterpillar. it also calls on the commission and the member states to ensure better access to finance for eu businesses, especially micro and smes. we need a long-term vision for european industry.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the automated data exchange with regard to fingerprint data in denmark, as the state has fully complied with the general data protection provisions, from which it should have the right to receive and supply personal data. i believe that automated exchange will help cross-border cooperation, increase the security and protection of citizens and help security structures in the fight against cross-border crime, and in particular against persons posing a threat to national security, persons engaged in illegal activity and misuse of personal data.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this agreement. i approve of the visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic passports.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i support the agreement between the european union and china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports, as the agreement reached is in the interest of the union and meets the negotiating objectives set by the council. the agreement provides for the abolition of visas for short-term visits to the eu only for holders of diplomatic passports and contains the necessary safeguards in respect of cases of abuse. the commission has also proposed that the visa waiver for holders of european diplomatic passports be applied to all citizens of the union. on the eu side, according to the commission, this concerns between 100 and 120 thousand passports in circulation, while on the chinese side the data is for 30 thousand passports in circulation. therefore, i believe that the agreement will benefit the relationship between china and the european union, which further conditionalizes its support.
in writing. ‒ i support the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the people's republic of china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. the agreement supports our strategic partnership with china and will facilitate bilateral exchanges and closer cooperation, as well as being an expression of goodwill on both sides. the abolition of visas will reduce the waiting time at consulates and the costs associated with travel. it will facilitate people-to-people contacts, an important condition for the stable development of economic, cultural, scientific and other links.
in writing. ‒ the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the union holding a valid diplomatic passport or an eu laissez-passer and for citizens of china holding a valid diplomatic passport when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party, for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. looking from this perspective, it can be argued that the agreement has great importance since it has been the first international agreement between the eu and china in the field of home affairs. in light of this, the agreement represents a real opportunity for both sides to develop economic, cultural, scientific and other ties between them. therefore, i fully support it. last but not least, i would like to stress strongly that visa liberalisation should go hand-in-hand with improvements in protection and promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. – china is a major partner of the european union. as a member of the delegation for china i supported this agreement, because i believe that the abolishment of visas will facilitate and intensify people-to-people contact (an essential condition for the steady development of economic, cultural, scientific and other ties) and reduce the waiting time in front of consulates.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report with the proposal for a regulation on financial management for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. i believe that increased eu co-financing will help countries experiencing budgetary difficulties to allocate funds for additional investment in regional policy projects and will have a positive effect on the economy of these countries. in the context of the financial and economic crisis, countries are forced to take measures of financial restraint in order to stabilise their national budgets. additional funding from the commission will support countries that are still experiencing severe economic difficulties and are at risk of not being able to benefit fully from the european structural and investment funds.
in writing. ‒ as a result of the 'tightening-up' policy imposed at european level, a large proportion of public investment in member states experiencing budgetary difficulties has been discontinued. against this background, the european structural and investment funds (esif) have become a major driver of the economy in those countries where the private sector has refused to invest following the global financial and economic crisis. i believe that if the eu is to emerge from the crisis it is in, it must provide adequate assistance to the member states, not abandon them in times of difficulty. i am of the opinion that the possible suspension of the esi funds in economies that have been experiencing serious financial difficulties for almost a decade will not only deepen the crisis in these countries but also trigger a chain reaction in other parts of europe. this is why i support the amendments to articles 24 and 120 of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 which do not interrupt the esi funds for member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties, but on the contrary help to maximise the investment opportunities provided in the 2014-2020 programming period.
in writing. – among my priorities is the promotion of funding and investment opportunities for projects in the member states. in this regard i consider it important to ensure the smooth implementation of one of the main eu funding tools, the european structural and investment funds (esif). for this and other reasons i supported the commission’s proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. although the negotiations took a while, a firm position on not extending the categories for data collection etc. was successfully upheld. this enabled us to prevent the commission’s proposal from exceeding its scope. i support the agreement to improve access to available data through better cooperation and statistical activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because there is no doubt that the eu needs statistics and data on transport infrastructure and rail transport of passengers as well as on rail accidents in order to ensure the monitoring and development of the common transport policy and preparatory measures in the field of transport safety. i warmly welcome the signing of the two memoranda of understanding (mous) between eurostat and the commission (27 april 2016) and between eurostat and the era (12 may 2016). mous are important instruments for optimising the use of existing information and avoiding overlapping between eurostat, the commission and the european railway agency (era). they will ensure that statistical data related to eu policies are easily accessible to eu citizens and stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ a key objective of european rail policy is to establish a fast, safe, secure and energy-efficient transport system that is comfortable for passengers and provides good conditions for the development of a european industry that creates jobs and economic prosperity. to achieve this, the eu needs to analyse a certain amount of data to help develop a streamlined strategy that takes account of the development of rail transport in the different member states. in this context, a key motivation for the amendment of the regulation is to simplify data collection in order to reduce unnecessary duplicate statistics. this will allow a more efficient distribution of the data collection work between member states, national statistical authorities, representatives of the railway sector and the competent european authorities. this in turn will go hand in hand with the faster development of a streamlined eu rail strategy. i supported the amendment of this regulation because i believe that the rationalization of the european rail strategy will save funds which have not been used optimally so far.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that good statistics will help create a well-functioning common transport policy and system. i supported a solution based largely on the signing of two memoranda of understanding, i.e. (1) between eurostat and the european railway agenda and (2) between eurostat and dg move, in order to guarantee the availability of data on ertms, the accessibility of stations to persons with reduced mobility and disabled persons, and on cross-border sections.
in writing. ‒ the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1365/2006 will encourage the collection of statistical data not only for the transport of goods by inland waterways but also for the transport of passengers. the collection of statistics on passenger transport is an important addition as it will contribute to the study of the development of inland waterway transport and in particular river tourism. to date, research on inland waterway transport has remained underdeveloped compared to other modes of transport such as sea, air and road. the commission notes that the measure is not imputable to the state and that the state has not provided any evidence to support its claim that the measure is imputable to the state. this puts my country, bulgaria, in a particular situation, as it is a major part of pan-european transport corridor no 7, which runs through the rhine-main-danube river channel. bulgaria has a 471 km stretch of the danube river, which runs through a number of beautiful bulgarian cities and provides an opportunity for international travel. however, the lack of statistics on passenger transport in europe by inland waterways prevents my country from analysing in detail the opportunities that can be derived from the development of river tourism. that is why i am in favour of amending this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the union legislative framework for customs offences and penalties because, although the directive represents a step forward by introducing more flexibility to the original proposal, i am highly sceptical of the approach the european commission has chosen to take.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for a directive on the union legislative framework for customs offences and penalties. compared to domestic law, customs infringements are treated in 28 different ways in the 28 member states. this leads to revenue losses for member states and trade distortions. i support the intention to establish in this directive a list of acts which would be considered as infringements of union customs legislation, because this will ensure transparency and the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because there is a real need for eu’s legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions. this need has been dictated by the fact that there is still no integrated approach for the enforcement of customs legislation, which consequently means that the rules are the same but when those rules are infringed, the applied sanctions significantly differ in member states. undoubtedly, these differences create a lack of mutual trust among member states’ administrations, which is not good for the functioning of the customs union and the single market. therefore, the eu should develop a common approach that enforces customs legislation. importantly, a proportionate system of sanctions should be in place in order to ensure that customs legislation is fully and correctly enforced. last but not least, the eu should urge member states to work towards improvement of the interaction and performance of customs administrations, ensuring controls with equivalent results and protection of the financial interests of the union.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report as it aims to harmonise the approach for the enforcement of customs legislation, particularly for infringement sanctions. this will help remove the inconsistency within the eu customs union and uncertainty for businesses. the ep report provides more flexibility to member states and their customs authorities, as following epp suggestion the report foresees the possibility for the member states to impose criminal sanctions, in accordance with national laws, instead of non-criminal sanctions provided by the directive where the nature and gravity of the infringement so requires.
in writing. ‒ i think that the increase in the budget for the security of the staff of the european institutions is justified. so far, i personally don't think the institutions are well protected, and if the funds are the reason, let's put a little more money in. of course, but let's use them properly and track their application. uncontrolled funds are easily lost. i'm also going to vote for a bigger budget for the security of every single citizen, because we see that as one of our major challenges today. but the better solution will always be to root out the problem, which my party and i have fought so hard to do.
in writing. – i supported draft amending budget no 3/2016 because it proposes to reinforce the security budget by a total amount of eur 15.8 million in the european schools, the european parliament, the european commission, the court of justice, the european court of auditors, the european economic and social committee, the committee of the regions and the european external action service. there is no doubt that the budget for security should be increased particularly in the wake of the november 2015 attacks in paris and those of march 2016 in brussels. another argument in support for security budget increase is the fact that eu institutions have reviewed their security needs and have found security lapses that should be addressed in short to medium term.
in writing. ‒ the signing of the agreement with iran is a huge step forward in the normalisation of our relations with that country. i fully support the lifting of sanctions against iran. these sanctions were an expression of the eu's clerical foreign policy, which favoured not the interests of the eu member states but those of the us and israel. however, i decided to vote against the resolution on the eu's strategy towards iran after the nuclear deal, as i do not agree with some of the extreme statements in the text, such as that a comprehensive agreement should be signed with iran, requiring it to accept western norms and values and change its structure and traditions. we've seen what the imposition of western values has done to countries like afghanistan, iraq, libya, and right now, it's happening in syria.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the joint comprehensive plan of action (jcpoa), also known as the iran nuclear deal, is a remarkable achievement that should not only lead to a significant improvement in eu-iran relations, but also promote stability in the entire region. both sides should work closely together on bilateral and multilateral issues to ensure greater stability in the region and effective implementation of the nuclear deal. i believe that eu-iran relations should be developed through a multi-layered dialogue involving political, diplomatic, economic, academic and interpersonal contacts involving civil society representatives and human rights defenders. trade and renewed access to the world trading system provide an opportunity to overcome iran's isolation. this can be an important tool to strengthen political dialogue and foster cooperation between countries in the region, with a view to accelerating regional development and increasing employment and stability in the wider region. i call for full gender equality, i welcome attempts to draft legislation to protect women from violence and i hope that the newly elected parliament will consider legislation that fully criminalises violence against women.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that the completion of the iran nuclear deal is a great success for the international community. on the one hand, it represents a triumph of diplomacy over nuclear proliferation, and on the other, it serves as a good basis for the development of cooperation and constructive dialogue between the european union and iran. in fact, the european union and iran can cooperate in a number of areas, with an emphasis on the development of trade. but it takes concrete steps to promote it. iran needs to work and focus on respecting human rights, improving the situation of ethnic minorities, ensuring free access to the internet and abolishing the death penalty. in addition, the country should focus on reforms by liberalising its economy and improving the business climate in the country. i believe that in the long term, deepening the eu-iran relationship will contribute to promoting peace and stability throughout the region, including the resolution of the military conflicts in syria and yemen.
in writing. – i supported this strategy as i believe that the joint comprehensive plan of action (jcpoa), was a notable achievement for multilateral diplomacy, and for european diplomacy in particular. the strategy can help promote stability across the whole region while at the same time it makes a substantial improvement in eu-iran relations possible. with this report, parliament calls on the government of iran to address the substantive concerns on the situation of human rights in iran, as well as the specific calls to action found in resolutions of the un general assembly.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report by mrs ferrara on the fight against corruption and the actions resulting from the resolution of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, as it contains some points with which i cannot agree. one of them is the call for concrete action at eu level, which i believe is contrary to the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i support the report on the fight against corruption and the actions to combat organised crime and money laundering, as i believe that we really need a review of the existing legislation to fight organised crime and corruption in order to optimise it, more police and judicial cooperation at european level, improving the sharing of information between law enforcement services and europol and the creation of an effective european prosecutor's office with clearly defined powers to support national authorities. according to the report, the irregularities detected in 2014 with regard to the european budget amounted to eur 538 million. this value reflects only the actual irregularities committed and does not take into account the negative impact of phenomena such as corruption, money laundering, tax avoidance. i therefore call again on the council to examine the remaining points of dispute and to adopt a decision on the proposal for the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, the proposal for a directive on the fight against fraud affecting the financial interests of the union and the proposal for a regulation on the eurojust criminal justice cooperation agency.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the fight against corruption and the actions resulting from the resolution of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, as i share the view that a revision of the legislative framework is necessary to overcome any shortcomings in the fight against organised crime and corruption and to improve cross-border judicial cooperation. it is necessary to provide for effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions against the unlawful acquisition of any financial and/or material benefit. organised crime, corruption and money laundering usually have a cross-border dimension, which requires close cooperation between competent national authorities and between national authorities and relevant eu agencies, and the regulation will contribute to enhanced police and judicial cooperation at european level. the adopted regulation creates a realistic environment to prevent organised crime and corruption from entering the legal economy and calls for the introduction of a comprehensive eu-wide 'electronic public procurement' system to reduce the risk of corruption in public procurement.
in writing. ‒ transnational organised crime and corruption constitute major global issues. looking from this perspective, the fight against both issues should be a top priority for the eu and its member states. we should adopt and support common european action plan for fighting organised crime and corruption. there are several reasons for this. firstly, the european action plan for fighting organised crime and corruption will facilitate effectively police and judicial cooperation between member states. secondly, it will break down national boundaries recognising the added value that the european legislation have. thirdly, it will provide law enforcement authorities at european level with the necessary tools to properly fight organised crime group across europe. last but not least, in order our fight against organised crime and corruption to be effective, the member states should set up secure and effective mechanisms in the current institutional framework to ensure that investigations into organised crime are properly coordinated and that mutual trust among law enforcement authorities in the member states is fostered.
in writing. ‒ i supported mrs ferrara's report because organised crime is a global threat to european citizens, requiring a common, coordinated response by the eu and its member states. organized crime groups have a wide range of activities, and one of their main characteristics is their rapid adaptation to different geographical, economic and social conditions and their weaknesses. a large proportion of the illicit proceeds of crime are laundered into the european economy. it should be noted that corruption and money laundering usually have a cross-border dimension, which requires close cooperation between the competent national authorities, as well as between national authorities and the relevant eu agencies. the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office would contribute to the fight against corruption in the eu and to the control of misuse of the eu's financial interests. the counterfeiting of various products in the eu, drug trafficking, tax evasion and organised crime and terrorism are just some of the activities of organised crime groups that we need to tackle. bulgaria is one of the countries that still has a high rate of organised crime, the level of corruption also remains high. i therefore believe that a multidisciplinary approach and the development of effective and innovative european legislation are needed to address these challenges.
in writing. – i supported this report as corruption and organised crime in the european union is a major problem that holds back the development of the national and eu initiatives and the well—being of eu citizens. this report analyses the current situation in the eu regarding the fight against crime and makes proposals for combating new forms of crimes with european instruments.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on human rights and migration to third countries. it contains a number of problematic points with which i cannot agree. among the main problems is the complete lack of distinction between the concepts of 'migrant' and 'refugee'. they are in no way interchangeable and it is unacceptable to put a sign of equality. the text repeatedly observes that rights normally granted to 'refugees' are extended to migrants, while making no distinction between legal and illegal migrants. the report also calls for the creation of 'safe and legal' migration routes. europe cannot afford to encourage migration, because many countries are already having major problems with their social systems, their security systems, etc.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, in recent years, many people have been forced to leave their countries and become migrants on account of conflicts, extreme poverty and particularly human rights violations. far more disturbing, however, is the fact that as migrants they continue to face human rights violations in numerous countries of transit or destination. the eu and its member states should lead by example in promotion and protection of the human rights of migrants, notably within their own borders, in order to be credible partners when discussing migration and human rights with third countries. therefore, the eu should identify specific actions that member states should take to combat xenophobia and to facilitate social integration of migrants. with regard to human rights and migration in third countries, the eu should use various policy instruments in its relations with developing countries in order to protect human rights/rights of migrants there. in this context, the eu and its member states should incorporate migration issues as a component of the political dialogue with third countries. the eu also should provide technical assistance to improve national and local human rights/migrants policies in third countries. last but not least, the eu should work actively with ngos and civil society in third countries.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries. this report shall promote the adoption of the un guiding principles and support their implementation worldwide. i believe it is important for companies to apply the un guiding principles, including by establishing due diligence policies and risk management safeguards, and by providing effective remedies where their activities have led to or contributed to adverse human rights impacts. i consider it necessary for member states to adopt a coherent, comprehensive, effective and binding approach in their legislative work so as to fulfil their obligation to prevent, investigate and sanction human rights violations committed by corporations under their jurisdiction, including those committed in third countries, and to compensate victims.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution. there are reports that stress that transnational corporations and other business enterprises may at times cause or contribute to human rights violations in third countries, particularly affecting vulnerable groups such as minorities, indigenous people, women and children. unfortunately, nowadays human rights violations by corporations are a worldwide concern. it is important to note that many transnational corporations, whether european or not, operating in third countries, have substantial business operations in europe and/or may be owned by european corporations, have assets or goods in europe, or control other corporations in europe, or receive investments or use the financial services of institutions in europe. in this context, the eu and the member states should lay down clear rules setting out that companies established in their territory or under their jurisdiction must respect human rights throughout their operations, in every country and context in which they operate, and in relation to their business relationships, including outside the eu. thus, in this manner, the eu will have a leading role in setting up of clear liability standards for corporate involvement in human rights abuses.
in writing. – the report highlights the increasing role of corporations in ensuring respect for human rights. it acknowledges that trade agreements can contribute to reinforcing the global rules-based trading system as well as human rights provisions. in this regard it recognises the major importance of corporate social responsibility and welcomes the growing use of instruments based on companies’ self-commitment. for this among other reasons i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and its storage has a significant role to play in achieving the ultimate goal of a european energy union. given that gas imports from russia were 7% higher in 2015 than in 2014 and that 41% of imports of natural gas from non-eu countries were from russia in 2015, it is necessary to put in place effective solutions to reduce the dependence on russian gas. the eu and eastern europe in particular need diversification of energy supplies, and this can be achieved through better coordination of national energy policies and the creation of an energy union with a single energy market and a common external policy. i believe it is important to promote the most efficient use of existing liquefied natural gas (lng) terminals before supporting new regasification terminals.
in writing. ‒ the eu is the largest energy importer in the world, importing more than half (54%) of the energy it consumes. this means the eu continues to be highly dependent on gas and oil imports from authoritarian regimes. therefore, the establishment of an energy union is an important step on the road to achieve energy security through diversification of energy sources and energy routes to europe. in a long term perspective, the establishment of the energy union will ensure that all eu citizens have secure, equal and affordable energy supply. in this context, the current developments on global liquefied natural gas (lng) markets present a major opportunity for the eu to deliver lower energy costs, security and resilience to eu consumers. therefore, the eu should focus its efforts on promotion and development of new lng terminals, distribution systems, interconnectors, transmission corridors and storage stations. lng is a particularly important element for the establishment of the energy union and will contribute significantly towards ending any kind of energy isolation or dependence of the eu member states and eu regions.
in writing. ‒ natural gas will play an important role, at least for the next few decades, for eu energy and industry, the integration of renewables and the shift towards a low-carbon economy based on clean energy sources. the eu's dependence on natural gas imports is growing and alternative sources and supply routes are needed to ensure energy security. in the field of transport, without natural gas, it is unlikely that an environmental breakthrough will be made. this requires a strategic approach to lng and gas storage as an element of our security, competitiveness and manageability of our energy dependence. i therefore fully support the ideas proposed in the report on taking account of the accessibility of lng terminals in eu cross-border gas infrastructure projects, on making the most efficient use of existing infrastructure, on a regionally and geographically balanced approach to project prioritisation. it is clear that we will neither reduce our dependence on the dominant supplier nor be able to build a market with competitive opportunities if lng and storage do not start to play a stronger role in creating the single gas market. i also support the strong texts relating to the potential of liquefied gas as an alternative fuel for land and water transport, which can easily contribute to reducing harmful emissions from transport.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for this report. i welcome the fact that it proposes to simplify and improve eu legislation in order to make it easier to enforce existing rules and tackle the current shortcomings. as it is, the current situation demands a number of improvements, especially when it comes to scope, training, control procedures and sanctions. because the report correctly recognises the importance of member states in all of these matters, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on how to standardise fisheries control in europe. the importance of ensuring effective control of fishing activities in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of living marine resources and to maintain a level playing field should be emphasised. it is necessary for member states to ensure the effective application of the control regulation. the introduction of european training for inspectors and the development of a common control model is of key importance. the training of fishermen should also be strengthened. it could be promoted and carried out through their professional organisations to improve understanding of the meaning and benefits of the rules and controls and to enhance the culture of compliance. it is also necessary to create online databases to make the rules accessible and understandable to all. i believe that fish auctions play a vital role in the seafood industry and are central to the control of landed fish. the eu's ambitious fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing worldwide must be combined with effective enforcement of the control regulation in our own waters.
in writing. ‒ european fishermen have the greatest stake in the sustainable management of living marine resources in the seas and oceans, whose reproduction is threatened by current overfishing conditions. however, unfair market competition in the fisheries sector, which is expressed in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, makes the future of the european fisherman's livelihood uncertain. i therefore support this resolution, which seeks to strengthen and standardise fisheries control in europe by insisting on strengthening the mandate of the european fisheries control agency. in order to reduce the risk of marine species extinction caused by illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, the european fisheries control agency needs to be able to apply common control, inspection and surveillance standards and to facilitate operational cooperation between member states through joint deployment plans. this resolution takes a step in this direction by encouraging the implementation of the agency's 'training programme' for fisheries inspectors, which standardises training and control procedures in this sector and will serve as a reference for countries wishing to train their fisheries inspectors in the future.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on improving the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. this is the first detailed document devoted entirely to transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. it is important to give equal attention to all transport corridors, regardless of where they are located in europe, in order to stimulate their potential.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on improving connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the conditions for the participation of third countries in union programmes in the field of research and technological development, in particular in the framework of the european research area. this will also help to make better use of existing regional cooperation policies and instruments such as european territorial cooperation (etc), interreg and european territorial cooperation groups (etcs). member states ensuring a high degree of transparency and control over eu spending should also be encouraged to adopt or continue to apply measures to move towards greener transport options.
in writing. ‒ connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure have a major impact on the economic growth, economic competitiveness, employment and territorial cohesion of the eu and its regions. unfortunately, nowadays central and eastern europe’s transport infrastructure is still undeveloped and significantly lags behind the one in western europe. undeveloped infrastructure is one of the reasons why central and eastern eu member states have slow economic growth and have not been attractive for foreign investors. therefore, the eu has been providing financial help to its central and eastern member states in order to improve and develop transport infrastructure. in this regard, there are several important points and priorities that should be taken into account. firstly, member states in central and eastern europe should foster coordination and synergy between european structural and investment (esi) funds, the connecting europe facility (cef), horizon 2020, the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) and eib and ebrd resources when implementing projects. secondly, member states should develop north-south transparent corridors and extend ten-t corridors, in particular projects such as via carpathia and rail baltica. thirdly, member states in central and eastern europe should improve connections between different transport modes in order to reduce prices for passenger and freight transport and to take into account ecological and social concerns.
in writing. ‒ i support this report on improving connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe because of the support it gives to the development of rail transport in the region of my country, bulgaria. given that the rail network in central and eastern europe is considerably less developed than in the rest of europe, i believe that its modernisation should be a top priority for the eu. the development of rail transport in this part of the old continent will have a positive impact on industry, freight transport, the quality of public services and tourism. this in turn will create conditions for economic growth and many jobs in countries like bulgaria. moreover, in addition to economic benefits, the improvement of rail infrastructure in the region will increase the mobility of european citizens from different member states, which will favour the level of social cohesion in the eu. finally, it is also important to note that rail transport is one of the most environmentally friendly modes of transport and its development must accompany any economy that seeks to be sustainable.
in writing. – as a european citizen and representative from bulgaria i supported this ini report as i believe that there is a need for further boost to improve the cross-border connectivity along the north-south direction between the member states in central and eastern europe. furthermore, it should also be recognized that the region’s potential for inland waterway transport ought to be further utilised, especially along the danube river. there is also significant potential for further developing shipping to the maritime ports in the baltic and black seas, not least in the energy sector.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report with recommendations to the commission to set up an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights because i believe that the ideas it proposes for treaty changes de facto run counter to the principle of subsidiarity. i also fear that the mechanisms proposed in this way could be used to exert political pressure on sovereign member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report containing recommendations to the commission on the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, as the european union has put democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights at the heart of its core principles and objectives. the community has a wide range of instruments for implementing its laws and treaties where substantive issues are concerned, but not so much when it comes to implementing the obligations of the treaties with regard to democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. attempts by the commission to remind a member state of its commitments are often met with reluctance or outright refusal to recognise the eu's generally accepted rules and powers to enforce them, and its intervention has so far been timid and arbitrary. although the eu has a number of existing instruments to guarantee fundamental principles and rights, there are still significant gaps and in practice these instruments often prove to be limited in scope, insufficient and ineffective, or unlikely to be used. instead of creating new procedures, an interinstitutional agreement is proposed, building on existing instruments, with its scope extended by a reporting, notification and sanctioning mechanism.
in writing. ‒ today, more than ever, the eu needs a comprehensive mechanism to guarantee democracy, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the fundamental rights and freedoms of union citizens. this need is dictated by the current level of integration in the eu and recent events in some member states. in recent years, there has been a negative trend in a number of countries to violate eu law, thereby de facto violating the fundamental rights and freedoms of european citizens, who are not always fully informed, and this is an even more serious problem. unfortunately, my native bulgaria is no exception. due to an undemocratic legal restriction in the bulgarian electoral code, i myself was fined for the fact that i used a few words in my native language during an election campaign in bulgaria. and the right of every citizen of the union to express messages and opinions in the language of his or her choice should be guaranteed. in this context, i fully support the creation of the eu mechanism in question, because it will guarantee that european citizens are treated equally, but also monitor the application of european law by member states.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the establishment of an interinstitutional agreement on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, as it will ensure respect for these principles through a representative group of independent experts, based on a quantitative and qualitative review of the available data and information provided by all member states. in addition, the eu pact for democracy provides for the preparation of an annual democracy report containing country-specific recommendations. the adoption of the report marks the beginning of the interparliamentary debate on the follow-up to the european democracy report. on the basis of the report, the commission may decide to initiate a 'systemic infringement' procedure under article 2 teu and article 258 tfeu by bringing together several infringement procedures. i support the resolution because i believe that the eu pact will remove the scepticism towards my country as a reliable business partner and the critical view of current non-compliance with eu law that exists in other member states.
in writing. – democracy and rule of law and fundamental rights are core values for the eu. given the challenges ahead of the union we have observed that some member states have weakened their promotion of these values. for this reason i voted in favour of this report, in line with the epp’s stance that the mechanism to be created must fit into the current treaties’ framework and must be legally sound.
in writing. the european commission has committed to focusing on the important issues and listening more to the concerns of its citizens in 2017. the work programme that juncker presented for the coming year has the ambition to take concrete actions that will bring about tangible changes in people's lives. the eu is going through the worst economic crisis since its creation, which also has a serious social dimension. today, more than ever, the union is faced with unacceptably high levels of unemployment, poverty and social inequalities, and young people have no prospects for development. the recovery of the european economy must at all costs be balanced against the need for a more social europe. in this context, i welcome the commission's decision to establish a european pillar of social rights. it is high time that due attention was paid to the need to ensure a work-life balance for working families. however, the commission should also consider concrete actions to reduce child poverty and ensure equal access to quality education and pre-school training. there are 26 million children in the eu at risk of poverty and social exclusion, and this statistic is absolutely incompatible with our claims to development and civilization.

in writing. three years after the start of the current programming period, europe is in a much different situation, characterised by new challenges and priorities. today, the multiannual financial framework is being implemented in the context of the migration crisis, threats to internal security and still unacceptably high levels of youth unemployment, which require significant additional funding from the european budget. to address these challenges, specific instruments have been mobilised in recent years, maximising the potential of the current multiannual financial framework. all this shows that the mid-term review of the framework is extremely timely and necessary. the current budgetary difficulties further threaten the already highly shaken confidence of citizens in the european union. it is therefore important that member states take their responsibility and back up their words with deeds, ensuring a predictable and reliable eu budget for the remaining years of the current programming period. in this context of the mid-term review, the question of replenishing the european budget with genuine autonomous own resources to replace the current system of national contributions should also be given serious consideration.
in writing. – the digital single market aims at bringing people together. for many of us, going online is the quickest and most convenient way of getting informed. however this is not a reality for around one fifth of the eu population. a great deal of the public sector bodies’ websites are not fit for use by people with disabilities, such as hearing and vision impairment. the swift implementation of the accessibility of public sector bodies’ websites directive will empower european consumers with disabilities to access information and public services available online. i invite the european commission to keep a close eye on the process of implementation. at the same time, however this process should not pose disproportionate burden on eu member states. the european parliament managed to keep the text realistic and reasonable, which i believe will help the smooth work-on-the-ground of this directive. i would like to thank all colleagues involved in the negotiations, who managed to widen the scope to all public sector bodies and also to include the mobile sites and applications. this is a step towards enabling people with disabilities to access the public sector bodies’ websites anywhere at any time and also a key step to future-proof this directive.

in writing. ‒ i supported the creation of a directive on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications, as it aims to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states on the accessibility of public authorities' websites. it lays down harmonised technical requirements which are essential for citizens' participation in economic and social life and for the full enjoyment of their rights. the accessibility of the public institutions' websites will be subject to constant monitoring. the adopted directive primarily concerns the websites of tax authorities, employment offices, social security institutions and those providing services such as the issuing of passports and driving licences, vehicle registration, the issuing of building permits, birth certificates and civil marriage. the scope also includes health-related services such as interactive advice, online services and booking a doctor's appointment, as well as those related to education university application, access to library catalogues.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that we should approve the directive on the accessibility of the websites and mobile application of public sector bodies. it is our moral duty to guarantee that people with disabilities will have better access to information published on the websites and mobile applications of public services. thus, in this matter, we will not only help europeans with disabilities to participate fully in society but also will make another step in the process of building of eu digital society.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a regulation on protective measures against plant pests, as their health is a key factor for sustainable and competitive agriculture, horticulture and forestry. healthy seeds and planting material are necessary for productive crops and for jobs, innovation in crop production and food security. the adopted legislation aims to protect european agriculture and forestry by preventing the introduction and spread of alien pests, also taking into account invasive alien species, under the mechanism provided for in the eu biodiversity strategy. it also lays down the basic provisions for quarantine stations where the use of such stations is required by the same or a secondary act. the introduction of a condition requiring that exports of plants, plant products and other objects to third countries be carried out in a strictly defined order is also new. the requirements for the introduction of plants through travellers' luggage are also updated as existing loopholes are becoming a growing risk to the phytosanitary status of the union. an electronic notification and reporting system shall be established.

five to national budgets.

in writing. ‒ i supported the joint resolution of the political groups on the european voluntary service and the promotion of volunteering in europe, despite some reservations, but in the name of consensus. i do not think that we should ask member states to define a legal environment for volunteering, because each of them should decide for itself whether to do so or not, but since the word 'encourages' is used in the resolution, i felt that this resolution should be supported, which can only reinforce the affirmation of the importance of volunteering. it is hoped that more young people will be willing to participate in such activities and that the funds allocated will be used properly and efficiently.
i am convinced that youth policies cannot exist on their own. synergies between the european union youth strategy and other policies are needed. it must be in sync with education and training, health and employment policies. in the same vein, i believe that the opinion of young people and the expertise of youth organisations must be taken into account when formulating and evaluating the strategy. in this connection, i share an opinion that is recorded in the report of the european youth forum. they believe that 57% of the expertise of youth organisations is not taken into account. i believe that their contribution should carry more weight, especially as they are the main provider of key skills and competences. in conclusion, i believe that the priorities that should be in the strategy for the next three years are to invest in horizontal skills such as entrepreneurship and digital literacy. i supported the report because i believe that young people should be at the heart of european policies.

in writing. – i have voted in favour of this resolution because youth is a topic that is very close to my heart. i wish first of all to underline my attachment to the reference to actively involving youth in policy and to empowering them. as an mep, i try to contribute by initiatives aimed at young people to promote citizenship and to seek solutions to challenges such as youth unemployment. therefore, i am happy with the reference to structured dialogue as well as the suggestion to involve local and regional authorities in the area of youth policy. secondly, i welcome the many references to eu programmes and eu funding aimed at employment and education of young people, especially eramus and erasmus+ programmes, the youth employment initiative, erasmus for young entrepreneurs programme and youth guarantee. i encourage eu institutions to simplify administration procedures and invest in communication so that a maximum of young people can benefit from these tools.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the evaluation of the eu youth strategy (2013 2015). i believe that young people should be actively involved in the planning, development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all youth policies. in addition, youth policies and national strategies should be developed in conjunction with and for the benefit of young people. member states should make full use of available eu policies, national policies and financial frameworks to promote appropriate investment in young people and the creation of quality and secure jobs. i welcome the fact that more than eur 12.4 billion from the european social fund (esf) and the youth employment initiative (yei) has been earmarked to tackle youth unemployment in the new programming period. i believe that a better understanding of eu values, the functioning of the eu and european diversity is crucial both to fostering participation in the democratic process and to promoting active civic participation among young people. it is important to note that young people and youth organisations need to be involved in shaping the priorities and a new eu framework for cooperation on youth after 2018.
