in writing. ‒ i voted against this report. it is clear, that there are certain aspects of the cap, which should be improved, such as simplifying the cap for individual farmers by providing better access to services and promoting research. however, the report is often overly prescriptive and in disregard of the important role of member states in this matter. especially when it comes to taxation and security, it is up to the member states to decide. furthermore, whilst i would gladly support improvements on the cap, the report also goes way beyond the current debate and issues on some matters, which in my opinion, are not realistic at this point.
in writing. ‒ agriculture is very important sector in the eu economy which currently employs 22.2 million people. it is important to note that predominantly rural areas cover nearly 52 % of the eu’s territory and are home to 112 million people. unfortunately, these rural areas have been particularly hard hit by the economic crisis. because of that, many rural areas in the eu are facing socio-economic challenges such as depopulation, high unemployment rates, lower levels of income, lack of opportunities for young people and women, and lower level of education and skills. in this context, cap is one of the eu’s main tools for action in rural areas. with its total budget of eur 408.3 billion, it involves large transfers of funds to rural areas, with an impact on job creation. however, currently cap cannot create the expected job numbers because direct payments from the policy are not fairly distributed among farmers and cap procedures are quite complicated and slow. therefore, in order to improve cap effectiveness in job creation in rural areas, better distribution among small and medium-sized farms should be introduced and cap procedures should be simplified.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the draft council implementing decision approving the conclusion by the european police office (europol) of the agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between ukraine and europol. the proposed report on the approval of an operational and strategic agreement between europol and ukraine provides for the exchange of expertise, general situational reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, participation in training, consultation and support for specific criminal investigations. i believe that ukraine is becoming increasingly important in the fight against organised crime, and more specifically drug-related crime and economic crime, human trafficking and smuggling, as well as mobile organised crime groups. the exchange of information will allow the eu, the member states and ukraine to prevent and combat organised crime, terrorism and other forms of transnational crime more effectively. in addition to the exchange of information, the agreement also creates new opportunities, such as training and crime prevention activities. the conclusion of this cooperation agreement is a very concrete and significant step towards ukraine becoming a key partner in the fight against organised crime.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that we should approve the proposed operational and strategic agreement between europol and ukraine, providing for the exchange of information, including personal data. indeed, there are many reasons why europol needs to deepen its operational cooperation with ukraine. first and foremost, ukraine remains source country for organised crime, more specifically drug related crimes, economic crimes, human trafficking and smuggling. second, exchange of information will enable the eu, member states and ukraine to prevent and combat organised crime, terrorism and other forms of international crime more effectively. third, reinforced security cooperation between the eu and ukraine is complementary with the rapprochement taking place in other areas such as the mobility of european and ukrainian citizens. last but not least, we should support the conclusion of this strategic and operational cooperation agreement with ukraine, because it will pave the way for ukraine to become a key eu partner in the fight against organised crime.
in writing. ‒ i supported the establishment of a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, as i consider this to be a very important step in the effort to restore cod stocks in the northern waters of the eu. the adopted plan aims to strengthen and extend cooperation between fisheries scientists and the sector. we have seen successful projects in a number of fisheries sectors related to atlantic cod. they aim to reduce catches of cod and to limit discards to the sea, while maintaining sustainable catch levels of the target species. this decision satisfies all interested parties.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards access to information by tax authorities for the purpose of combating money laundering. the fight against tax evasion and tax avoidance, including in relation to money laundering, is an absolute priority of the union, which needs to ensure effective control by the relevant institutions carrying out a comprehensive audit, which could not happen without access to information direct, timely and comprehensive. information regularly entered into harmonised ict systems between member states will improve the functioning of all levels of administrative cooperation. the proposal for a directive also stresses the importance of exchanging up-to-date information that will contribute to an effective investigation. the directive, implemented in the national legislation of each member state, should help and make much more reliable the work of public institutions in the fight against tax fraud.
in writing. ‒ we should support and adopt the commission’s proposal to amend directive 2011/16/eu so that tax authorities with anti-money-laundering (aml) responsibilities in any eu country can have consistent access to aml information, procedures, documents and mechanisms in other member states. in this sense, it is important to note that including aml information in mandatory automatic exchanges between national tax authorities will be an important step in the fight against tax avoidance and evasion because it will improve tax transparency. nevertheless, i call on the eu to extend the scope of aml information available to national tax authorities with regard to virtual currency exchange services and custodial wallet providers to limit money laundering in the digital age.
in writing. ‒ the discontent that european citizens have felt towards the eu in recent years is not an unexplained phenomenon. this can be largely explained by the fact that the main burden of dealing with the financial and economic crisis has been and continues to be borne by ordinary people. meanwhile, powerful figures with substantial wealth are escaping legal and financial liability through offshore centres, such as those revealed in the 'panama papers'. in this context, i expressed my support for this resolution because it outlines the fight against tax evasion and tax avoidance, including in relation to money laundering, as a top priority for the eu. i hope that as this fight is put on the eu agenda, concrete policy action will follow to eliminate offshore centres globally.
in writing. – recent media leaks exposed the large-scale concealment of offshore funds. the main new element of the report is that the tax authorities of a member state shall automatically exchange the documents and information on aml with any other member state. as a substitute member in the econ committee, i supported this report because i believe that better cooperation is essential to ensure that member states can counter money-laundering practices better.
in writing. ‒ this report is the european parliament's response to the annual report of the european central bank (ecb) for 2015. i am pleased to see that mr tremosa's report addresses the ecb's policy in a sensible way. it was high time we saw critical language on problematic issues, such as low and even negative interest rates. however, for me and my group, there are important elements in the report that contradict our ideas. we disagree with the asset purchase program aimed at long-term refinancing operations, and we don't understand why the negative interest rate policy was imposed. it is important to emphasise that we take a much more critical view of the banking union and we differ from the view expressed in the report. because of the strengths and weaknesses of the report, i voted to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ecb's annual report for 2015. i believe that the commitment of the european central bank in august 2012 to 'do whatever is necessary' to protect the euro has made a significant contribution to ensuring the financial stability of the euro area. i believe that a well-functioning, diversified and integrated capital market will support the transmission channels of the single monetary policy. in this context, i call for the gradual completion and full implementation of the banking union and for full compliance by member states with the related legislation, as well as for the building of a capital markets union, as this is a decisive step to increase the effectiveness of the single monetary policy and to reduce the risks arising from shocks in the financial sector. addressing the non-performing loans problem for the most affected national banking sectors is essential to restore the smooth functioning of the monetary policy transmission mechanism for the euro area as a whole. i believe that the ecb needs to examine how the implementation of monetary policy differs between member states with centralised and concentrated banking sectors and those with a more diverse network of local and regional banks, and between countries that rely more on banks or capital markets to finance the economy.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, the european central bank’s (ecb) annual report for 2015 stresses that the euro area continues to suffer from a high level of unemployment, excessive low inflation, low level of productivity growth, lack of investment and large macroeconomic imbalances. to this point, ecb continues to underline the urgency of much-needed structural reforms and sound fiscal policies in the euro area. the report also expresses caution in a number of fields such as low interest rates, a damaging reduction in bank profitability, inflation of asset bubbles and impediments to the sound functioning of pension funds. therefore, on the basis of the european central bank’s (ecb) annual report for 2015, i urge the eu to put pressure on member states in order to implement vital structural reforms as soon as possible. furthermore, i call on the eu to facilitate the completion of banking union and to encourage the establishment of a capital market union. i certainly believe that these actions would be a decisive step towards improving the effectiveness of the single monetary policy and ensuring the financial stability of the euro area.
in writing. – as a substitute member in the econ committee, i supported this report because it provides a good assessment of the interplay of monetary policies and structural reforms and the risks of low interest rate policies. the text as finally adopted takes a balanced assessment of the asset purchase programme (app) of the ecb. it does not call for an expansion but requests an impact study concerning secondary markets for public debt.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. this report is a response to the commission's green paper on retail financial services, with the aim of launching a debate on the possible opening of the european financial services market. markets across the european union are very diverse in nature due to regional and national characteristics and this is also the case for financial services within the eu. i agree that better coordination and exchange can be of great benefit, and i welcome the fact that the rapporteur has produced a fairly balanced report, taking into account many proposals from other political groups. some of the proposals that i support and that have been included are a reference to a common tax identification number, alignment of the summary of the prospectus with the key information document for retail and insurance-based investment product packages (ripipip), the european supervisory authorities to increase their activities on consumer and retail investor issues, and a call for intensified work against the geoblocking principle applied by a legislative proposal targeting the financial sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the green paper on retail financial services because i believe that differences in tax, social, legal, health, contract and consumer protection systems, as well as different national specificities, cannot be overcome by means of digitalisation alone. i consider it essential to promote positive developments in the retail financial services market by creating and maintaining a level playing field between all participants, subject to rules that are as neutral as possible with regard to technology and business models. to be a leading market for innovation, and to enable consumers to have better choice at lower prices, europe must put a strong emphasis on creating an eu market where well-protected consumers have equal opportunities and access to products at good value for money.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because the objective of the green paper on retail financial services is to consult on the next steps toward creating a more integrated european market for retail financial services for both consumers and businesses. thus, the green paper in the eu works in the interests of consumers and gives them the best deals, better products, more choice, and greater opportunities regardless of their age, skills and country of residence. in this context, i would like to note that the green paper comes at the right time because digitalisation is now opening up new possibilities for consumers, investors, smes and other companies in terms of competition and cross-border activities. therefore, i urge the eu to coordinate the green paper with the process of digitalisation, because this in practice represents a golden opportunity to link financial actors established all around europe to consumers residing all around europe. in a long term perspective, such a link between green paper and digitalisation could foster job creation, sustainable growth, financial stability and the role of the consumer in the european economy.
in writing. ‒ the retail financial services sector in the eu is currently underdeveloped and highly fragmented. this is clearly reflected in the amount of fintech funding in europe, which amounts to just us$348 million. by comparison, in north america and china, which are direct competitors of the eu in this sector, fintech funding amounts to 1.8 and 2.6 billion respectively. against this background, i have advocated this resolution because it focuses on digitalisation as a way to develop the retail financial services market in europe. it can help to unlock the potential of this sector by making it more attractive to the european consumer through easier product comparison, better access to cross-border investment and faster registration and payment processes. i supported this resolution because i believe that the use of personal data and big data by financial service providers should be strictly limited to the data needed to improve retail financial services in the eu.
in writing. – this report is the parliament contribution to the consultation process opened with the commission green paper. the objective is to decide how the european market for retail financial services – namely insurance, loans, payments, current and savings accounts and other retail investments – can be further opened up, bringing better results for consumers and firms whilst maintaining an adequate level of consumer and investor protection. as a member of the imco and substitute member of the econ committees i fully support the digitisation and portability of services, issues which have been taken on board in this report.
in writing. ‒ new conditions and continuing threats to security in europe have triggered a new debate among european politicians. two main lines emerged in the new debate. the first is that of those who want 'more europe', or in other words the federalists. the second is the one that my group and i believe is correct, namely that security and defence are the most important feature of sovereignty and should be the competence of national states. i think that first of all the countries in europe should fulfill their commitment to nato and start spending 2% of gdp on defence and security, and then we can build a new defence union. that is why i voted against the report on a european defence union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which reiterates the european parliament's call for the eu to be empowered to meet citizens' security expectations. the report rightly stresses that the level of ambition needs to be significantly raised in view of the growing instability and unpredictability in our neighbourhood, and now in view of the outcome of the us presidential election. it is high time that all the possibilities offered by the lisbon treaty are exploited to ensure greater coherence and effectiveness of the union in defence matters. the report also shows that greater defence autonomy will only enhance nato's credibility. the report also devotes particular attention to research and industrial base issues, for which adequate resources are urgently needed. finally, the european defence union must be seen in the context of the common defence and security policy and the coherence of internal and external policies, in a world where security threats originate both within and outside the union.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because nowadays the eu and the member states face many complex and interconnected security threats such as terrorism, violation of international law by third countries, energy insecurity, cyber attacks and hybrid warfare. undoubtedly, the current state of the csdp does not allow the eu and the member states to address effectively these security threats. the inefficiency of the csdp can be regarded as one of the reasons why approximately two thirds of eu citizens would like to see greeter eu engagement in matters of security and defence policy. we should not turn a blind eye to the fact that in times of rising euroscepticism and nationalism, eu citizens increasingly regard security as a high priority and want the eu to show greater leadership. offering our citizens security makes the establishment of the european defence union (edu) a matter of urgency. i strongly believe that the establishment of edu starts from a thoroughly revised csdp, based on a strong collective defence principle, efficient financing and coordination with nato. in a long term perspective, the establishment of edu will foster the process of european integration, the eu’s role in world politics, safety and security of eu citizens.
in writing. – the eu needs to reflect about its defence policy in the long term. i supported this report, due to the fact that current increasing security challenges and complexities make this defence policy a more pertinent task. the level of eu ambitions in the area of defence need to significantly increase and be coupled with political will at the highest level to unleash the potential of the treaties (i.e. permanent structured cooperation) in this regard. this will help to ensure long-term security of the eu and its citizens.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report and the commission's new legislative proposals to simplify and improve the common rules on the safety of passenger ships in eu waters, with a view to enhancing safety and competition by clarifying and simplifying the rules and taking account of legal and technological developments. however, there is still an additional need to simplify the existing regulatory framework in order to remove outdated or overlapping requirements. greater attention needs to be paid to the safety of crew and passengers on coastal vessels in the context of uncontrolled flows of illegal migrants to europe by sea. i believe that further improvements are needed to develop integrated ticketing schemes and to increase reliability and frequency. a framework for ensuring connections with islands, island regions and remote areas should be promoted, with measures to facilitate better quality ferries and suitable terminals. all this is well described in the report and that is why i supported it.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on unlocking the potential of passenger transport by water, as waterborne passenger transport, including sea ferries, river ferries, barges and cruise ships, plays a key role in achieving a more sustainable and efficient european transport sector. most of europe's daily commuters travel by road, and this creates congestion, congestion and delays on europe's urban routes. more efficient use of available waterborne passenger transport capacity can not only help reduce congestion and co2 emissions, but can also improve air quality and provide better transport services overall. the geographical characteristics of europe, including many rivers, waterways, estuaries, long coastlines and islands, create exceptional opportunities for water transport. there are many areas in europe where water travel would be more sustainable, easier and faster, thus increasing the social and economic well-being of the region, while protecting the environment and the health of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ waterborne passenger transport (wpt) is a very important transport sector for the eu and member states. the importance of the wpt sector comes from the fact that some ferry connections are lifelines – vital for territorial, social and economic cohesion in the true sense – connecting outermost regions to the mainland and the economic and industrial growth areas, thus contributing to european cohesion and integration. in addition, the wpt sector plays a crucial role in development of tourism, in particular in remote and peripheral regions of the union such as coastal, island lake and rural regions. looking from this perspective, i supported the resolution because the wpt sector is sustainable and efficient mode of transport for eu citizens. importantly, we should support the wpt sector by making policies that address safety, environmental standards, cross-border cooperation and competitiveness as well as service quality, passenger rights and barrier-free accessibility. in this sense, we should put the wtp sector at the top of the eu’s maritime transport policy strategy to 2018.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution because it focuses on a measure that would not only benefit the development of river tourism in my country, but i believe it would also improve the daily lives of many of my fellow citizens. the resolution calls on the commission to support infrastructure investment in passenger transport by water, in particular in the hinterland of populated areas. i believe that such investments are of great benefit to the bulgarian citizens who live near the danube river and other rivers in the interior of the country. first, they help to reduce congestion in large river-side cities, improving their environmental performance and increasing their comfort and quality of life. secondly, such infrastructure can provide services to provide remote areas and develop the capacity of river tourism in the country.
in writing. – waterborne passenger transport, including maritime ferries, inland ferries, barges and cruises, plays a crucial role in achieving a more sustainable and efficient european transport sector, assisted by policies that address safety, environmental standards, cross-border cooperation and competitiveness as well as service quality, passenger rights and barrier-free accessibility. as a member coming from a country with access to the river danube, i support this report because i believe that a better and more efficient framework for travelling on waterborne passenger transport will be beneficial to the member states economies and the cities with access to major rivers.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by my colleague, mrs preda, on improving the effectiveness of development cooperation. the eu and its member states could work on new initiatives to develop trilateral cooperation projects, attracting new donors and middle-income countries. the eu could be more active in engaging national parliaments, local authorities and individuals in programming and financial commitments related to development assistance by publishing country-specific views on development cooperation. i support the logic of the draft report, as more needs to be done (with less financial resources) both at eu and global level to increase the effectiveness of development aid. it endorses all the proposed policy principles in particular the need to partner with the private sector through blending and public-private partnerships.
in writing. i voted in favour of this excellent report, which contributes to a clear and precise positioning of the european union in the process of implementing the 2030 agenda and achieving the sustainable development goals. while reiterating the importance of the commitment to allocate 0.7% of gdp to development aid, the report encourages an innovative and pragmatic approach, also aimed at mobilising private investment. in addition, the report places particular emphasis on the importance of inclusiveness and partnerships with all actors to achieve the sdgs. i am also pleased that the report takes into account the role of women and the importance of gender equality in ensuring the effectiveness of development cooperation. finally, the report has the merit of recalling the extremely close link between improving transparency, good governance and the rule of law in developing countries and the effectiveness of development cooperation.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on increasing the effectiveness of development cooperation, as it supports the eu's long-term commitment to developing standards for the effectiveness of development aid and to the adoption of the 2030 agenda. the eu is a major financial donor in support of the development of countries in financial difficulty, and a key factor in the fight to eradicate poverty by 2030. i welcome the idea of a global partnership and the joint setting of sustainable development priorities and the effectiveness of development cooperation between international donors, national governments, the private sector and civil society. international cooperation will help to make aid more effective where it is needed most. i believe that the eu should play a leading role in international efforts to make progress on the development effectiveness agenda. at the same time, the eu must be a guarantor of peace, respect for human rights and the rule of law as the basic preconditions for the transparent management of the resources allocated to the beneficiary countries. the main commitment of these countries is to pursue a transparent and targeted policy to achieve the 2030 agenda's sustainable development goals.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution because the eu is the world’s biggest development aid donor and as such it has a special responsibility to improve the effectiveness of aid and development cooperation. in fact, this is necessary because aid and development effectiveness can play a crucial role in implementation of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development and the achievement of the sdgs. in this context, the eu should enhance the accountability, transparency and visibility of eu aid in order to improve its quality and thus help developing countries achieve the millennium development goals. the eu has played a major role both in building the current standards for aid and development effectiveness, and in the adoption of agenda 2030, therefore i believe it should continue to assume leadership on these issues. last but not least, aid and development effectiveness is in the interest of the eu because the fragmentation of the aid effort means an additional cost of between eur 2 and 3 billion a year for the eu. certainly, with more effective aid delivery and development cooperation the eu can ‘do more, with less’.
in writing. ‒ i supported mr preda's resolution as i believe that the global partnership for effective development cooperation should be seen in the context of the implementation of the 2030 agenda and the addis ababa action agenda. account should be taken of the fact that the emphasis is shifting from 'aid effectiveness', which refers to traditional public development aid, to the concept of 'development cooperation effectiveness'. development assistance and cooperation are necessary but insufficient factors for effectively eradicating poverty and promoting the sustainable development goals. this is why i believe that the eu can learn from the experience of countries such as china, brazil, russia and india, which have expertise and technology in the field of development. given that development aid plays an important role in combating poverty and in improving access to quality public services for the most vulnerable groups in need, i support the idea of codifying and strengthening mechanisms and practices. i believe that this would contribute to better complementarity and effective coordination of development aid between countries.
in writing. – the eu has a long-standing commitment to improving aid and development effectiveness through development cooperation. i voted in favour of this report because it reaffirms the importance of official development aid and sustainable financing for development, while promoting an approach that goes beyond aid and aid-providing agendas. placing the un sdgs at the centre of the development cooperation global framework, the report insists on the need for a concrete and measurable impact of development policies. to this end, they should be coherent and ensure domestic ownership. in this regard, the involvement of local actors and civil society is imperative.

in writing. – i have always said that we cannot guarantee jobs or income to our citizens. but today we are talking about equipping people with skills, and this is a very welcome development. with this, we are making a strong political commitment to support the relentless development of our creative people. i welcome the commission’s skills guarantee. particularly, defining digital skills as basic capabilities marks a major development in mindset – being tech savvy is a key competence in life. in order to make the new skills strategy work, we should: create a culture of learning across europe – individuals must feel disposed to learn throughout their lives and confident in doing so; ‘embed’ basic skills – integrating literacy, language and numeracy learning into other trainings for a holistic approach to learning; ensure collaboration with employers and businesses, demonstrating basic skills training is an investment rather than a cost; and, most importantly, develop a strategic perspective, bringing together an understanding of the wider context and awareness of the need to adapt or change previous practice. following these steps, we can truly upskill our younger and older generations. тhis is crucial, because skills are the currency of the 21st century, they are europe’s strongest asset.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, three years have passed since the publication of the clean air act, a time of long but important debate and search for acceptable solutions for cleaner and healthier air in our towns and villages. i support the compromise reached with the council on the new directive, which sets ambitious targets for reducing air pollution by 2030. recent attention has focused on greenhouse gas emissions, and this has led to a slowdown in the reduction of other pollutants that have serious impacts on human health and the environment. for example, the growth of diesel cars due to lower co2 emissions has led to an increase in harmful nitrogen oxides from them. almost 400 000 people in the eu die prematurely from polluted air, and another 40 million people breathe in dust particles far above the norm. the new legislation must restore confidence in emissions reductions with its ambitious targets and sound control mechanisms. i welcome the considerable flexibility given to member states to achieve their individual objectives set out in the directive, as this will help to identify the most effective and appropriate measures to tackle the problem. the directive is particularly valuable in its concern for agriculture and its specificity for response, even though the sector is responsible for most of the ammonia and methane emissions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution. i am definitely awaiting an opinion of the court of justice of the european communities on the compatibility with the treaties of the proposed agreement between canada and the european union (ceta) , requiring parliament to suspend its consent procedure for the agreement. i personally do not agree with the idea that the opinion of the legal services of the european parliament is sufficient. an agreement of this scale is not sufficient and legally adequate, assessed solely by the legal service of the ep. this assessment cannot replace a court judgment or national legal discretion. the court of justice of the european communities is the appropriate binding instrument for delivering an opinion. national parliaments have not even started, nor have they had enough time for the procedures of analysis, legal control and ratification and have simply expressed a political, legally non-binding readiness to further develop trade relations with canada. moreover, according to the procedural rules for the negotiation and implementation of this type of international agreements, the necessary assessment of each member state, which will make its own individual analysis at national level, would be required, after which the procedure for ratification and implementation of ceta could be initiated, and without an appropriate preliminary assessment, only further political and procedural issues would be raised.
in writing. ‒ today i voted against the proposed resolution to request an opinion from the court of justice of the eu on the trade agreement with canada (seta). the resolution argues that there is legal uncertainty as to whether the agreement (and in particular the new investor-state dispute settlement system) is compatible with the treaties. i would remind you that this very issue was referred to the european parliament's legal service back in the spring and it came to the conclusion that none of the text in the chapter on investments in ceta is in conflict with the eu treaties. i have no reason not to trust the lawyers working in the legal department of the european parliament, which is not tied to political groups. the purpose of the resolution was more to delay ratification. the trial itself would take about a year and a half. to use legal procedures in this way, just to delay the decision-making process, is wrong to say the least. the best possible outlook for bulgaria is currently in place: provisional application of the agreement, a procedure for its approval in each individual member state and a clear commitment to visa waiver. let us not confine the discussion of ceta to the european parliament. it is high time that a broad, evidence-based public debate was held in the member states.
in writing. - i voted for this file. as part of the revised national emission ceilings directive (necd), part of the commission's clean air package, it replaces the current union regime of the annual national emission ceiling for air pollutants as set out in directive 2001/81/ec for sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane volatile organic compounds (nmvocs) and ammonia (nh3) until 2020. the new directive will create new national emission reduction commitments applicable from 2020 and 2030 for these pollutants, as well as for fine particulate matter (pm2.5) and methane (ch4). i support the view that member states should have some flexibility in achieving the 2030 targets, as the situations and requirements for achieving those targets differ drastically between them, but that the wording itself should be fine-tuned to ensure that the provisions are not open to abuse. as this is for the health of all citizens in all member states of the european union, this issue must be a priority. methane is excluded from the scope as the commission confirmed that it would carry out a review of methane even if it is not mentioned in the directive.
in writing. ‒ i supported the agreement reached on reducing national emissions of certain air pollutants, as i believe that new concrete targets are needed to reduce air pollution, which is a major problem for both the environment and human health. i support the new national targets set for reducing emissions of five major air pollutants by 2030 and the specific commitments provided in the report to adopt national control programmes. the eu is a major player in the fight against climate change, partly caused by air and environmental pollution. at the same time, the health of european citizens must be a core commitment for the eu. for this reason, i believe it is necessary for member states to commit themselves to meeting their specific emission reduction commitments under the directive.
in writing. ‒ after years of political neglect, air pollution has become the single largest environmental cause of premature death in urban europe, productivity loss, crop yield loss and damage to buildings. over the last couple of decades, emission reductions have led to improvements in air quality in europe, but not enough to avoid an unacceptable 400 000 premature deaths in europe and growing damage to environment. i supported the resolution because the growing air pollution represents a real health threat to the eu, its member states and citizens. i call particularly on member states to adopt and implement national air pollution control programmes with a view to meeting their emission reduction requirements and to contributing effectively to the achievement of the union air quality objectives. most importantly, in order to reduce emissions from the main contributors, national air pollution control programmes should include measures applicable to all relevant sectors, including agriculture, industry, road transport, non-road mobile machinery, inland and domestic shipping, domestic heating and solvents.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the finalisation of basel iii. basel iii is a comprehensive set of reform measures developed by the basel committee on banking supervision aimed at strengthening regulation, supervision and risk management in the banking sector. they aim to improve the capacity of the banking sector to absorb shocks arising from financial and economic stress, irrespective of its source, and to improve risk management and governance, enhance transparency and disclosure of banks. i believe that a sound and well-capitalised banking system is a prerequisite for preserving financial stability and supporting economic growth.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the finalisation of basel iii because i believe it is our duty to ensure a sustainable and well-capitalised banking system. bulgaria is one of the countries that has experienced a banking collapse. in my country, it was born out of the revelation of the ktb financial pyramid. the bank's bankruptcy has raised a number of questions among citizens about the stability of the banking system in the country and the control of banks. therefore, i believe that the reforms enshrined in basel iii, focused on the enhancement of the risk sensitivity and stability of the standardised approach to credit risk, the further restrictions on the internal modelling approach and the finalisation of the definition of the leverage ratio and potential capital base, will contribute to the stability of banks. the banks must be well capitalised in order to provide real support to the economy. we need to take the necessary measures to prevent systemic risks and to reduce the possibility of large-scale bailouts. the stability of banks in the eu is a step towards a stable economy for the member states.
mr president, unfortunately nowadays the eu and its member states live in a more dangerous and less predictable security environment. we are facing a broad and evolving set of challenges, both conventional and hybrid. despite the fact that these challenges represent common risks and threats to the security of the eu, they affect us differently. consequently the member states react to them in an uncoordinated and fragmented way. therefore, i strongly believe that a substantial revision of the common security and defence policy will enable the eu to effectively cooperate and coordinate their efforts and capabilities in order to contribute in a decisive way to the security of the union. working from this perspective, a revised csdp will not only assert the european union’s strategic autonomy and strengthen its resilience, but will also further enhance political integration within the eu. this strategy should be based on a strong collective defence principle, efficient financing and should be implemented in coordination with international institutions in the field of security and defence, particularly in full complementarity with nato.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy because i believe that the call for wider eu competences in the field of security and defence is unacceptable. the european union is a political union, a political union of the peoples of europe. i am part of the latter group because i believe that europe will be stronger if it returns to the idea of a 'europe of nations'. i believe that security is the exclusive competence of the member states and should remain so. security and defence are the last mark of sovereignty of the member states and i will continue to uphold these views.
in writing. – i have voted in favour because security is a priority for european citizens. no country can face the current security challenges on its own. first, because the changing european neighbourhood and complex crises have showed that internal and external security are becoming more and more intertwined. therefore the eu should be empowered to act along the entire spectrum of internal and external instruments. secondly, because over the last years, csdp cooperation, such as border assistance, capacity building and training in the (broader) eu neighbourhood has proven its benefit. we should strengthen existing csdp tools and use them more efficiently. i encourage further cooperation and coordination between member states, also in the framework of the provisions of the treaty of lisbon, with the commitment, ownership and support of member states and national parliaments. i therefore welcome the roadmap on csdp that vp/hr mogherini will present, with a concrete timetable and actions. finally, i welcome all references to increased dialogue and enhanced cooperation on security and defence with international institutions and third countries. without duplicating nato structures, we should strengthen the partnership, in full complementarity. cooperation, be it between eu member states or with partner countries and institutions, will entail practical and financial benefits.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy because i believe that the security of european citizens is of paramount importance to the eu. the eu needs an adequate defence and security policy today more than ever to protect its borders, to be able to prevent crises and to pursue an active policy against hybrid warfare. i think the eu and the member states should invest more in their own defence. building common defence capabilities and more investment in common defence equipment procurement, common defence sector science, common training of military personnel and building common intelligence and counter-intelligence activities is of paramount importance. i support the idea that the eu should have its own strategic defence, complementing nato's capabilities, not duplicating them. nato is a strategic partner of the eu with which it has close cooperation, but in today's conditions of migration and crises, the eu needs its own defence alliance with which to safeguard security and peace in europe.
in writing. ‒ in the face of a radically changed international environment, the eu needs a new approach and a new security strategy. the report underlines that europe is no longer in full control of its security environment and calls on the eu to adapt to new challenges by making more effective use of existing csdp tools. the report calls for better cooperation and coordination between member states, especially in the field of counter-terrorism. the report also fully supports further strengthening of security and defence cooperation with other institutional partners such as the un.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on budgetary control. – mr president, the creation of a single vat area in the eu could support a deeper and fairer single market, boosting jobs, growth, investment and competitiveness. while vat is one of the major sources of revenue in the eu, we should recognise that the current vat system is fragmented, complex for the growing number of businesses operating cross-border, and prone to fraud. the vat system needs to be reformed, and the recommendations in this regard include simplification, in order to become business-friendly; combating the growing risk of fraud; increasing efficiency, in particular exploiting the opportunities of digital technology; integrating the cost of revenue collection; enhancing trust, both between business and tax administrations and among eu member states’ tax administrations; and improving the quality of member states’ replies to information request and the reliability of the vat information exchange system. the commission and the member states should strengthen cooperation with non-eu countries and enforce vat collection. we need to implement necessary reforms in order to combat fraud efficiently, remove administrative barriers and reduce regulatory costs so as to simplify life for european businesses.

in writing. ‒ the the report states that, at almost €1 billion in 2014, vat is one of the main sources of revenue in the eu and its contribution is growing. vat represents around 7% of the union's gross domestic product and provides part of the eu's own resources. according to the proposed report, cross-border vat fraud results in losses for member states and european taxpayers of almost eur 50 billion per year. vat fraud also leads to a loss of revenue for member states and therefore for the eu, creating a distorted fiscal environment that is particularly harmful to small and medium-sized enterprises. the report notes the need to coordinate member states' efforts to reach agreement on a definitive vat system. the report also welcomes the commission's intention to propose by 2017 a final vat system that is simplified and fair and that limits the possibilities for fraud. the proper functioning of the digital single market is also based on a simplified vat system.

member of the commission. – madam president, the umbrella agreement on which you are asked to cast your vote tomorrow is of great importance for the protection of all europeans whenever their personal data are transferred to the united states for law enforcement purposes. it is with this in mind that i ask you for your consent to the agreement so as to allow its conclusion under the current us administration. let me briefly recall what the umbrella agreement is about and what type of immediate benefits it will bring to europeans. first – and this is unprecedented, not only in the trans-atlantic context, but also more generally at international level – for the first time we will have a genuine data protection agreement in the field of law enforcement cooperation. by that, i mean not an agreement that authorises transfers, but instead an agreement that focuses exclusively on data protection safeguards and the rights of individuals, an agreement that contains the same type of catalogue of principles, safeguards and rights that we have in our data protection legislation. these include purpose limitation, restrictions on onward transfers, the right to access and rectification, administrative and judicial redress, and independent oversight. in assessing the value of the umbrella agreement, let us also recall the current situation and what the status quo would mean. as we speak, data is being shared between eu member states and us law enforcement authorities. these exchanges are taking place on the basis of legal instruments, in particular bilateral agreements that very often lack basic privacy safeguards or contain only limited protections. as we know, these transfers will continue to take place and are likely to intensify, notably in response to terrorism threats. the umbrella agreement addresses this serious deficit of protection. with its entry into force, all these transfers will benefit from the additional safeguards and rights provided by the umbrella. in other words, this is an agreement that will bring immediate and very substantial improvements to the situation of the eu data subjects. in doing so, the umbrella agreement will also remedy the current imbalance of protections between both sides of the atlantic. today americans already enjoy these protections when their data is transferred to the eu, while this is not the case for europeans when their data is transferred to the united states. this is why you asked us, in your resolution of 12 march 2014, to put rights for eu citizens on an equal footing with rights for us citizens. the consequence of all this is clear. it is first and foremost the protection of the fundamental rights of our citizens which will benefit from the agreement. i see no benefit in delaying its conclusion. this will only be to our detriment. i would like to warmly thank the rapporteur, mr albrecht, for his support on this important agreement. the help from the parliament has also been essential to ensure the adoption by the us congress of the us judicial redress act, which extends important rights to our citizens that were previously reserved only for americans. i would like to thank all of you for your continuous support on that. i know that certain aspects of the umbrella agreement have raised questions among some members of this house. the commission has taken these concerns very seriously, and on various occasions provided explanations and clarifications to the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. most recently we have transmitted to parliament a statement that contains these clarifications. the commission will issue this statement at the time of the conclusion of the agreement by the eu and it will be published in the official journal. while i understand that some of you still have reservations, i hope that our central message has been heard. this is a big leap in terms of data protection, and a major improvement compared to the status quo. this includes the adoption of the judicial redress act, something which would not have been possible without the pressure stemming from the umbrella agreement negotiations. making the judicial redress act operational still requires that the us attorney general designates the eu as being covered by the act. this is a necessary step for full implementation, and we have agreed with the united states that the official notifications triggering the entry into force will only be exchanged once this designation has been made. so time matters here. we understand that this can still happen in the coming weeks under the current administration.
the rapporteur on the opinion of the committee on legal affairs. madam president, commissioner jurova, as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on legal affairs, i supported the position of the rapporteur of the committee responsible, ms albrecht. parliament gave its consent to the conclusion of that agreement. it is important and will bring visible results. the aim of the agreement is primarily to establish a broad set of safeguards and guarantees that will be offered for the transfer of personal data for criminal law enforcement purposes between the united states of america, the european union and its member states. as a condition of legal certainty, the protection of personal data is a clear priority and is guaranteed in this agreement. i believe that this agreement ensures a high level of protection of this data, contributes to legal certainty and will further improve law enforcement cooperation with the united states of america. it is important to note that the agreement does not cover the exchange of data between national security services, as these are not within the competence of the union.
madam president, the adoption of the umbrella agreement is a very important step forward in improving security in europe, while at the same time not compromising human rights, and more specifically the protection of the personal data of european citizens. here in this parliament we have repeatedly called for increased cooperation, both between law enforcement agencies in the european union and with our international partners, in order to exchange timely and high-quality information on suspected terrorists, traffickers and other criminals. this is necessary to prevent future terrorist attacks and to make european citizens feel safer in their daily lives. but this cooperation cannot and must not be at the expense of the fundamental rights and freedoms we have won in europe. european citizens have a right to know that their data is not being misused, that the state is not monitoring them, but on the contrary is doing everything possible to protect them and their data. in the specific case of the umbrella agreement with the us, the european union does not unconditionally transfer personal data of europeans. the aim of the agreement is to ensure that the high standards of data protection we have here in europe will also apply to the exchange of data with our us partners. the agreement is by no means a slap in the face of europe to the united states, but on the contrary it provides european citizens with protection from american law enforcement and courts unlike anything that has ever existed. so in the name of international cooperation and protecting the privacy of european citizens, we should all vote in favour of the agreement tomorrow.

in writing. ‒ the full entry into force on 1 may 2016 of the provisions of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council of 9 october 2013 establishing the union customs code and of the subsequent delegated acts implementing it have revealed certain drafting deficiencies. this proposal to amend article 136 of the union customs code aims to ensure equal treatment of goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the union. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 establishing the union customs code, as regards goods temporarily leaving the customs territory of the union by sea or air.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the current proposal to amend article 136 of the union customs code (ucc) in order to ensure effective application of other ucc, notably these on customs supervision. the main reason why we should modify the article is that its current text says that certain provisions do not apply to goods that have temporarily left the union customs territory while moving by direct route between two points of that territory by sea or air without a stop outside the union. in other words, under the current text of article 136 ucc custom authorities have no clear legal basis through which to require presentation of union goods and non-union goods that have temporarily left the union customs territory. in this context, the proposed modification to the scope of article 136 ucc will ensure equal treatment of goods and will provide a legal basis through which customs authorities at the european union’s ports and airports will be able to levy correctly import duty and other charges, to apply correctly non-fiscal measures (e.g. veterinary or phytosanitary controls) as well as to identify risks on goods arriving at the european union’s ports and airports.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this, as it will clarify the legal situation as regards customs supervision of goods where they enter the european union through one seaport or airport but continue their way on the container to the second port in the european union where they are unloaded. according to the current article 136 of ucc, the person bringing the goods to the second sea port or airport does not have the legal obligation to go through certain formalities such as presenting goods to custom authorities, filling in the summary declaration, etc. this situation could jeopardise customs supervision obligations foreseen in article 134 in the ucc. to correct this legal gap the commission proposes to amend article 136 of the ucc by shortening the list of non-applicable provisions and thereby re-establishing the obligation to present the goods which have been brought into the customs union at the second point of entry under certain circumstances.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. the proposal concerns the rejection of regulatory technical standards (rts) proposed by the european securities and markets authority (esma) and the commission. in order to give the commission and the abovementioned european body time to amend the regulatory technical standards, a more than reasonable 12-month delay in the submission of the application has been agreed, as the amendments should not be applied without mandatory verification and analysis.
in writing. – the regulation on key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (priips) introduces a key information document (kid – a simple document giving key facts to investors in a clear and understandable manner) covering not only collective investment schemes but also other ‘packaged’ investment products offered by banks or insurance companies. in light of this, we should sustain amendments made by regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 on key information documents for priips as regards the date of its application. by doing so we actually will postpone the date of entry into application of the priips regulation, which means that it shall apply from 1 january 2018. thus, the eu and its member states will have more time to prepare for the application of the new rules.
in writing. ‒ the cotonou agreement defines the relations between the european union and the republic of kiribati, which are governed by the partnership agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states, of the one part, and the european union and its member states, of the other part. the signed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and for citizens of the republic of kiribati when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a period of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official and special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the purpose of engaging in a gainful occupation. i supported the abolition of the visa regime under the conditions mentioned above. i believe it can have a positive impact by simplifying travel conditions for entrepreneurs and increasing investment in tourism.

in writing. ‒ the solidarity fund has become a working fund in a short time, which unfortunately is used in natural disasters to help those affected. unfortunately, however, many of the affected areas were left out of the scope of this fund because the disasters in them did not meet the aid framework. that is why i welcome the change the ep's desire to reduce the threshold from 1.5% to 1%. i am also disappointed that the commission has not wanted to reduce it, but i hope that we will be able to achieve this very soon. i hope we can reduce the response time of the institutions, because 12 weeks to submit the aid documents and then another 6 for approval is still a long period for people in distress. finally, i hope that there is no reason for the money from this fund to be wasted, i.e. i hope that there are no major natural disasters in europe, and in the world in general.
in writing. ‒ the eu solidarity fund is a robust and flexible instrument providing real assistance to european citizens affected by major natural disasters. this is evidenced by the fact that the fund, since its creation in 2002, has mobilised a total of €3.8 billion in relation to over 70 disasters in 24 member states and candidate countries, including my own country, bulgaria. to continue to be a concrete and tangible instrument of eu solidarity towards communities affected by natural disasters, the fund needs to continue to evolve. in 2014, when the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 entered into force, the 'solidarity' fund was substantially renewed. the procedures for applying for financial assistance from the fund have been improved and simplified so that regions affected by natural disasters can receive a response within six weeks of the date of submission of an aid application. this resolution, for its part, again makes another interesting proposal to take the human development index and the regional social progress index into account when determining the financial assistance received by the affected regions. i think that the successes of the solidarity fund, as well as its continued development, should be encouraged, and that is why i support this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mrs albrecht on the conclusion of an agreement between the united states of america and the european union on the protection of personal information in connection with the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, as i believe that this will ensure additional protection of personal data. the aim of the agreement is primarily to establish a broad set of safeguards and guarantees that will apply to the transfer of personal data for criminal law enforcement purposes between the us and the eu and its member states. i believe that it ensures a high level of protection of personal data and contributes to legal certainty. it will also contribute to enhancing law enforcement cooperation with the united states of america. it is important to note that the agreement does not cover the exchange of data between national security services, as these do not fall within the competence of the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report as the agreement represents a significant advance on the protection of personal data when transferred between the eu and the us for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism. it should be emphasised that it does not restrict or infringe in any way the rights of data subjects as it does not constitute a legal basis for the transfer of data. the envisaged agreement contributes to legal certainty by creating a legal framework for the protection of personal data. it also provides a sound basis for the negotiation of future agreements between the eu and its member states, on the one hand, and the united states, on the other, providing for the transfer of personal data in the field of criminal law enforcement. the definition of common standards in this area of cooperation contributes to rebuilding trust in the exchange of data between europe and the us and sends a positive message about the strategic importance of strengthening and further deepening the transatlantic partnership in various areas.
in writing. ‒ i supported this agreement because it will have a significant impact on police and law enforcement cooperation between the european union (eu) and the united states (us). by establishing a common and comprehensive framework of data protection rules and guarantees, this eu-us data-protection umbrella agreement will safeguard citizens’ personal information during law enforcement investigations on both sides. thus, in a long-term perspective, this agreement will contribute significantly to restoring trust in transatlantic data flows as well as increasing anti-terrorism cooperation between the eu and the us. in general, this agreement will protect both eu and us citizens from common security challenges.
in writing. ‒ on 1 december, the european parliament approved the agreement between the united states and the european union on the protection of personal information in connection with the prevention, detection and prosecution of criminal offences. the agreement struck a very good balance between the protection of personal data and the protection of public policy and security in the case of joint eu-us actions. strengthening information exchange mechanisms is an important step towards better cooperation between the us, the eu and member states. the clauses of the agreement ensure that the high level of protection of personal data of european citizens is maintained through accountability mechanisms, a continuous dialogue between the responsible authorities, a proportionate use of the data provided and effective legal remedies. i believe this agreement will be the foundation on which the us and the eu will continue to build their relationship at a time when dialogue and cooperation at the international level are key to the detection and prosecution of crimes.

in writing. ‒ in 2016, the eu budget was extremely burdened as a result of the migration, refugee and security crisis. as a result of these unforeseen circumstances, an amount of eur 240,1 million is to be mobilised to provide commitment appropriations under heading 3 'security and citizenship' of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2016. the contingency margin is an instrument under the multiannual financial framework that allows the eu to mobilise additional funds in the event of unforeseen circumstances. it was established by article 13 of council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 and may raise an amount corresponding to 0,03% of the union's gross national income, which in this case may cover the union's outstanding commitments. i supported the mobilisation of the contingency margin in 2016 because i believe that the additional costs generated by the migration, refugee and security crisis were and are necessary for the eu to cope with the difficult situation it is in.
