in writing. ‒ unfortunately, the latest earthquakes in italy have led to death of 290 people; 400 people were injured, 150 000 italians have become homeless. furthermore, the latest earthquakes have destroyed towns, seriously damaged local and regional infrastructure, ruined historical and cultural heritage, and done serious harm to economic activities, especially those of smes which are in agricultural, tourist and gastronomic sectors. thereby, i call on the european commission to ensure that all the available instruments within the cohesion and regional funds are effectively used for reconstruction activities in full cooperation with the italian national and regional authorities. in addition to this, i urge the commission to undertake all the necessary measures to allow and provide a rapid financing for italian national and regional authorities from the european union solidarity fund. last but not least, i would like to remind the commission and italian national and regional authorities that sustainable reconstruction efforts need to be properly coordinated in order to fully overcome the economic and social losses from the earthquakes.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's legal affairs committee recently had to analyse the alleged conflict of interest of the european commissioner for climate and energy, miguel arias cañete. the powers of our commission were not very clear and a conclusion on the subject was almost impossible to make. many members of the house, including myself, felt that we were not a court and could not determine whether the commissioner was guilty or not. these guidelines, which i have supported in this report, are intended to clarify the competences and powers of the legal affairs committee in assessing possible conflicts of interest of commissioners. i still think we have not reached a final text that clarifies everything, but i supported the report because i think it is a good step and it gives a little more clarity and leads to a more transparent procedure.
in writing. ‒ it is more than clear that the european commission should revise its code of conduct for commissioners, to ensure that their declarations of interests give a complete picture of the financial situation and activities of a commissioner and his or her family. in fact, i fully support the proposition that the absence of any conflict of interest must be an essential precondition to be met before the commissioner’s hearings, and that the financial interest declaration forms must therefore be completed and made available before a commissioner is heard by the relevant european parliament committee, and that they should be reviewed at least once a year and each time there is a change to the information concerned. thus, in this manner, we will ensure the degree of transparency which is needed for the proper functioning of the commissioner’s appointment procedure and parliament’s accurate assessment on it.
in writing. ‒ this report largely seeks to increase the scope of responsibility for the conduct of offshore oil and gas operations. it calls for an eu liability framework in this area, with a request to harmonise minimum liability for civil damages, and recommends a common eu-level mechanism for dealing with incidents (i.e. another agency). the report also calls on the commission to consider the creation of a legislative mechanism for compensation and proposes that the scope be extended to include secondary damage. calls on the commission to include major oil accidents in the environmental crime directive (osd); it also proposes the creation of a fund based on fees paid by the offshore industry, with a request for a possible assessment by the commission. i do not support many of these proposals and i believe, above all, that the legislation currently in place is quite sufficient in this area and that what is required in this report does not meet the real needs. in such cases, european legislation should not be used.
in writing. ‒ in fact, over 90% of oil and 60% of gas produced in europe (eu and norway/iceland) comes from offshore operations. offshore operations (exploration and exploitation) are ongoing or planned to take place in the territorial waters of 18 member states. in view of the liability systems available in member states, it appears there is a crucial issue as to whether the majority of civil claims from accidents resulting in widespread pollution damage will be met by the current legislative or non-legislative and ad hoc or judicial regimes in place in these states. in this context, i fully support the rapporteur’s opinion that the commission should work closely with the member states and ensure that the compensation and financial security systems for offshore oil and gas operations in the eu are available. thus, in this manner, the eu will assure its citizens that there is an effective compensation regime for offshore oil and gas operations accidents and that operators or other liable parties would have adequate financial assets to meet compensation claims.
in writing. – the offshore safety directive was adopted with the aim of establishing minimum requirements for preventing major accidents in offshore oil and gas operations in the eu and to limit the consequences of such accidents. i voted in favour as the report calls on the commission to consider the establishment of a legislative compensation mechanism for offshore accidents at least for sectors that may be severely affected. such sectors include fisheries and coastal tourism and other sectors of the blue economy.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the situation in the democratic republic of congo, as what is happening in the country is deeply worrying. most recently, in october, congolese authorities announced that due to inaccuracies in the electoral lists, the presidential election scheduled for december 19, 2016, was postponed to december 2018. the current president, joseph kabila, took office in 2001 after the assassination of his father and was re-elected twice, in 2006 and 2011. after the president's attempt to change the constitution so he could run for a third term, he was thwarted by parliament and the country began to riot. it is believed that the decision to postpone the elections was made by president kabila, who still wants to change the constitution and run for a third term.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the resolution on access to energy in developing countries, as it draws attention to the growing energy poverty in these regions and underlines the eu's leading role in tackling this problem. it underlines the great potential of renewable energy in africa in terms of wind and solar power generation to provide access to energy for all, especially in rural areas, and calls on the eu and its member states to provide support and technical assistance in the implementation of the action plan of the african clean energy corridor initiative, which aims to meet half of total electricity consumption from clean, local, cost-effective renewable sources by 2030 to achieve carbon dioxide emissions reductions.
in writing. – access to reliable and safe energy is crucial for the satisfaction of basic human needs and rights, a key driver of development and a must for modernity. unfortunately, nowadays 1.2 billion people lack access to electricity, half of those without access to electricity live in africa; this number is growing, since the population on this continent is increasing at a faster pace than that at which access to energy is being extended. i supported the commission’s ‘energising development’ initiative, which aims to provide access to sustainable energy for an additional 500 million people in developing countries by 2030 through programme elements such as the creation of a technical assistance facility, drawing upon eu experts to develop technical expertise in developing countries, and to promote capacity building and technology transfer. in my opinion, the ‘energising development’ initiative must be fully aligned with the eu development policy and it should urge the eu and its member states to facilitate technology transfer (renewable energy resources) in developing states, in africa particularly.
in writing. – the main objective of this resolution is to take stock of the energy poverty in developing countries by emphasising the large number of people who lack access to electricity. i voted in favour as i support the main objectives of the resolution. i also believe this resolution also pays attention to respect on climate change in achieving global access.
in writing. ‒ the european order for payment procedure falls within the category of measures in the field of judicial cooperation in civil matters which have cross-border implications and which are necessary for the functioning of the internal market. the procedure is applicable to civil and commercial matters relating to uncontested claims, the main purpose of which is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the cross-border recognition and enforcement of creditors' rights in the eu. the report stresses that no change to the existing legislative framework is necessary. given the different types and lengths of procedures in the member states, i believe that the european order for payment will be much quicker and cheaper and will make it easier for europeans. it is for these reasons that i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european order for payment procedure is a procedure applicable in civil and commercial matters relating to uncontested claims whose main objective is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the cross-border recognition and enforcement of creditors’ rights in the eu. in this regard, there are several elements that should be taken into account in order for the european order for payment procedure to be more effective. first and foremost, member states should accept applications in languages other than their own where possible. in most member states, however, applications in foreign languages are not accepted. second, digitalisation of the procedure is necessary, which means that forms should be submitted online. this will reduce the number of errors and omissions on forms and will speed up the whole procedure. last but not least, member states should issue the orders within 30 days, the maximum term according to the regulation, no longer because the procedure becomes very slow and ineffective.
in writing. – regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 creating a european order for payment procedure is intended to simplify, speed up and reduce costs of the litigation in cases involving more than one eu country. i supported this report as it supports the work being done to allow the electronic submission of applications. furthermore, it calls on the commission to adopt updated standard forms and encourages the member states to strive to issue orders within the 30-day period provided by the regulation and to accept applications in certain foreign languages.
in writing. – solidarity and fairness are at the core of european values. europe must deliver to business and to citizens clean energy at a fair price. i welcome the proposed ‘clean energy for all’ package and i believe we must be even more ambitious if we are to be at the forefront of the low-carbon economy. we must also abide by the historic cop21 agreement. i call on the two co-legislators to ensure the swift negotiation and implementation of the proposals; only in this way will we deliver security of the energy supply. by making the energy market more flexible, i believe it will bring about more resilience and adaptability of the energy sector. working together is crucial. we must provide and strengthen the rules to ensure cross-border participation and that no country is left behind. europe must work towards greater fairness of the cost of energy in order to increase consumers’ trust. i look forward to working on this package here in the european parliament.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate the commission for presenting a comprehensive legislative package for the european energy union in just two years. the current clean energy for all europeans package outlines the future of european energy by 2030 in both an ambitious and achievable way. energy efficiency is put at the forefront as a universal means of reducing energy consumption, energy dependence, energy poverty and harmful greenhouse gas emissions. the proposed 30% energy saving target by 2030 will allow the current pace of energy efficiency improvements to be maintained. the package adopts the principle of technology neutrality in energy support policies, which provides the necessary flexibility for member states to seek the most cost-effective solutions to meet the targets of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and ensuring a reliable supply of clean and affordable energy, including from nuclear sources. i welcome the reduction of the super-privileges for renewable energy. after their technological development and entry into the energy sector, it is time to move to market mechanisms of their participation in the energy supply. the prospect of a declining role for fossil fuels in energy is also clear, but setting the unenforceable 550 gco2/kwh emissions target for new coal plants is effectively a cessation of investment in new capacity on existing coal technologies.
in writing. ‒ algeria's relations with the eu are based on an association agreement signed as part of the euro-mediterranean partnership in 2005. they cover politics, economics, trade, technical and financial cooperation and humanitarian aid. economic cooperation under the association agreement is carried out through several mechanisms involving both parties. the eu also funds a number of programmes aimed at supporting algeria's efforts in different areas of the economy. the first assessment of the benefits of the association agreement was carried out in 2009. the second assessment is currently underway. in 2014, an agreement was signed establishing the general principles for algeria's participation in eu programmes. i supported this report because it is technical and i believe that algeria, as a country that has maintained its stability and is performing well, can benefit from eu programmes.
in writing. the gradual opening up of certain eu programmes and agencies to the participation of the european neighbourhood policy partner countries represents a concrete opportunity to bring the two shores of the mediterranean closer together. it is an indirect but effective way of promoting reform, modernisation and transition in the european union's neighbourhood. algeria's participation in union programmes will also promote economic growth and security cooperation. the agreement also opens up the possibility for algerians, especially young people, to participate in programmes such as erasmus+, horizon 2020 and creative europe. beyond the economic and political benefits, it is a step towards a new history of relations between algeria and the european continent, a step that brings people closer by building new ties, which are not those of colonization, nor those of war. algeria has long expressed its strong interest in participating in european union programmes and i am pleased that the european parliament has given its almost unanimous agreement to this memorandum of understanding as a concrete element of the euro-mediterranean partnership.
in writing. ‒ i support the recommendation for the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the people's democratic republic of algeria, of the other part, on a framework agreement between the european union and the people's democratic republic of algeria on the general principles for the participation of the republic in union programmes. this protocol contains a framework agreement on the general principles for the participation of algeria in union programmes. it contains standard clauses which are intended to apply to all countries european neighbourhood policy partners with which such protocols are to be concluded. i believe that, as part of the european neighbourhood policy, the gradual opening of certain union programmes and agencies to the participation of countries partner countries in the european neighbourhood policy is one of the many measures aimed at providing support for the process of reform, modernisation and transition in the countries neighbouring the european union. i believe that a deeper partnership between the european union and the people's democratic republic of algeria is needed to improve the situation in terms of stability, democracy, good governance, the fight against corruption, economic development and employment in the region.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour on the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of algeria on the general principles for the participation of the republic of algeria in union programmes (hereinafter referred to as ‘the protocol’). the signing and provisional application of the protocol will lay down the financial and technical rules enabling algeria to participate in certain union programmes which in a long term perspective will foster bilateral relations between algeria and the eu.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because it is our moral duty to reduce the destructive impact on the marine ecosystem that has been caused by the use of bottom trawls in international waters. as a matter of fact, deep sea stocks are very vulnerable to fishing, stock depletion can occur within a short period of time, and recovery might take very long or even fail. therefore, i urge the eu to impose a ban on fishing below a depth of 800 metres in the north-east atlantic in order to protect vulnerable deep-sea marine ecosystems more effectively. i encourage the eu to insert stronger transparency safeguards, by including obligations to provide public information on eu vessels targeting deep-sea species and to report all catches (fish and vulnerable ecosystems). in general, i believe that the eu should lead global and regional efforts to promote more responsible deep-sea exploitation and to boost protection of deep-sea ecosystems.

in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of the report on the overall revision of the rules of procedure of the european parliament, as i believe that this will make the institution work better, increase transparency, and protect the ep from political attempts to block its work. the more substantial changes to the rules were driven by the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making adopted in 2016 and by the creation of new bodies in the context of the banking union. the considerations of the 2015 'corbett' report on procedures and practices relating to the hearing of commissioners also played a role in the formulation of the new rules. the amendments to improve the efficiency of work are the order of voting for legislative acts, question time, questions for written answer by the commission, motions for resolutions, roll-call votes and written declarations. meps will now be sanctioned by the president if they use defamatory, racist or xenophobic language or if they take actions that disrupt parliamentary business. the amendments are mainly due to technical, legal and linguistic considerations.
in writing. – given the changing political landscape in the european union and globally, i believe that it is necessary to adapt the rules of procedure of our house accordingly in order to be able to deliver quicker and better. for this reason i voted in favour of streamlining the current thresholds at plenary and committee level, also supporting the clarifications of some aspects of the legislative procedure and the inter-institutional negotiations and other provisions. the european parliament must lead by example.
in writing. ‒ the 2015 annual report on fundamental rights summarises the state of play on issues that have been on the agenda throughout the year. the report covers a wide range of topics such as migration, rights (of children, women, roma, people with disabilities, in relation to citizenship), sexual health, trafficking in human beings, equality, older people, violence against women, lgbti rights, etc. the positive elements are the calls for action on trafficking in human beings (support for victims, people with disabilities, women's rights, condemnation of rape, female genital mutilation and poverty among the elderly). however, the report still has some problematic points such as lgbti rights, calls for inclusion in the istanbul convention, etc. that is why i voted 'abstention'.
in writing. ‒ the charter of fundamental rights of the eu contains fundamental rights and freedoms that are protected in the eu such as dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, rule of law, human rights and minority rights. despite the fact that the charter of fundamental rights has become a fully-fledged component of the eu treaties and the national legislation of the member states, fundamental rights violations do occur in the eu and its member states. unfortunately, nowadays in the eu there is increasing racism, homophobia and xenophobia in the forms of afrophobia, anti-gypsyism, anti-semitism, islamophobia and anti-migrant sentiment. furthermore, there is a growing presence of hate speech on the internet, from within certain institutions, political parties and media. last but not least, in some member states eu citizens have been disfranchised of their citizen/national voting rights in eu and national elections when they exercise their fundamental right to use a minority language in an election campaign. therefore, i take the view that further efforts should be made towards a consistent and uniform implementation of the charter of fundamental rights, including through awareness-raising measures among practitioners and the general public, in order to guarantee that the rule of law and fundamental rights of european citizens are respected and promoted.
in writing. ‒ i supported mr nade's report because the european union is a community founded on values such as respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality and the rule of law. i believe that member states should take more serious action on the violations of fundamental rights found in reports by the european commission, the european union agency for fundamental rights (fra), the council of europe and non-governmental organisations. i believe that instilling values such as peace, equality, justice and respect for human rights in young people will strengthen their engagement with eu issues, allowing them to express their views more often in a democratic way. fundamental rights are universal, indivisible and always complementary. therefore, not only the european institutions, but also all actors at national level must step up their efforts to protect them. i support the adoption of the necessary measures for the accession of the european union to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms (echr) in accordance with opinion 2/13 of the court of justice of the eu, as this will enhance the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms of eu citizens.
in writing. – the protection of the fundamental rights of people is at the core of european values, together with solidarity and non-discrimination. i voted in favour of this report as i believe we must address the increasing challenges ahead of us with regard to tackling issues such as hate crime, hate speech, freedom and security, violence against women, minorities, or children, as well as protection against violation of digital rights. by granting the integrity of the fundamental rights of all eu citizens i believe we will be a step further and we will ease the discontent about europe.
in writing. ‒ the cultural and creative industries need support for their development and prosperity. the policies pursued by the european union in this respect must be consistent and that is why i fully supported the initiative for such a report. i am also pleased with the final result, achieved after some compromises on the part of my political group. that's why i supported the report. the cultural and creative industries are based on cultural values, individual creativity, skills and talents, which have the potential to generate wealth and jobs through the creation of value from intellectual property. statistics show that 7.5% of the eu's workforce is provided by these industries, which have shown growth in recent years. the report analyses the impact and potential of the cultural and creative industries and calls for their inclusion in the strategic objectives of the european union as well as in common political priorities.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on eu policy towards the cultural and creative industries, as i believe that a single strategy is needed, covering all the components of the cultural and creative industries and translating into an action programme. the cultural and creative industries are an important sector for the european economy and the eu's internal market, making a major contribution to the creation of new jobs, which are mainly employing young people. it is thanks to it that many small and medium-sized enterprises exist and function. that is why i support the idea of creating a strategic policy and long-term commitments that will help reduce youth unemployment, new investments in science and digitalisation, and increase growth in the eu economy. i support the proposal to allocate more funds and funding through various european programmes to promote the sector.
in writing. ‒ indeed, the cultural and creative industries (ccis) play an important role for the social and economic development of the eu and its member states. ccis on the one hand preserve and promote cultural and linguistic diversity by strengthening european, national, regional and local identities while on the other hand sustaining social cohesion and economic growth by promoting new business models, creativity and innovation, investment, digitalisation and skills building. in this context, i supported the resolution because the eu should develop a comprehensive and above all coherent long-term industrial policy framework for the ccis. moreover, i urge the eu to include the development, effective promotion and protection and adequate funding of ccis in its strategic goals and overall priorities in order to boost their competitiveness and enable them to fulfil their potential in terms of creating quality jobs and growth.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution because i share the view that the eu is not making the most of the economic and social potential of the cultural and creative industries (cis). this sector represents a significant part of the european and global economy and is a unique source of jobs and employment, especially in small and remote regions. in addition, it should be noted that cet provides the most jobs for young people and is one of the few sectors that has maintained its resilience in the context of the economic crisis. while it is true that cultural policies are primarily the responsibility of national governments, the eu has a role to play in complementing and supporting member states' actions in the cultural field. unfortunately, we must acknowledge that the care of our cultural heritage is being neglected in both the national and european context. last but not least, it should be noted that the digital age offers us an incredible opportunity to digitize our cultural and historical heritage and preserve it for future generations. for countries like bulgaria, this will give them a reason to feel confident, because we will be able to show the world the bulgarian beat, culture and traditions. for this reason, i believe that securing funding for digitisation and online access to europe's cultural heritage should be a priority.
in writing. – as a member of the committee on internal market and consumer protection i supported this report, as i am confident that it is a step towards harmonisation of the sectors. the report calls on the commission to develop a comprehensive, coherent and long-term industrial policy framework for the creative and cultural sector, and to provide adequate funding for ccis, in order to boost their competitiveness and to enable them to fulfil their potential in terms of creating quality jobs and growth. to achieve this ambitious goal, the report proposes a harmonised definition of ccis on which statistical data should be based.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report for several reasons. calling for the ratification of any international treaty is not the eu's job, and therefore i do not think we should do it here (in relation to the istanbul convention). we know that women's rights and gender equality are well established in the constitutions of the eastern partnership countries. the additional report calls for more traditionally male professions to be opened up to women, which i do not think is the right step in the development of our society and i would not invite the eastern partnership countries to do it, nor would the idea of quotas in political governance, which is supposed to give women more equality - that is not the right approach for me. of course, the report also offers some useful recommendations that i cannot condemn, and finding ways to eliminate gender stereotypes should be our goal.
in writing. the challenges faced by the eastern partnership countries in terms of women's rights are generally common to those faced by the european union. in different proportions, the achievement of equality between men and women must be the subject of determined efforts on both sides, in order to meet the foundations and objectives of the eastern partnership and the european neighbourhood policy of security, peace, stability and prosperity. the report places a strong emphasis on promoting greater participation of women in political life, including with a view to fostering democratic transitions. the report also takes stock of the situation of women's rights in different areas and proposes ways of closer cooperation, for example in the fight against trafficking in human beings, including by involving european agencies such as europol. finally, the report also calls for the establishment of specific objectives within the eastern partnership, in addition to the cross-cutting approach to gender equality, taking into account the principle of differentiation and within a quantified approach based on harmonised data collection and the use of the gender equality index developed by the eige.

madam president, nowadays the european union faces unprecedented internal and external challenges including conflict zones, state collapse, terrorism, hybrid states, cyber- and energy insecurity. unfortunately all these challenges have direct and serious consequences for the security and wellbeing of eu citizens. for that reason, eu citizens see an effective common foreign and security policy as a priority area on action for the eu where extensive cooperation can bring most valuable contributions. in that regard i call on both eu institutions and member states to work together in a common and truly coordinated effort in order to develop a strong, coherent common foreign and security policy. it is important to note that a strong and coherent cfsp is achievable only if democratic reforms are being implemented and member states start to speak with one voice and act together.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on budgets. – madam president, commissioner hogan, dear colleagues, the volatile prices in the agricultural market can have a strong negative impact on the food security of consumers, incomes of farmers and the well-being of entire countries. this volatility can be caused by a combination of the economic and natural factors and can be intensified by the broad political and legislative environment and speculation on agricultural products. in order to overcome the negative consequences of the price volatility in this important sector of the economy, some measures could be introduced as follows: firstly, rural development programmes should be used more broadly to contribute towards insurance, mutual funds and income stabilisation schemes for farmers. secondly, improving synergies between the cap and other eu policies, in particular regarding energy, water supply, land use, biodiversity and ecosystems, as well as development of remote and mountainous areas. thirdly, the creation of a system to protect the farmers’ incomes through the use of risk management tools. and last but not least, better monitoring the significant price volatility of agricultural products by improving the european food price monitoring tools and using the information to make an adequate and timely response.
madam president, commissioner, the last council of 2016 is necessarily the council of the year and, possibly, the council of the mid-term, in my opinion, positive. but it is even more so the projections for next year. remarkable work has been done on migration. the foundations for a new holistic approach and partnerships have been laid. so it seems to me that the priority for 2017 must also be the external investment plan for the neighbourhood and africa, to really tackle the roots of irregular and uncontrolled migration flows. two remarks in this context: it is crucial that the economic environment is improved for the plan to work. our partners must carry out the necessary reforms, as tunisia is doing now. secondly, on the new partnership framework - it should be remembered - we can only succeed with those countries that show a willingness to work with us, including with readmission agreements, and if member states actually use the added value of the union. on security, there has been significant progress: the border and coast guard agency and an agreement on the anti-terrorism directive. but in the face of today's threats, the internal and external dimensions are merging. we need a europe of defence. the commission has made proposals, the ball is in the court of the member states to turn wishes repeatedly expressed into deeds. finally, a word about ukraine. you're going to talk about the association agreement, but let's talk about visas. it is high time that the union issued visas to ukrainians today. the criteria are met.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the polish proposal, submitted to the commission in december 2015 and taking effect on 1 january 2016. the proposal clearly aims at ensuring that the scope of the recast regulation is adjusted to the current legal framework of the member states (poland) on insolvency by the time of its application. because the proposed amendments by the council, rapporteur and commission are purely technical and the majority are also identical, they constitute only an official codification of a legislative text. in the interest of efficient action within the framework of the polish restructuring and bankruptcy proceedings, the proposed measures seem justified, necessary and urgently needed. therefore, i fully support the proposal.
in writing. ‒ nowadays companies and individuals in the eu are increasingly establishing business activities in eu countries other than where their core activities are located. if they become insolvent, there may be direct implications on the proper functioning of the internal market. to avoid that the eu commission has a proposal that sets common principles and more targeted rules for insolvency proceedings and insolvency practitioners. the proposal focuses on the key priorities of making sure that effective frameworks for preventive restructuring, insolvency second chance frameworks, as well as discharge procedure are available. in addition, it introduces measures to increase the efficiency – and in particular reduce the length – of all insolvency procedures. therefore, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i supported the eu-uzbekistan textiles protocol because such a consent will constitute a positive sign of encouragement to the uzbek government to further pursue its efforts to fully eradicate child labour and all other forms of forced labour, as well as to further strengthen cooperation with the eu. nevertheless, i call on the uzbek authorities to undertake democratic reforms, to create more space for independent civil society, to eradicate child labour and all other forms of forced labour, to meet uzbekistan’s commitments under the international covenant on civil and political rights and the convention against torture. on the other hand, i call on the eu to make full use of the extension of the protocol to urge the uzbek government to respect human rights and rule of law. last but not least, i call on both the eu and uzbek authorities to work together on diversification of uzbek economy, which could gradually alleviate the disastrous environmental situation with regard, in particular, to what is left of the aral sea and its tributaries.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this decision because it acknowledges the efforts by the uzbek government in pursuing the eradication of forced and child labour and recommends giving consent as a positive sign of encouragement for further actions and strengthening of the cooperation with the eu. however, if the uzbek authorities fail to follow through on their commitment to abolish forced labour, parliament reserves the right to ask the commission and the council to activate articles 2 and 95 of the pca. the resolution also takes account of the recent political developments and notes that the sudden death of president islam karimov should not have any impact on the continuity of the ongoing process of improving labour conditions in the cotton fields in uzbekistan.

in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the eu-norway agreement on the reciprocal granting of access to fishing in skagerrak, which was de facto concluded between denmark, sweden and norway as early as 1967. with the accession of denmark and sweden to the eu, the european commission becomes responsible for the management of fisheries in these countries, and therefore of this agreement, on behalf of the two member states. this is the main reason why iceland doesn't want to join the eu. this agreement updates the previous one to reflect new trends in international fisheries law, such as the promotion of fisheries conservation and management measures in the area.
in writing. ‒ this report is about an operational and strategic agreement between europol and georgia. it will provide the means for a better exchange of information, including personal data. there are operational needs for europol to deepen operational cooperation with georgia, which is a key partner of the european union within the eastern partnership. this agreement will help to combat crime, which is one of the main tasks in order to fully achieve the objectives of this partnership. i believe that georgia can be a good ally in the fight for greater security and that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the adoption of this report as georgia has the potential to be a key partner of the eu in the fight against organised crime, including trafficking in human beings, terrorism and corruption. in this context, the conclusion of the operational and strategic cooperation agreement between georgia and europol is a decisive step that can make a significant contribution to a more effective fight against international organised crime. enhanced security cooperation between the european union, its member states and georgia is also of strategic importance in relation to the mobility of european and georgian citizens and the finalisation of the visa liberalisation process for georgian citizens. that is why i support the conclusion of the strategic and operational cooperation agreement with georgia.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report approving the conclusion by the european police office (europol) of the agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between georgia and europol. the proposal concerns the approval of the operational and strategic agreement between europol and georgia providing for the exchange of information. this information may be in the field of specialised knowledge, general situational reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods and support for specific criminal investigations. i believe that there are clear operational needs for deeper operational cooperation between the two sides. according to europol, georgia is becoming increasingly important in the fight against terrorism and organised crime, in particular as a transit country for so-called foreign fighters and a key partner in the fight against georgian organised crime groups. in this respect, the conclusion of this strategic and operational cooperation agreement with georgia would therefore support and strengthen the fight against terrorism and organised crime, which are by definition international.
in writing. ‒ i supported the operational cooperation agreement between georgia and europol. there are clear operational needs for europol to deepen its cooperation with georgia. according to europol, georgian organised crime (oc) has been active in the eu, steadily growing in scale over that time. currently, several eu member states are facing serious issues with criminality caused by georgian oc, which by its nature is very international and has interlinked clusters in many countries. in addition to this, georgia continues to be a transit country for foreign terrorist fighters. looking from this perspective, the conclusion of the operational cooperation agreement between georgia and europol would definitely facilitate and reinforce the international fight against terrorism and oc.
in writing. ‒ i supported the conclusion of the operational and strategic cooperation agreement between georgia and europol, as i believe that it will be beneficial for both parties. at a time of constant terrorist attacks, the european union is increasingly vulnerable and a sense of fear and insecurity is being instilled in european citizens. i call on the institutions, and in particular the commission, to exercise strict control over the provisions concerning the exchange of personal data and to inform parliament of the results of this analysis. ensuring transparency in the conclusion of such agreements is key to addressing the concerns of european citizens regarding the safeguards for the protection of personal data. the entry into force of the new regulation (eu) 2016/794 of 1 january 2017 amending the procedure for the conclusion of international agreements also aims to enhance safeguards on protection in the collection and exchange of data. i hope that the conclusion of this strategic and operational cooperation agreement will help to make the fight against organised crime more effective, reducing the number of threats and acts of violation of citizens' rights.
in writing. – i supported this operational and strategic agreement between europol and georgia because it provides for the exchange of information, including personal data. such information could be in the field of specialist knowledge, general situation reports, results of strategic analysis, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime-prevention methods, and support in individual criminal investigations. i believe it is important to maintain a good relationship with eu neighbouring countries and that this agreement will deliver on this objective.
in writing. ‒ globalisation is causing dynamic changes in industry that are causing many sites to close. i am aware that the european union's globalisation adjustment fund aims to reduce the damage caused by these trends, but i believe that this is not the right approach and the money invested would not produce the desired result. that's why i'm voting against the motion. we need to aim at growth and job creation and i support measures that would support those policies, but this is definitely not one of them and spending €1.4 million on 250 redundant workers would not achieve the growth we are aiming for.
in writing. ‒ as you know, the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to provide support for workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or as a result of a continuation of the global financial and economic crisis. in this regard, the main aim of the fund is to help people who lost their jobs to reintegrate into the labour market. the eu should mobilise the fund to support spain’s submitted application egf/2016/004es/ comunidad valenciana automative, following redundancies in the economic sector classified under the nace revision 2 division 29 (manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers). in this particular case, 250 redundant workers eligible for the egf contribution are expected to participate in 12 different measures: 6 are personalised services actions in accordance with article 7 (1)(a) and (c) of the egf regulation and types of measures are allowance and incentives as referred to in article 7 (1)(b) of the egf regulation. personalised services actions represent more than 75% of the overall amount. looking from this perspective, i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the egf.
in writing. ‒ as a result of the decline in domestic demand in the eu, and the weak positioning of the european automotive industry in relation to the growing asian market, a number of companies operating in this sector have been forced to close down their operations and lay off their employees. this is the case of the 250 workers made redundant from the production of car parts and accessories for the spanish company bosal s.a. the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) will allow the eu to help spanish workers to receive training to adapt to the labour market needs in their region. i consider that the circumstances which led to the dismissal of the spanish workers and the measures taken by spain to reintegrate them into the employment sector are eligible for financial assistance under the egf. that is why i supported the granting of eur 856 800 to bosal s.a. employees.
in writing. ‒ in view of the liberalisation of the transport market and the fourth railway package already adopted, either the list of railway undertakings had to be supplemented or this regulation had to be abolished altogether. it would take a long time to fill this list every year and check for new railway companies and those that are dropping off the list. i agree with my colleagues who propose that this regulation should be dropped because member states can continue to use other regulations to compensate railway undertakings.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eec) no 1192/69 allows member states to compensate railway undertakings financially for the payment of obligations not normally borne by other types of transport undertakings. such obligations include, for example, the payment of pensions to workers who retire early in the event of heavy physical work and the payment of overhead travel expenses. however, with the change of european legislation, financial compensation to railway undertakings is now practiced rather rarely and mainly by four member states, not including bulgaria. the commission notes that the commission has not yet adopted a new legislative proposal for the rail sector, which is based on the principle of proportionality. in this context, i consider that the council's proposal to repeal the regulation is justified, especially given the fact that countries wishing to compensate their railway undertakings for the additional obligations will be able to do so provisionally through directive 2012/34/eu.
in writing. – i supported this report, as it will allow member states to adapt their national legislation concerning the compensations of costs relating to certain level crossing facilities. in the framework of the fourth railway package the commission proposes to repeal regulation 1192/69 of the council on common rules for the normalisation of the accounts of railway undertakings. we must support the railway sector as it is the environmental friendly means of transportation of passengers and cargo as well as being of strategic importance for the eu’s security.
in writing. ‒ i am concerned that the opening of the rail passenger market will lead to the bankruptcy of 'public' carriers in the smaller eu member states. as we all know, rail transport is a social activity, i.e. it uses the poorer part of our population to get from point a to point b. unfortunately, the solidarity that the union proclaims is not in people's incomes and thus the railway will lose its social character and/or the state will have to take over the greater difference in the cost of transportation of the socially weak and people beyond working age.
in writing. ‒ i supported the interinstitutional agreement reached on the regulation on the opening of the market for domestic passenger transport services by rail. the aim of the regulation is to improve the quality of rail services and to increase their operational efficiency. this will improve the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail transport compared to other modes of transport and will contribute to the further development of the single european railway area.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that easier access for all rail operators to domestic rail markets will give rail passengers more choice and better quality services. in fact, the liberalisation of domestic passenger transport services by rail will boost business, investment, innovation in the sector and most importantly will provide new passenger services in eu countries’ domestic markets. therefore, i strongly support easier access to the market for rail operators. nevertheless, i totally disagree with the notion that member states could limit a new operator’s right of access if a new service would compromise the ‘economic equilibrium’ of an existing public services contract. i believe that member states should not intervene or limit competition in a free market because thus they will put railway transport in an unsatisfactory position vis-à-vis other modes of transport.
in writing. ‒ the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 contains many positive elements that would improve the quality and efficiency of rail services in central and eastern european countries. however, i did not support its amendment because, in addition to the positive components, it includes a clause which is against the interests of railway workers. the modernisation of rail transport has enormous added value for both citizens and businesses in countries in the bulgaria region, because it will make travel faster, cheaper and more sustainable. however, this modernisation cannot be built on the backs of the employees of enterprises, who must be guaranteed normal working conditions and safety. support for this regulation would be de facto support for a clause allowing for the mass dismissal of workers from railway undertakings in the event of a change of ownership. that is why i did not support the amendment of this regulation.
in writing. – the general objective of the commission proposal for an amendment of regulation (ec) 1370/2007 is to improve the quality of rail passenger services and to enhance their operational efficiency. this should improve the competitiveness and attractiveness of rail vis-à-vis other modes of transport and develop further the single european railway area. i voted in favour of this report because the tabled recommendations will deliver a more resilient and flexible market for domestic passenger transport services by rail.

in writing. ‒ by establishing a single european railway area, the eu will manage to bring together in a single text the main principles governing railway transport, granting licences to railway undertakings and the levying of charges for the use of infrastructure. this move will raise the level of competition and guarantee financial transparency and fair financing conditions. equal market access and the increasing number of operators should ultimately generate new business activity and additional traffic. increasing competition and specialisation of the market players should also have a positive effect on productivity and efficiency and lead to increases in investment into rail transport infrastructure, making the sector more responsive to customers’ needs and allowing rail operators to compete with other modes of transport. looking from this perspective, i supported the directive.
in writing. ‒ the over the last two decades, rail transport in europe has been experiencing a decline in growth. apart from the increase in car ownership among european citizens and the development of air transport, excessive regulation at national level can be identified as a major reason for the contraction of this sector. it is a significant factor which prevents competition from arising in this sector. this in turn has a negative impact on the quality of rail services, which is mainly suffered by european passengers. unfortunately, bulgaria is a prime example of this trend. in this context, i supported the amendment of directive 2012/34/eu, which contains measures aimed at ensuring equal access to infrastructure and eliminating conflicts of interest in decisions on its use.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report, as it put in place important safeguards aimed at ensuring the impartiality and independence of the infrastructure manager, by reinforcing the provisions on: double mandates, essential functions, traffic management and maintenance planning, outsourcing and sharing of the functions of the infrastructure manager and financial transparency. furthermore, special rules governing the access of high-speed passenger services to the union rail infrastructure have been established, with a view to developing the market for high—speed passenger services and promoting its competitiveness for the benefit of passengers. the market development of common information and through-ticketing systems was put forward as a priority in order to facilitate more efficient multimodal and cross-border passenger transport.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for market access to port services and financial transparency in ports, as i consider that the proposed amendments are fully in line with my views. the proposed amendments emphasise the need for the independence of the managing body of the port in order to be able to pursue its economic strategy, while respecting certain key principles. in addition, the report underlines that the aim is to avoid the administrative burden associated with the application of this regulation. in summary, this regulation should lead to legal certainty for ports and have a positive impact on the successful functioning of the ten-t network.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european commission's proposal for a framework for market access to port services and financial transparency of ports, as it aims to contribute to the objective of more efficient, interconnected and sustainable operation of trans-european transport networks by creating a framework that improves the performance of ports and helps them to cope with changing transport and logistics requirements. the main priorities are related to the modernisation of port services and operations and the creation of framework conditions to attract investment in ports. there is a desire to counter weak competitive pressures and possible market abuse in order to increase the efficiency of port services. the existence of a clear framework on state aid rules is also an important condition for fair competition between ports on a level playing field. the regulation will apply to the maritime ports identified in the ten-t guidelines and will avoid the unnecessary burden for well-functioning ports while creating the necessary conditions for other ports to address the structural challenges they face.
in writing. ‒ europe is one of the densest port regions worldwide. at the same time, the port sector is very heterogeneous and characterised by a wide diversity in types and organisation. the eu is highly dependent on its ports for its trade with the rest of the world and for proper functioning of its own internal market. in this context, the commission’s proposal on the trans-european transport network (ten-t) seeks to contribute to the goal of more efficient, interconnected and sustainable functioning of eu ports by creating a framework which improves the performance of ports and helps them to cope with changes in transport and logistics requirements. in general, the commission’s proposal aims to counteract weak competitive pressure and possible market abuses, in order to increase the efficiency of port services and to promote financial transparency. looking from this perspective, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. – the regulation aims to increase transparency in the financial relationship between the state, ports and port service operators. this will contribute to better use of public funds and to the effective and fair application of eu competition rules in ports. as a member—substitute of the econ committee, i supported this agreement because i believe that financial transparency is crucial for building and maintaining trust.
in writing. ‒ i supported mr buzek's report on the research programme of the research fund for coal and steel, which proposes to change the regulatory framework of this fund, which was set up in 1951 with the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community. but in 2002, the treaty expired and the member states decided to transfer the assets of the european coal and steel community to the research fund for coal and steel. the fund is currently managed by the european commission and has some €50 million available for development and research in sectors such as steel and coal mining, environmental improvement and safety at work.
in writing. ‒ i support the proposal for the adoption of the research programme of the research fund for coal and steel and on the multiannual technical guidelines for this programme. the coal and steel sectors are important in the european integration process and play a key role for the entire union industry. at the same time, working conditions in these sectors are harsh and often lead to harm to the health of workers and citizens. companies should therefore respect all legal requirements on social responsibility, propose solutions and minimise the social impact of the switch-over or closure of installations.
in writing. ‒ the research fund for coal and steel (rfcs) gives funding of over €50 million every year to innovative projects to enhance the safety, efficiency and competitive edge of the eu coal and steel industries. it is important to note that rfcs is complementary to and managed outside the horizon 2020 programme. rfcs brings together industrial partners, smes, leading research centres and universities from across the eu to develop knowledge and foster innovation in the sector with regard to production processes, utilisation and conservation of resources, environmental improvements and safety. however, i do not support the commission’s proposal for a proportionate alignment of rfcs rules with those of horizon 2020 because the beneficiaries are the same in both programmes (rfcs and h2020). therefore there is no real need to amend the legal basis.
in writing. – the purpose of this proposal is to amend the legal basis of the research programme dedicated to the coal and steel sectors after the periodic assessment of its management rules with a view to implementing certain objectives. i voted in favour because it will inter alia align the programme with the commission’s rules on expert groups. i believe it will ensure transparent management of what is a programme funded from the eu general budget.
in writing. ‒ i supported mr buzek's report that the research fund for coal and steel should continue to exist, in addition to the horizon 2020 programme, and be managed independently by the european commission. the steel and coal fund has been in existence since the signing of the treaty establishing the european coal and steel community in 1951, which marked the beginning of the unification of the european continent. the fund currently provides eur 50 million a year in funding for r & d and innovation in both the coal and steel sectors (with a breakdown of 72.8% for steel and 27.2% for coal). the research fund brings together industrial enterprises, smes, leading research centres and universities across the european union, both to develop knowledge and stimulate innovation in the sector and to research production processes, the use and protection of resources and the environment and safety in the workplace in these sectors. i do not think that the time has come yet for us to stop research into steel and coal in an attempt to shut down coal as an energy resource altogether. at least another decade of intensive research is needed to determine whether technologies can be found that can offer the use of coal in a clean way.
in writing. ‒ i voted 'abstention' on the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world and the european union's policy on the matter (2015), as it contains many opinions with which i do not agree, such as the sharp criticism of the eu and the member states for not complying with european migration legislation. we cannot ask member states to apply and comply with legislation imposed by the european institutions that does not work in their favour but instead aims to weaken member states and destroy european traditions and culture.
in writing. – the european union is committed to a common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and all other policies with an external dimension founded on the advancement of democracy, rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms. i voted in favour of it as it pays particular attention to women, children, people with disabilities, elderly people and eu human rights policy in this regard. the report further underlines the fact that conflicts, wars and failures of governance constitute key causes of migration and displacement. in its holistic approach to finding sustainable, long-term and coherent solutions, based on international human rights standards, it highlights the importance of differentiating between refugees and migrants.
in writing. ‒ for another year, mr elmar brock's report on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy (article 36 teu) calls for the abandonment of the 'narrow national point of view' and the pursuit of a common eu foreign policy and the creation of a common european army. the lisbon treaty has already made a major step forward in this respect, and i believe that any further step will be a step towards centralisation in brussels, federalisation of the eu and the abandonment of national sovereignty. the general approach certainly gives the european union greater weight in foreign policy and in achieving its objectives, but the eu's objectives do not always coincide with the interests of individual member states. that is why the european external security and defence policy should not replace or restrict the ability of member states to pursue their own foreign policy in order to achieve their foreign policy objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of a resolution on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy, as i believe that the european union is facing unprecedented internal and external challenges, including interstate conflicts, state breakdown, terrorism, hybrid threats, cyber and energy insecurity, organised crime and climate change. the community will only be able to respond effectively to these challenges if its structures and its member states work together in a common and effectively coordinated effort. the european union is one of the greatest achievements in european history, aiming to achieve peace, stability and prosperity. it remains the world's most significant economic power, the world's largest donor of humanitarian and development aid, and a leader in global diplomacy on issues such as climate change, international justice, non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and human rights. i believe that the eu should strengthen its security and defence capabilities. enhanced and shared civilian and military capacity is a key element for the union to provide a comprehensive response to crises, build the resilience of its partners and protect europe from challenges.
in writing. – i supported this report, which acknowledges the multifaceted challenges the eu is facing in the external domain, from terrorism, cyber security and misinformation to the fight against human trafficking or radicalisation. effectively countering the ever-blurred nexus of external and internal security challenges will be possible with strong commitment, ownership, political will and leadership from the member states. furthermore, the report underlines that eu external action needs to be based on three pillars (the ‘three ds’): diplomacy, development and defence.
madam president, european producers are facing a number of difficulties. while the authorities in the us, brazil and other countries competing in agricultural production adopt and maintain measures to protect their producers through financial means to develop risk-related policy models, europe still fails to cope. the crisis in a number of agricultural sectors across the continent is proof of this. geopolitical decisions, climate change and rising equipment prices are just some of the factors affecting the volatility of the sector in europe. under regulation no 1305/2013, member states were invited to provide for a 'risk management' measure under the second pillar of the cap. the bulgarian government, led by boyko borisov, which almost daily appeals with successes for the implementation and assimilation of the common agricultural policy in bulgaria, has not yet proposed a mechanism for this measure. we must not wait for other forms of embargo or crisis to be proposed as a mechanism to protect the bulgarian farmer. it's time for a qualitative change in this strategically important sector for bulgaria and gerb have proven that they can't do it.
in writing. ‒ this report calls on the commission to come forward with new proposals to reduce the negative effects of price volatility by facilitating the introduction of contractual relations by adapting competition law, by further developing risk management tools, in particular the different types of insurance and mutual funds, and by applying the european observatory on agricultural prices to the different agricultural sectors. as the proposal to continue to pay financial assistance under the operational programme for agriculture after the end of the 2014-2020 period has lapsed, i voted 'abstention'.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it contains concrete ideas for reforming the risk management tools under the second pillar of the current cap in order to limit the impact of price volatility on farmers' incomes. the report proposes, first of all, to strengthen the organisation of the sector and the bargaining process. the call on the commission to develop additional public and private instruments and a mandatory early warning mechanism to respond more effectively to market crises is also important. i also support the proposal to set up european observatories to provide a permanent analysis of prices on agricultural markets to improve transparency and limit abusive practices such as price speculation. i regard the emphasis on the key role of young farmers in the future of european agriculture as a very positive element of the report. the eu's food security and the development of a competitive and sustainable agricultural sector that meets the needs of european citizens should be a strategic objective that cannot be achieved without ensuring stable incomes for farmers.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on cap instruments to reduce price volatility in agricultural markets, as this is one of the main reasons for the disadvantage faced by many farmers in the eu. i think the eu should help to solve this problem. the recommendations provided in the report provide an appropriate set of measures to make this happen. i support the proposal to facilitate the introduction of contractual relations by adapting competition law and developing risk management tools as well as monitoring tools for greater market transparency.
in writing. – agriculture is confronted with higher levels of price volatility than other economic sectors due to a variety of economic, natural and political factors. i voted in favour of this report as it recommends facilitating the introduction of contractual relations by adapting competition law, further developing crisis and risk management tools and monitoring instruments for greater market transparency. a major objective for the future cap must be the tackling of price volatility in order to ensure a fair income for farmers, stabilise agricultural markets and guarantee viable food production.
in writing. ‒ colleagues, the deteriorating climate, droughts, floods, pests and whatnot are having an adverse impact on the level of harvest and the stability of production prices. farmers face increasing production costs and mounting debts, while sustainable agriculture as a source of livelihood can only be guaranteed if purchase prices cover all production costs. the cap is designed to guarantee a decent standard of living for farmers and to provide food security at affordable prices for consumers. therefore, the maintenance of direct payments in the cap, alongside the single area payment scheme, constitutes public service compensation and is vital to guarantee farmers' incomes. risk management tools, insurance, individual protection mechanisms and mutual funds need to be further developed in the cap in order to limit the effects of price volatility. the commission should encourage the exchange of best practices between member states and develop new tools that are acceptable and accessible to farmers, including better information and promotion of farmers' organisations. the commission should also be able to provide information on the impact of the measures on the environment and the environment protection.
the migration crisis facing europe requires solidarity with the countries most affected by the migration flows, such as bulgaria and greece, and new measures to deal with it. the eu-turkey agreement is one such new measure. it has succeeded in reducing the flow of refugees to europe, but to be truly successful, all countries on it must abide by it and cooperate. at the same time, european asylum legislation requires radical change because it does not work in its current form. the gradual resumption of the return of applicants for international protection to greece can be seen as a visible sign of a functioning european asylum system, but in no case should countries like bulgaria and greece become major refugee hubs on the periphery of the european union. this will only be possible by removing the principle that the primary responsibility for migrants lies with the countries of first entry. it is time to put the principle of genuine european solidarity into european law!
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, first of all, thank you and congratulations to the rapporteur for his outstanding work. the european parliament is a co-legislator for this visa policy and we must continue to enforce our prerogatives. i would like to make three comments. first, the review of the suspension mechanism is part of the holistic approach to smart and controlled management of migration and mobility. more security through greater flexibility to trigger the mechanism; it's a first. however, we must remember the fundamental principles which will guide our decisions if the mechanism is to be triggered: a case-by-case examination, based on specific criteria, with the interests of citizens as a guiding principle. secondly, and i must congratulate the rapporteur again, because by introducing the possibility of suspending the exemption for certain categories of persons, we are preserving the potential of visa policy as a tool for foreign policy and political dialogue. finally, i also insist on visa liberalisation with georgia and ukraine. the council had decided to link the review of the mechanism to these two other cases. we have reached an agreement on the mechanism and i will not accept any further unnecessary delays. i am counting on the maltese presidency to start the trilogues on ukraine in january.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, the lack of visa reciprocity with the united states of america affects millions of european citizens in bulgaria, romania, croatia, cyprus and poland. as a citizen of the country directly concerned and as a shadow rapporteur for alde on this subject, i am strongly and unreservedly committed to achieving real visa reciprocity for europeans. the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs has repeatedly stated that the european commission is obliged to take action to address the lack of visa reciprocity by temporarily suspending the visa-free regime for us citizens by means of a delegated act. i understand the diplomatic sensitivity and the need to find the right moment and means to maximise the results in relations with the us, but i believe it is high time that the commission took a firm stand and showed that the different treatment of european citizens is unacceptable. that is the view shared by the majority of my colleagues in the libe committee of the european parliament. i take this opportunity to point out again in this debate that the inaction of the european commission creates a sense of double standards, of a two-speed europe and of different classes of europeans. it certainly undermines the trust of european citizens in the institutions of the countries concerned, but it also determines the way in which europe looks united to the outside world. i therefore call on the commission to fulfil its role as guardian of the treaties in the interests of all european citizens, by clearly demonstrating the administrative will to fulfil its obligations and the political strength to win back the european union's rightful place on the world stage.
mr president, commissioner, i listened very carefully to your statement. i see three important things in it. first, visa reciprocity is a basic principle of the common visa policy of the european union. i am pleased that this issue is as much a priority for my country bulgaria as it is for the european commission. the concrete results of the agreed visa phase-out for bulgarians and romanians are proof that only coordinated action between the commission and the member states - but here it is time to take the european parliament into account - can make progress. that is why i am also drawing attention to the second aspect, so that we can continue to speak with one voice on the international stage. we must take very seriously the fact that the current situation creates a different feeling for a different category of countries and citizens of the european union. this negative trend can have very long-term consequences. finally, i would like to thank you, commissioner, for your efforts so far. pre-emptive action is the clear identification of the negative consequences of certain actions. but that is precisely why i call for a decisive defence with all the instruments of diplomacy, so that, by defending the authority of the european union, we can meet the expectations of all european citizens.
