mr president, commissioner, the european union is a strong force when it speaks with one voice. the visa reciprocity mechanism therefore requires a collective and solidarity-based response when discriminatory visa restrictions are applied to european citizens. why, commissioner, do we have this legislation if we don't follow it? i believe it is unacceptable that the european commission continues to delay the application of the delegated act to propose a temporary suspension of the visa-free regime for us citizens. i also believe that this not only hinders direct business contacts and partnerships, cultural and tourist exchanges between us, but also undermines our strategic links and partnerships. for bulgaria, achieving full visa reciprocity is an absolute priority, and i welcome the efforts of the bulgarian government that have been put in place, both with respect to canada and with respect to the united states, at every meeting with representatives of congress, with representatives of the administration. we demand that they do so as soon as possible. unfortunately, we see a reluctance on the part of both the u.s. congress and the current administration to take steps in this direction. therefore, i call on the commission to adopt this delegated act.
in writing. on 1 january 2017, bulgaria will mark the 10th anniversary of its eu membership - a decade in which we have continuously tried to prove ourselves as an equal partner in europe and the world. unfortunately, this struggle continues and the fact that we from bulgaria, along with five other member states, are the only ones who need visas to travel to the us is an example of double standards and unequal treatment of bulgarian citizens. as a bulgarian representative, i find such an attitude unacceptable, especially from the european commission. it is responsible for applying eu law to protect all european citizens and member states. the interests of our international partners must not be allowed to be put ahead of the rights of europeans. i therefore urge the european commission to comply with its legal obligation and to come forward as soon as possible with a delegated act in accordance with regulation (eu) no 1289/2013 so that it can be discussed by the european parliament and the council. the commission also needs to actively negotiate with the new us presidential administration to continue the us visa waiver for citizens of the five member states. we already have such a positive example with canada and i hope that we will soon see a solution to the problem with the united states.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, a few months ago we managed to make progress with the member states on the adoption of the regulation on the abolition of the apostille on the presentation of certain official documents in the european union. but this is a different matter altogether. indeed, different countries do not have the same vision of family law, especially with regard to marriage, adoption, registered partnerships. family law is about relationships, not just facts. their creation and existence is based on legal necessity, specific legal rules and arrangements. this means that a family relationship which exists under the law of one member state may not exist under the law of another. recognition of the content of the civil status documents would lead to a change in the substantive family law of the member states. under the treaties, the eu does not have the power to change the substantive law relating to civil status, particularly as regards registered partnerships or marriages. this falls within the competence of the member states. if the european commission were to include registered partnerships in such a legislative text, it would be contrary to the treaties and would amount to a kind of imposition of legislation that is not desired by many member states. we cannot oblige member states to recognise legal instruments from other member states, such as registered partnerships, which are not known in their own national law.
